# Decisions

Running log of what we decided and **why**, dated. Short and punchy — this rots if it gets heavy. The *current* architectural truth lives in `VISION.md` and `CLAUDE.md`; this file is the history and the reasoning, not a re-explanation.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 5 T3: manifest-walking is a trait primitive — `origin_packs`, the plural sibling

The per-origin unification's enumeration mechanism is a new `PackSource` trait method `origin_packs(kind, id)` — **every** constituent shipping the id, precedence order, empty when none (no `self` fallback, unlike the singular) — because `assert_schema_freeze` holds only `&dyn PackSource` and "walk every manifest-shipping constituent" is unanswerable through the one-winner `origin_pack`. Per-doctype resolution funnels through one `governing_version(pack, ty)` helper (`origin_pack(Schemas, ty)`'s own manifest entry); `frozen_doctype_versions` becomes the governed union keyed off `list(Schemas)` ids (the stem==type convention both shipped packs honor); `frozen_doctype_set` is subsumed and deleted. No-op while methodology is manifest-less — full gate green unchanged.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 5 T2: the census bit — CRLF front-matter parsed only its FIRST field (production parse defect, fixed)

The methodology byte-stability census (9 `arb_doc()` arms, the M33 pattern) surfaced a real one on its first run: `scan_blocks` kept only the **first** `Text` event's range inside the metadata block, and pulldown-cmark emits one `Text` **per line** under CRLF (one for the whole block under LF) — so a CRLF doc's multi-field front-matter silently dropped every field after the first (parse still "ok"; `set_field` on `date`/`verdict` errored `NotPresent`). Dev-pack-wide too, not methodology-specific — the M33 census masked it by only ever editing the *first* header field and asserting parse-*ok*, not parse-*shape*. Fixed by accumulating the Text ranges across the block (`parse.rs::scan_blocks`), pinned by a deterministic CRLF-ADR regression (`parse.rs::crlf_front_matter_parses_every_field`), and the census's clause 1 now asserts LF-vs-CRLF **parsed-structure equality** (same field keys, same item anchors) on every arm, so this defect class can't re-hide behind parse-ok. Census discharges doctype-map.md's recorded freeze precondition ahead of T4's hash-freeze.

The nine persisted methodology doctypes are 4 placement + 5 location homes; with the transient `commit` shadow the manifest lists **ten**.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 4 T2: the `doc schema` contract's `required` means presence-in-a-conformant-instance

Three executor elaborations of the pinned contract (`design/doc-read-surface.md` → Why json is a contract here), golden-locked in `crates/cli/tests/doc_schema.rs`: **(1)** a field's `required` = the author must supply it **or** the CLI stamps it (`is_author_required(f) || default || set`) — so an optional `ref` (adr `supersedes`) and a pack-typed anchor read `required: false`, never the misleading raw `!optional:`, while `author-required` stays T1's shared engine predicate verbatim; **(2)** an item slot projects as `{id, optional?}` and a nested repeatable as `{id, item}` (the recursion point) — kind is implied inside an item; **(3)** the unknown-doctype block reuses the read surface's `store.unknown-type` code, routed to `jigc describe` (one failure class, one code — no new id for the same "address names no doctype" fault).

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 4 T1: the skeleton stamp lives at the engine empty/seeded-instance seam; absence now blocks as present-but-empty

The author-required pre-stamp lands inside `engine::state`'s `empty_instance`/`seeded_instance` (header sections only, merged with the on-create seeds in schema-declared field order), so **every** `provision_doc` consumer inherits it — `doc create`, `doc author`, and the engine test substrate's commit fixtures (whose `provisioned_empty_commit` golden gains `type: `; the *production* commit mint stays on `start.rs::fillable_form`, byte-identical, its all-minus-optional-ref rule now reading the engine's pub `is_optional_ref`). The canonical empty line is `key: ` — the field-block emitter's one form, the same bytes the commit form always stamped. Consequence (the Settle-corrected caveat, now pinned by tests): an un-set author-required field on the 3 affected doctypes blocks at **`field-value-conformant`** (present-but-empty) instead of `required-field-present` — the gate holds, only the finding code/message shifts (flow20/flow21/dogfood-record repairs); repeatable-item fields are NOT stamped, so their absence keeps `required-field-present`.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 4 — F1: the schema-visibility pair](implementation/roadmap.md) into **2 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded in the code at HEAD `513ad84` (tree clean). Verified bases: the predicate is `engine::validate::is_author_required` (private, `validate.rs:1790`; helper `ref_min_cardinality_zero`) and the hand-maintained mirror is `start.rs::is_optional_ref` (`start.rs:447`, used only by the commit `fillable_form`); the doc-create mint (`doc.rs::run_create` **and** `run_author` — one shared seam, `state::create_gated` → `seeded_instance`/`empty_instance`) stamps **no** author-required fields today, only the CLI-computed `default:`/`set: on-create` seeds — so `doc create idea` genuinely lacks `trigger:`; the exactly-3 blast radius holds against every shipped schema (idea `trigger` · completion-record `verdict`+`owner-artifact` · dogfood-record's **14** meta fields, none default/set/optional/ref/pack — all other doctypes' header fields are default/set/optional-ref/pack-typed or absent, incl. prd/changelog/roadmap/decisions-log/deferral-ledger which have **no** header section and milestone-record which is all-`set:`); the adr regression tripwire is the `doc_code_gate.rs:557` front-matter prefix lock (exactly `status`/`date`/`schema-version`, "no stray supersedes/cites-code line"); the commit doctype's author-required `type` is out of blast radius because the commit doc mints through `fillable_form`, whose stamping *rule* (all header fields minus optional refs — `type:`+`scope:`) must stay byte-identical; the verb's task-free resolution idiom exists (`doc.rs::committed_schemas` → `CascadeDefs::all_schemas`) and the schema-version value surface is `stamp_schema_version`/`manifest_versions` (methodology is manifest-less until Inc 5 → null, exactly the pin's "stamped version, else null").

- **T1 — the generalized fillable skeleton via the shared engine predicate (the write half).** `is_author_required` (+ the optional-ref helper the CLI needs) goes `pub`; the shared doc-create mint seam pre-stamps every author-required header field as an empty `key:` line in schema-declared order, merged with the existing on-create/default seeds (both `doc create` and `doc author` inherit through `create_gated`); `start.rs::is_optional_ref` retired in favor of the engine predicate surface — **byte-neutral for the commit form** (its all-minus-optional-ref rule keeps `type:`+`scope:`; only the predicate's home moves); fold in the forced repairs — byte/golden asserts for exactly idea/completion-record/dogfood-record mints plus any engine `state.rs` empty-instance expectation tests. *Done:* a new named test proves `doc create idea` stages an empty `trigger:` line (red today); the `doc_code_gate.rs` adr front-matter prefix lock passes **unmodified** (the tripwire: no stray optional-ref/pack/default/set stamping — adr/spec/prd mint bytes unchanged); full gate. Files: `crates/engine/src/{validate.rs,state.rs}`, `crates/cli/src/start.rs`, affected tests (`design_altitude_schemas.rs`/`flow_park_idea.rs`/`methodology_completion_record.rs`/`flow20_completion_encode.rs`/`dogfood_record_schema.rs`/`dogfood_apparatus.rs` as the gate surfaces them).
- **T2 — `jigc doc schema <doctype>`: the separately-pinned, explicitly versioned contract (the read half).** The verb (task-free, the `committed_schemas` store-read idiom) + the deterministic renderer of the [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) pin: `contract-version: 1` / `type` / `schema-version`-or-null (via the manifest surface) / `fields` `{id,type,required,author-required,default?,set?}` (`author-required` computed by T1's pub predicate; the resolved schema is projected as loaded, injected stamp field included) / `sections` `{id,kind,optional?,item:{fields,slots,nested}}` with the **recursive** `item`; non-json renders a human listing (non-contractual — only the json shape is the pin); unknown doctype → routed non-zero error. *Done:* a golden test pins the exact `--format json` bytes at ship covering dogfood-record (schema-version null, **all 14** meta fields `author-required: true` — the roadmap Proves line), a schema-version-2 dev doctype with the recursive nested item (changelog), and adr (ref/pack/default/set field rendering); full gate. Files: `crates/cli/src/{doc.rs,cli.rs}` (+ `describe.rs` only if the schema-listing helper is lifted), new `crates/cli/tests/doc_schema.rs`. Note for Inc 5 (A1): the methodology manifest will flip dogfood-record's `schema-version` to non-null and inject its stamp field — that golden refresh belongs to Inc 5's blast radius, pinned here against the Inc-4 resolved shape.

All three grouped-scope bullets map: the shared-predicate refactor + mint change → T1 · the three affected doctypes' golden updates → **folded into T1** (they are the repairs the mint change forces in the same motion — the atomic gate-green rule, not a scope drop) · the verb + renderer + golden → T2. Order is load-bearing: T2's `author-required` projection consumes the predicate T1 makes `pub`. No design-doc task — write-commands.md (create note) and doc-read-surface.md (the pinned shape + third-surface sentence) already carry the M40 blocks from Settle; the fold-back is Inc 8. *Why 2:* the increment is one predicate with two consumers — the write half is a single atomic byte-changing unit (mint change + its forced golden repairs share one commit boundary), the read half is purely additive and gate-green alone with the golden as its red step.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 3 T5: the unregistered tier mints `file-state.unregistered-doc`

The two-tier orphan advisory's never-adopted arm gets its own check id, **`file-state.unregistered-doc`** (executor-chosen per the T5 delegation — the design pinned only "a looks-managed-but-unregistered advisory"), un-keyed/non-inventory like its `orphaned-doc` sibling; route text: migratable → *"adopt it with `jigc migrate <path> --as <doctype>`, or ignore it if it is not meant to be managed"*, else → *"ignore it if it is not meant to be managed, or route it to a human (no `migrate-<doctype>` workflow ships to adopt it)"*. One planner-note staleness corrected in passing: the migrate-route arm **does** pair live today — `migrate-adr`/`-spec`/`-prd`/`-arch-doc` shipped in M25 and those doctypes are location-bearing — so "no live pairing until Inc 7" holds only for the methodology doctypes.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 3 T4: triage annotations are the pinned strings themselves, byte-identical across formats

`TriageRow.annotations` carries the pinned shapes (*"adopted — structurally empty: 0 \<items\>"* / *"adopted — N surplus trailing sections"*) as plain strings — the JSON row serializes the exact bytes the human/agent render prints (one vocabulary, no format skew), rendered as indented lines under the row with the base adopted marker kept (executor-chosen per the T4 delegation). The `<items>` noun is the hollow section's id from the engine finding's address; the surplus N is the leading count of the engine's pinned message.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 3 — F8+F4+F3: ingest & store visibility](implementation/roadmap.md) into **5 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded in the code at HEAD `fe316e5` (tree clean). Verified bases: `discover_candidates`' single production call site is `crates/cli/src/ingest.rs:100` (the engine walk + its tests are otherwise self-contained — the "engine-test substrate" pin holds); `.jigc/AGENT.md` is deliberately un-gitignored (`setup.rs:42`), so it **does** appear in `ls-files` and the internals prune must stay on top; the git shell-out idiom is `crate::task::git_capture` (already used by `orphan.rs:129`). **One planning-verified correction is load-bearing for T2/T3:** `schema_conformance_store` walks only `location:`-bearing schemas (`validate.rs:549` — placement doctypes are skipped by the whole fifth family), and `roadmap`/`changelog` are **placement** doctypes — so wiring the two new checks only into family 5 would make this increment's own roadmap Proves line (a zero-item **roadmap** advising in the store sweep) unreachable; the pair needs its own placement-covering store arm. Also verified: the knobs.rs per-check filter (`.severity` + exactly 3 dots, knobs.rs:611) excludes the new `.exempt` string knob, so the severity-key count goes 29 → **31** and `CHECK_INVENTORY` 26 → **28** (the store-scope-tunable precedent is `mention-resolves`, result.rs:220); `scan_blocks` is `pub(crate)` (parse.rs:442) so the raw-block surplus scan is engine-internal-reachable against the positional-mapping blindness (parse.rs:246–283); the orphan loop and the `FileStateRecord` already share one fn (`cli.rs:772` / `cli.rs:729` — the threading is genuinely CLI-local); the `migrate-` workflow prefix scan is `migrate.rs:85-90`, and today only `migrate-changelog` ships while changelog is placement (no location basename), so the two-tier migrate-route-present arm has **no live doctype pairing until Inc 7** lands the seven methodology migrate workflows — unit-proven here, tracked to that landing.

- **T1 — the ingest candidate-set swap (F8).** Replace `discover_candidates(&jigc_home, &schemas)` at the single call site with a CLI-computed set: `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard -- '*.md'` via `git_capture` at `jigc_home`, `.jigc/` internals prune kept on top, `BTreeSet` re-sort/dedup (same-repo-in → same-verdicts-out), **no no-git fallback** — a git failure is a hard error (ingest already hard-requires a repo, `ingest.rs:82`); the engine walk + tests untouched. *Done:* a new named CLI integration test proves a gitignored `node_modules/pkg/README.md` is **absent** from the triage report while an untracked non-ignored `.md` **appears**; the existing `ingest.rs`/`ingest_flow12.rs` suites stay green; full gate. Files: `crates/cli/src/ingest.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/ingest.rs`.
- **T2 — engine `schema-conformance.repeatable-populated` + its two knobs + the store-scope arm.** A new engine check fn (schema + parsed doc → advisory when a required repeatable section parses zero items), **never wired into `schema_conformance`/`validate_task`** (fire points are store scope + T4's adopt arm only — "never a gate"); exemptions via the new **string knob** `validation.schema-conformance.repeatable-populated.exempt` (pack-default `"changelog#unreleased-changes milestone-record#tasks completion-record#findings"`, read through `Resolved::scalar`) + the tunable severity key + its `CHECK_INVENTORY` row; the store arm is a **dedicated walk covering location AND placement instances** (do *not* wholesale-extend family 5's presence/value checks to placement docs — scope creep), appended **after** the `doc_findings.is_empty()` version-mismatch adjudication (`validate.rs:585`) so the pure-stamp v0 case stays surfaced. *Done:* named tests green — a committed zero-item roadmap (placement) **and** a zero-item location-doctype instance each advise in the store sweep; an exempt token suppresses (`milestone-record#tasks`); the knobs/inventory count tests repaired in the same motion (30 keys / 27 rows), plus any flow-corpus repairs the new advisory forces; full gate. Files: `crates/engine/src/{validate.rs,result.rs,knobs.rs}`, `crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml`.
- **T3 — engine `schema-conformance.surplus-sections-absent` + its knob.** The raw-block scan: `scan_blocks` H2 count vs the schema's body-section count — **trailing** surplus only (a surplus H2 *between* sections already trips `conformance.section-renamed`); tunable severity key + `CHECK_INVENTORY` row; rides T2's store walk (location + placement). *Done:* named tests green — a committed doc with a trailing surplus H2 advises with the surplus count in the message; a between-sections surplus still trips `section-renamed` and does **not** double-fire this check; counts land at **31 keys / 28 rows** (validation.md's declared M40 landing tally); full gate. Files: `crates/engine/src/validate.rs` (+ `parse.rs` only if `scan_blocks` needs re-exposure), `crates/engine/src/{result.rs,knobs.rs}`, `crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml`.
- **T4 — the adopt-time triage annotations, row-carried in ALL output formats (F4's ingest half).** The CLI re-parse arm at `classify_row`: for an adoptable row, re-parse the in-hand source against the matched schema and run T2+T3's engine fns (the exempt knob applies — `resolved` is already in scope, `ingest.rs:86`); `TriageRow` gains a serialized annotations field (JSON additive — repair any exact-shape assertions in the same motion); the human/agent render carries the pinned shapes *"adopted — structurally empty: 0 \<items\>"* / *"adopted — N surplus trailing sections"*; **fixed-advisory** — an annotation never flips a verdict, blocks adoption, or exits non-zero. *Done:* a named integration test adopts a zero-item roadmap + a surplus-trailing-H2 doc and asserts the annotation on the row in **both** human and `--format json` output, rows still marked adopted; full gate. Files: `crates/cli/src/ingest.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/ingest.rs`.
- **T5 — the two-tier orphan route (F3).** `orphaned_docs` surfaces the matched doctype alongside the path (single call site); the `cli.rs` loop discriminates on `FileStateRecord` membership (`record.get(rel)`): **registered** → the existing stranded → `unmanage`/relocate route; **unregistered** → a "looks-managed-but-unregistered" advisory whose route is conditioned on the `migrate-<doctype>` workflow existing (the `migrate.rs` prefix-scan idiom): present → `jigc migrate <path> --as <doctype>` or ignore; absent → "ignore, or route to a human". Emission is **never** gated on membership — both tiers fire (fresh-clone = the unregistered arm); both codes stay un-keyed/non-inventory (exit stays 0). *Done:* `orphan_detection.rs` gains — (1) a registered strand keeps the stranded route; (2) a never-adopted basename-coincidence file (`research/notes.md` shape) yields the unregistered advisory routing "ignore, or route to a human" (no `migrate-research` ships yet); (3) a unit test over the route builder proves the `jigc migrate … --as …` text when the workflow exists (live pairing lands with Inc 7's seven workflows); full gate. Files: `crates/cli/src/orphan.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/orphan_detection.rs`.

All four grouped-scope bullets map: the candidate-set swap → T1 · the engine check pair + knob → **T2 (repeatable-populated + exempt knob) and T3 (surplus scan)** · the CLI re-parse arm at `classify_row` → T4 · the two-tier route → T5. Order is load-bearing: T4 consumes T2+T3's engine fns; T1 first so the ingest substrate T4 tests over is final; T5 is independent and closes. No design-doc task — validation.md/project-setup.md/parsing.md already carry the M40 blocks from Settle; the fold-back is Inc 8. *Why 5:* each task is gate-green alone with a real red step — T1 is a self-contained substrate swap, T2/T3 each fold their knob's forced count-test repairs in atomically, T4's annotations are additive visibility, T5 re-routes an existing un-keyed advisory.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 2 T4: `title-names-symbol` joins `CHECK_INVENTORY`; the route suggests, never dictates, the new title

The minted knob (`validation.doc-code.title-names-symbol.severity`, advisory-default, unfloored) needs a `CHECK_INVENTORY` row to be re-promotable — the post-pass re-grades members only — so the membership count goes 25 → 26 (29 keyed / 18 intrinsic / 11 tunable). The route text names `jigc doc retitle-item <item-addr> --title "<new title>"` with a **placeholder** title, not the anchored symbol: for the brand-name false-positive class the symbol would be the *wrong* title, and a descriptive (identifier-free) retitle also clears the check (executor-chosen per the T4 delegation).

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 2 T3: the set-field id-from guard mints `write.id-from-field`, one code, type-aware route

`set-field` on a repeatable item's heading-derived `id-from` field rejects with the single write-time code `write.id-from-field` for both arms (not `write.identity-change` — the string arm is a wrong-verb reject, not an identity change; the defect class is one, only the **route** is type-aware: string → `doc retitle-item <item-addr>`, enum → `remove-item` + `add-item` under the target category, T2's route text). The guard lives in `apply_field_target`, so the per-leaf verb and the `doc author` batch inherit it in one place (executor-chosen per the T3 delegation).

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 2 T2: the retitle-item enum refusal is `write.identity-change`, guard-before-presence

The CLI verb's unconditional enum-id-from refusal mints the write-time code `write.identity-change` (not `ID_FROM_ENUM_CODE` — the new title may BE a legal member; the reject is about *identity*, not value conformance) and runs **before** any read/copy-in, so a categorically-refused address never moves bytes regardless of item presence (mirrors add-item's guard-first ordering). Route text: `remove-item <addr>` + `add-item <dest-repeatable> --title "<new>"`, moving the prose in the same motion. `retitle-item` shares `remove_item_target`'s item-address forms verbatim (executor-chosen per the T2 delegation).

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 2 T1: `retitle_item`'s enum arm defers to the CLI guard

The engine op type-checks the new title against the block-declared id-from field (`check_value` → `MalformedValue` for a non-member enum title) but does **not** refuse a member-to-member enum retitle — the unconditional enum-id-from refusal lives in T2's CLI guard, one authoritative refusal seam mirroring add-item's (executor-chosen per the T1 delegation). Empty/whitespace titles reject as `WrongShape` (a titleless heading has no defined round-trip); errors use `GenerateError` (the nested-write shapes), since the id-from re-validation needs `MalformedValue`.

Outcome-compatible for every existing shape (tracked-unmodified: in index → included both ways; untracked foreign: absent both ways) — only the pre-staged shape changes behavior. *Done:* new tests in `crates/cli/tests/migrate_rollback.rs` green — (1) a migration finalize with a pre-staged `git rm <foreign>` + `--approve` exits 0, exactly one commit lands, `git show --name-status HEAD` carries the `D <foreign>` + the promoted doc (red today: exit 1, "did not match any files"); (2) the plain unstaged-`rm`/tracked-retire shape still stages the deletion (no regress); (3) `--dry-run` on the pre-staged shape forecasts the foreign as deleted, matching the landed manifest (the self-heal claim, proven) — plus the full gate. - **T2 — the return-type change + the two-axis scoped rollback.** `stage_migration` **returns its staged-pathspec set**; `try_execute_finalize_plan` captures it beside `retired` and threads it to `rollback_promotions`, which re-keys: **worktree** restores keyed on the retire **byte-capture set** (rewrite the captured bytes), **index** restores keyed on the **staged set** (`git restore --staged`) — a planned-but-untouched retirement is never restored; promotion rollback unchanged; the non-migration stage arms pass an empty staged set (they stage no retirements). Return + re-key are one task: the return exists solely to key the restores. *Done:* new test green — pre-staged `git rm` + a rejecting `pre-commit` hook: finalize fails, and afterwards the foreign stays absent from the worktree **and** its deletion stays staged (porcelain X column `D`), promoted copies removed (red today: the unconditional restore resurrects it); the two existing rollback tests (tracked-retire restore, untracked-foreign byte-rewrite) stay green under the re-key — both verified outcome-equivalent (tracked: captured bytes rewrite the worktree + the staged set restores the index entry; untracked: capture-set rewrite, never in the index) — plus the full gate. Files: `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/migrate_rollback.rs`.
- **T3 — the routed stage-phase wrap; commit-phase stays verbatim-raw.** A git failure during **staging** (`git_run` inside `stage_migration`/`stage_index_honoring`) surfaces as a **blocking routed finding** — a new `finalize.*` code + route, the git stderr embedded verbatim in the message — through the existing `blocked()` envelope, with the rollback still running first (the wrap discriminates stage-vs-commit failure inside `try_execute_finalize_plan`; mechanism is the executor's). The **commit-phase** path (`git_commit` hook rejection) is untouched — the recorded hook decision ([finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → 6. Commit) honored, its existing test asserting the raw output stays green as-is. *Done:* new test green — a deterministic stage failure (seed `.git/index.lock`) yields the findings envelope with the code + route + the verbatim git stderr, and the rollback ran (promoted copies gone); the commit-phase hook-rejection tests unchanged-green; full gate. Files: `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/migrate_rollback.rs`.

All four grouped-scope bullets map: discriminator swap → T1 · return-type change + scoped restore loops → T2 · routed wrap → T3 · dry-run self-heal → T1 (proven by test, per the gate-record claim). No design-doc task: finalize.md's rollback row + auto-migration.md's transaction rewrite already landed at Settle; the fold-back is Inc 8. *Why 3:* each task is gate-green alone with its own red step — the swap changes only the uncovered pre-staged shape, the re-key is outcome-equivalent for the covered shapes, the wrap is additive.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 6 build: tee install gated on the knob

The fd-tee is installed **only when the `invocation-log` knob resolves ON** (`enabled_logs_dir()` read once up front, before `Cli::try_parse()`), not unconditionally — because teeing repoints fd 1/2 at a pipe (`isatty` → false), which suppresses clap's terminal colour for `--help`/errors. Gating keeps that cost on the opted-in trial operator alone and matches the rest of `invocation_log`'s "no-op when OFF / outside a jigc repo" posture; the knob read needs no parsed `Cli`, so `--help`/`--version` still tee + log. The two `main()` log sites collapse to one (the clap `Err` arm now returns its `Outcome` instead of early-`return`ing after its own log call). EINTR-retry in the drain loop and a std-stream flush before fd restore keep the count exact and Unix-portable (no glibc-specific errno location). Landed test-first (`output_bytes` absent → red).

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 7 / T3 build: the form-vision empty-research advisory

Mechanism = a **CLI-side marker-block resolve**, not a new engine primitive (the general `state-aware-compose` stays stretch/1.1 per G7). `packs/methodology/steps/author-vision.yaml` carries the advisory prose (pack-owned content, right layer) at its opening, delimited by inert `<!-- research-advisory -->` / `<!-- /research-advisory -->` HTML-comment lines — which the step emitter passes through **verbatim** (comment-drop is top-level workflow-body only, not step bodies). `resolve_research_advisory` post-processes the composed `text`: it **keeps** the inner line when `warrants_research_advisory` (the workflow's `allows-create` admits `vision` **and** `committed_store` has no `research` key — absent ⇔ empty, since `committed_store` omits empty collections), else drops the whole block; the markers are **always** stripped, so they never leak. Applied at **both** compose exits — `compose_core` (mint / `--workflow form-vision`) **and** `compose_task_workflow` (resume), the only two paths that emit `author-vision` — because a strip in one alone would leak markers on the other. Keyed on `allows-create: vision`, not the literal workflow name, so it is not a hardcode. Advisory, never blocking (`grounded-in` is `0..*`; zero research is legal). No engine/schema change → freeze untouched. Test-first: `flow_form_vision_advisory.rs` red on the empty-store assertion (advisory absent) before the pack+CLI landed.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 7 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 7 — minting ergonomics: slug word-cap + `--slug` override + form-vision advisory](implementation/roadmap.md) into **3 ordered, single-concern tasks** (`T1`–`T3`), grounded in the code at HEAD `7fc8f6b` (tree clean). Settled basis: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 2026-07-06 M39 planning → *Slug (G6)* (word-count cap ~5 + reuse the `jigc rename` `--slug` flag, routed through the reject/resume collision path, **freeze-safe** — mint is CLI behavior, outside `schema-hash`) and *form-vision advisory (G7)* (query committed `research` count → print the route line; `grounded-in` is `0..*`, zero research a legal state). **The three grouped-scope bullets map one-to-one to the three tasks; none narrowed or deferred.** The tasks are independent (each gate-green alone) and ordered per the roadmap.

**Atomic-gate correction — the roadmap parenthetical "golden churn contained there [`slug.rs`]" is verified FALSE and must not be trusted as a pin.** `slugify` is called for *every* minted id (task ids, doc slugs, item anchors, migration ids), so the ~5-word cap re-slugs every existing test that hard-codes a **>5-word-derived** id — grepped at HEAD, **15 `crates/cli/tests/*.rs` suites** pin such literals as `--task` resume args / asserted paths (e.g. `move-the-session-cache-to-a-shared-redis-cluster` → capped `move-the-session-cache-to`; `cache-sessions-in-a-single-in-memory-node`, `enforce-the-rate-limit-at-the-gateway`, `add-a-greeting-helper-to-the-utils-package`, `cite-a-symbol-with-a-dirty-file`, `log-a-habit-in-one-tap`). The cap **breaks** those gate-covered suites and only re-pinning them repairs the gate, so the cap + its dependent-test updates are **one inseparable gate-green motion** (T1) — a `slug.rs`-only task can never reach a green `cargo test -p cli`. The tasks:

- **T1 — the slug word-cap (~5) + fold in the churn it forces.** Replace the 50-char `MAX_LEN`/`cap_at_boundary` in `crates/engine/src/slug.rs` with a **word-count cap** (keep at a `-` boundary, re-trim any exposed trailing `-`; the output stays a valid slug and idempotent). Re-pin the `slug.rs` `golden_table` insta snapshot (the `cap-at-boundary-50` / `cap-one-long-word` cases change) and add a point assertion proving a >5-word intent caps to ≤5 words. **Then update every dependent test the cap re-slugs** — the 15 suites that hard-code a >5-word-derived id: `crates/cli/tests/{e2e_audit,finalize_outcome_surface,finalize_to_git,file_state_soundness,superseding_decision,prd_inverse_cardinality,mention_resolves,validate_envelope,flow13_acceptance,flow13_contract_and_severity,implement_from_spec,flow15_dogfood_walk,doc_code_gate,prd_batch_author,doc_show}.rs` (update each hard-coded task-id/anchor literal to its capped form). `is_slug` is **not** length-capped (a ref to an existing long slug must still recognize it) — leave it untouched. *Done:* `cargo test -p engine slug` green with the re-pinned golden + the new >5-word point assertion, **and** `cargo test -p cli` green (every dependent id re-pinned), full dev gate clean. Files: `crates/engine/src/slug.rs` + the 15 cli test suites above. *Why:* the cap re-slugs every long id and only re-pinning the broken suites reaches a green gate — one atomic unit.
  - **T1 build note (2026-07-07):** the gate surfaced **5 more suites** the planner's literal grep missed — `flow27_marquee`, `flow28_marquee`, `migrate_adr`, `migrate_arch_doc`, `migrate_prd` — which derive the **migration task id** through their own `migration_task*` helpers rather than a hard-coded literal. Cause: a migration id-source is `migrate-<doctype>-<slug(path)>`, then `mint_id` re-slugifies it, so the cap now applies **twice** and a >5-word migration source truncates (e.g. `migrate-adr-docs-adr-0001-use-mysql` → `migrate-adr-docs-adr-0001`). Re-pinned by making each helper mirror the mint's outer `slugify` (wrap its result in `engine::slug::slugify`), which tracks the cap automatically. **Consequence noted (not a halt):** the cap makes `slugify` no longer the identity for a migration id-source, so two distinct foreign files sharing a 5-word path-prefix (e.g. deeply-nested `docs/decisions/architecture/records/adr-0001` vs `…/adr-0002`) now mint the **same** migration task id — this routes through the existing `mint_task` **serial-collision block** (a blocking, actionable finding, never silent), so it degrades gracefully within the settled collision path; the `migration_task_id_source` doc-comment's "the id-source is the id / slugify is the identity" now holds only for ≤5-word sources.

- **T2 — the `--slug` override on `jigc start` + `jigc doc create` + its collision routing.** Add the `--slug <explicit>` clap arg (reuse the `jigc rename` shape) to `StartCommand` and `DocCommand::Create` in `cli.rs`; validate the override via `engine::slug::is_slug` (reject a malformed override with an actionable route, do not silently re-slugify). Thread the optional override so it **drives the minted id** instead of `slugify(intent)`/`slugify(title)`: `start.rs::mint_in_repo` → `engine::state::mint_task`/`mint_id`; `doc.rs::run_create` → `engine::state::create_gated`/`create` (add an `Option<&str>` slug-override param; all in-crate callers updated in the same motion — additive, `None` = today's behavior, so no existing test breaks). **Collision routing is inherited, not new** (verified against the code): an explicit slug drives the id into the existing `dir.exists()` (start → `collision_finding` serial-collision reject/resume route) and `path.exists()` (create → `instance_collision_finding`) guards, so a colliding `--slug` rejects through the settled path — no new `--id`, no silent suffix. *Red-step assumptions to prove:* (1) `jigc start "<long intent>" --slug <explicit>` mints the task under `<explicit>` (not the capped-intent slug); (2) a `--slug` equal to an active task rejects via the serial-collision route; (3) `jigc doc create adr --title "<X>" --slug <explicit>` mints `adr:<explicit>` and a `--slug` colliding with a staged/committed instance rejects. *Done:* a new `crates/cli/tests/*.rs` suite asserting (1)–(3) over the built binary; full dev gate clean. Files: `crates/cli/src/{cli.rs,start.rs,doc.rs}`, `crates/engine/src/state.rs`.

- **T3 — the form-vision empty-research advisory.** A **CLI-side query** of the committed `research` count at compose of `form-vision`: zero committed `research` → emit the advisory route line ("no committed research exists; a vision grounds in research — consider `do-research` first") at the `author-vision` opening step; a non-empty store is **silent**. Advisory, never blocking (`grounded-in` is `0..*` — zero research is a legal state). ## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 6 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 6 — invocation-log output-size (fd-level tee)](implementation/roadmap.md) into **one** ordered single-concern task, grounded in the code at HEAD `38ad02f` (tree clean). **The atomic-gate call — why one task, not four:** the fd-tee, the `Record` field, the new dep, and the test are **one inseparable gate-green motion**. Verified against the code: (a) the tee's only observable output is its byte count, which is invisible until threaded into the recorded `output_bytes` field — a "tee-only" task has **no real red step** (a transparent pass-through tee leaves a known verb's output byte-identical, so an "output unchanged" test passes *without* the change); and (b) the dev gate runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `invocation_log` is a **binary-crate** module (`mod invocation_log;` in `main.rs`, driven by integration tests via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc`, never called directly), so a tee fn whose only user is `#[cfg(test)]` is **dead code in the `--bins` compile** → gate fails. Both point the same way: the tee must be wired into `main()`'s live dispatch in the same commit that introduces it. **The `Record` add is verified additive** — the existing `crates/cli/tests/invocation_log.rs` asserts fields by presence over `serde_json::Value` (no exhaustive golden), and `Record` is `#[derive(Serialize)]`-only with no `deny_unknown_fields`, so `output_bytes` breaks no existing test. The task:

- **T1 — the fd-level counting tee + `output_bytes`.** At `main()`, inside the span the timing `Instant` already opens (before `Cli::try_parse()`), save fd 1/2 (`libc::dup`), replace them with pipe write-ends (`libc::dup2`), spawn a per-stream drain thread that reads → counts → forwards to the saved fd; after all emission, restore the fds, close the write-ends, join the threads, read the two counts; add `output_bytes: u128` (stdout+stderr total) to the invocation `Record` and thread the count through `log_invocation`. Add the Unix-only dep (`libc` — the fd-swap needs raw `dup`/`dup2`; `os_pipe` is an optional pipe-construction helper, executor's call per the settled fork). *Red-step assumptions to prove (the tee's load-bearing properties, tested not trusted):* (1) **size == emitted** — a known-output verb's logged `output_bytes` equals the exact stdout+stderr byte count the driven binary emits (`Command`-captured); (2) **captures the clap arm** — `jigc --help` (the differentiator vs the rejected per-emitter tally, which records 0) records `output_bytes` == its emitted-stdout length, which forces the tee to span the `Err(err) => err.print()` arm and be torn down only *after* that emission but *before* the `log_invocation` write; (3) **transparency** — the verb's own captured output is unchanged (the tee forwards, never swallows). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli --test invocation_log` green incl. the new size==emitted + `--help` assertions, and the full dev gate (`build`/`test`/`clippy -D warnings`/`fmt --check`) clean. Files: `crates/cli/src/{main.rs,invocation_log.rs}`, `crates/cli/tests/invocation_log.rs`, `crates/cli/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.toml` (workspace dep).

All four grouped-scope bullets map to T1, none narrowed or deferred: the tee in `main.rs` · the `Record` field · the new dep · the size==emitted test. The design's "captures the true total incl. clap `--help`/`--version`" claim ([measurement.md](design/measurement.md):70 — byte-counts, *not* the deferred stderr-text capture) is pinned as red-step assumption #2, so the executor proves the clap-arm span rather than trusting it. No creep into later increments; the exhaustive reading-order fold-back (incl. `measurement.md` output-size) is Inc 8. *Why:* the tee, its recorded field, its dep, and its proof are one atomic unit — no sub-piece reaches a green gate alone.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 5 / T5: the foreign-squatter move-into-workbench arm + the two-resolutions reconcile

A **collision at a relocation destination** is resolved by the occupant's *kind* (`crates/cli/src/relocate.rs` → `displace_foreign_squatter`, threaded through `relocate_one`; reconciled in `design/reconciliation.md` → Relocation collisions): a **managed** instance already there (baselined in `file-state`) → adopt-in-place (M24), and moving the incoming managed instance *into* it (a managed move-INTO) is **deferred** — surfaced as a **block, never a clobber** (it needs an unmodeled managed-but-uncommitted state); a **foreign** (untracked/unmanaged, un-baselined) file → **moved into the gitignored `.jigc/` workbench**, out of the destination and uncommittable, so the managed instance lands and a stray working file is never committed or silently destroyed. Classification is by baseline — the same managed-vs-foreign line the rest of reconciliation draws. A committed-but-unmanaged squatter's tracked index slot is freed (`git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch`, a no-op for an untracked one) so the managed `git mv` into the vacated destination succeeds. **Workbench-subpath elaboration (the planner left the subpath an executor detail "within Inc 4's gitignore-3→1 collapse"):** a **dedicated `.jigc/displaced/`** entry added to the single-source `gitignore::ENTRIES` (+ the `milestone.rs` golden bumped) rather than reusing an existing ignored dir — every existing ignored subdir is either **enumerated** (`tasks/`/`milestones/`/`worktrees/` — `state.rs`/`milestone.rs` read them back as task/milestone/worktree ids) or a **typed cache** (`state/`/`index/`/`logs/`), so parked foreign detritus there would masquerade as a work-unit or pollute a cache; a dedicated home has no reader. The bound is settled **foreign-only** (the safe half — a foreign file has no identity/referrers); the managed half waits on the state it needs.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 5 / T4: the parallel freeze-exempt relocation path — a new `jigc relocate` verb

The frozen relocation arm (`migrate_corpus`) gates to the manifest set and *derives* each doctype's prior home from the versioned snapshot; a **freeze-exempt** doctype has no snapshot, so nothing pins where its instance *was*. Built the **parallel path** (`crates/cli/src/relocate.rs` → `relocate_freeze_exempt` / `relocate_stranded`): detect the committed instances stranded at a **human-supplied** prior home (`orphan::is_stranded` over `git ls-files`), then `git mv` each to the current schema home via the T1 primitive (`relocate::move_doc`), byte-preserving, file-state re-keyed. **Resolution-surface choice (the planner left this "new flag/verb vs. arm" as executor design):** a **new `jigc relocate <type> --from <prior-home>`** verb — freeze-exempt relocation needs a human-supplied prior home, so a first-class verb taking `--from` is the honest entry point (not an arg on `migrate-corpus`, whose contract is snapshot-derived + version-gated). `--from` parses to a `Home`: a `.md` value is a placement file, else a location dir. **The two paths are reconciled**: `relocate_freeze_exempt` **refuses** a doctype in `frozen_doctype_versions` (routes it to `migrate-corpus`), and `migrate-corpus`'s frozen gate skips the freeze-exempt complement — every persisted doctype relocates through exactly one path, keyed on frozen-vs-exempt. **Scope honesty (F8 / `storage.md:148`):** M39 closes *detect+route+offer-move with a supplied prior home*; it does **not** (cannot) auto-detect a freeze-exempt doctype's prior home — there is no record, by construction. Move is best-effort per-doc (`blocked` surfaced, never fatal), staged-not-committed like the T3 sibling.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 5 / T3: `config set docs-root` detect+route+**moves** (auto-move, staged-not-committed)

`config set docs-root` replaces its M36 warn-then-strand with **detect+route+move** (`crates/cli/src/config.rs` → `route_docs_root_repoint_orphans`): each committed doc the re-point would strand under the prior resolved root is **relocated** to the new root via the shared move primitive (`relocate::move_doc` — `git mv` + file-state re-key) and surfaced. **Auto-move is safe here** because a `docs-root` re-point has a *recorded prior home* — the old resolved root, deterministic from the current cascade (the freeze-exempt path, T4, has no snapshot → human-supplied). The destination is a **whole-path prefix swap** old-root → new-root (`reroot`): `docs-root` is a uniform prefix over every location doctype, so the doc's `<location>/<slug>.md` sub-path is invariant — no per-schema destination math. **Elaboration pins:** (a) the move is **staged, not committed** — it rides the working tree alongside the (already-uncommitted) manifest edit `config set` writes, so the operator commits both together (config-set never committed); (b) **best-effort** — a resolution/store hiccup returns silently and a per-doc move failure is surfaced (route: move by hand) but never fails the write (the set always lands). The `validate` orphan fire-point stays intact for strands that arise *another* way (an out-of-band manifest edit, a cross-machine commit landing before its docs move) — `orphan_detection.rs`'s validate case now re-points via a direct manifest edit to preserve that coverage.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 4 / T7: stale-base detection is a CLI git probe guarding *every* base-reading op; the engine owns only the finding shape

The stale-base edge (`design/team-ready-state.md` → Stale-base edge (history rewrite)) — a base-SHA pin naming a commit a history rewrite orphaned — is caught by a CLI `guard_base_live` run right after each op reads the base pin, *before* any git operation against the missing commit. **Detection is CLI-side** (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet <sha>^{commit}` — exit 0 ⇒ resolves to a commit, non-zero ⇒ gone): the engine does no git I/O, so it owns only the routed `milestone.stale-base` **finding shape** (`engine::milestone::stale_base_finding`, the `unknown_milestone_finding` sibling). **Guarded uniformly across all three base consumers** — `provision` (before `git worktree add`, else a half-provisioned worktree set), `finalize` (before the worktree-combine + base-guard `merge-base`, else materialize/flip/commit against a phantom base), and `join` (before resolving the committed index against a missing commit, which would silently mis-report the cross-area ref walk) — because a stale base is invalid for *every* op that reads it and "routes to the human" must be the same everywhere, not a hole in the omitting ops. The **zero-commit sentinel** (`EMPTY_TREE_SHA`) is exempt (a valid pre-first-commit base, never stale), so the guard adds no block on that path. Pre-fix the ops reached git with the bogus SHA and died with a raw `fatal: invalid reference` / `merge-base` error (provision partially); now a routed block fires first, no corruption/partial write. Proven by `crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_stale_base.rs` (a non-existent base SHA re-derived from the record on a fresh clone → provision registers no worktree, finalize makes no commit + does not flip the record).

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 4 / T6: the record reconcile preflight uses `reconcile_committed` (per-doc, `task_touched: true`), not the store sweep

The No-silent-overwrite guard (`design/team-ready-state.md` → F3) runs before every `set: on-transition` record overwrite (`add-task` append, finalize status-flip) and conflict-blocks if the committed `milestone-record` drifted out-of-band. **Elaboration (faithful to F3's intent, not its literal wording):** F3/the T6 planner-note named `reconcile_committed_store`, but that whole-store wrapper *cannot* express the guard F3 mandates. F3 is explicit — "detected + conflict-blocked, **not absorbed**" — yet `reconcile_committed_store` would **absorb** a *conformant* OOB edit (the `DRIFTED + UNTOUCHED` arm silently re-baselines it, e.g. a valid `status: active → joined` hand-edit), which is exactly the silent clobber F3 forbids; and it sweeps sibling records + every unrelated committed doc the milestone op has no business gating on. The CLI op *is* the machine touching the record, so the guard drives the **per-doc primitive** `reconcile_committed` with **`task_touched: true`** — precisely the `DRIFTED + TOUCHED → reconciliation.conflict-block` arm ("both sides moved; no silent merge"), scoped to this one record. Baseline lifecycle: each record **write** (`create`/`add-task`) advances the `.jigc/state/file-state.json` baseline to what the CLI wrote, so a legit sequential op sees `IN_SYNC` (the guard is inert on a clean record) while an OOB edit reads as drift; no edge-index write reaches disk (absorb, the sole mutator, is unreachable under `task_touched: true`). Dev-only (no `milestone-record` schema) is inert. Proven by `crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_reconcile.rs` (a *valid*-enum OOB edit blocks both overwrite sites → the record is not overwritten; the clean path stays green).

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 4 / T4: the `join`-flip folds into the finalize commit, transactionally

`milestone finalize` under `[dev ▸ methodology]` now flips the committed `milestone-record` (`engine::join_record` — every `tasks` item + header `status` active → joined, byte-stable) and **path-adds the flipped record into the ONE finalize commit** alongside the promoted docs (via the shared `overlay_docs_commit_and_ff` pathspecs, threaded through the milestone `StagePolicy::Combine`/`ChainPerSubtask` variants) — never a second commit; the flip's byte-change gates `has_diff` so a docs-only milestone whose only change is the flip is not an empty-commit block. **Elaboration (kept minimal-correct):** a `RecordFlipGuard` restores the pre-flip bytes on any blocked/failed finalize (base-mismatch, hook rejection) and is disarmed only once the commit lands — the flip is a write to a *committed, tracked* path, so "Writes are transactional" (CLAUDE.md) demands it not persist without its commit; the design's "join folds into the commit" ([team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The commit model) implied but did not spell out the block-restore. Dev-only (no `milestone-record` schema) resolves no record → inert, the finalize path byte-untouched.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 build: the milestone-finalize base-guard refinement (Inc 4/T4 fork)

The build halted at Inc 4/T4: the per-op record-commit model (settled 2026-07-06) advances HEAD, but `plan_milestone_finalize`'s preflight requires `base.sha == head_sha` ([finalize.rs:510](crates/engine/src/finalize.rs)) — the M31 worktree-combine external-drift guard — so finalize blocks; and **`record.base` is structurally always ≥1 commit behind HEAD** (a record commit cannot store its own resulting sha), so `base == HEAD` can *never* hold once per-op record commits land, on a fresh clone too. A genuine fork planning missed (the design-review's F4 checked commit *staging*, not the HEAD-advance-vs-finalize-guard interaction; the Inc-4 planner asserted "no new fork"); the build harness caught it and halted rather than guessing. **Settled (human): relax the guard, keep per-op commits.** The preflight becomes: if `base == HEAD` proceed (fast path); else if `base` is a **linear ancestor** of HEAD **and every commit in `base..HEAD` touches only this milestone's record path** (`docs/milestone-records/<id>.md`), advance `base → HEAD` and proceed; else block (`base-mismatch`, unchanged). This matches the guard's *true intent* — catch **external** drift, not the milestone's own bookkeeping — and preserves the M31 worktree-combine guarantee (a record-only commit touches no code, so the combine base is unaffected; any foreign code/doc commit in the range still blocks). The **engine does no git I/O** (invariant intact): the CLI computes the range's linearity + record-only-ness and feeds the result to `plan_milestone_finalize`. Design of record: [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The commit model; owed to finalize.md/storage.md at the Inc-8 reading-order fold-back. Fix lands **test-first** (a foreign commit in range still blocks) as a task before T4 resumes.

Cut [Increment 4 — team-ready layout: record/WIP split + commit model + fresh-clone](implementation/roadmap.md) into **7 ordered, single-concern tasks** (`T1`–`T7`), grounded in the code at HEAD `39f3307` (tree clean). ## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 3 T4: the record's `base` field stores both sha and short

Building T4's read-back, the planning claim (e) round-trip obligation resolved **not-lossless**: `short` is `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, a **variable-length** unambiguous abbreviation, so it is *not* a fixed prefix of the full sha and cannot be reconstructed from the sha alone. Per the planner's pre-resolved contingency ("if it isn't lossless, the base field must store both"), the record's `meta.base` header field now stores **both**, space-joined (`base: <sha> <short>`) — mirroring `base.json`, which already persists both. This makes `read_back_record` a lossless inverse of `render_fresh_record`, so deleting the `.jigc` cache and re-deriving from the committed `.md` yields a byte-identical `BasePin` (sha AND short). Cost: T1/T2's byte-goldens gained the short on the `base:` line (freeze-exempt doctype, no version-gate; no CLI/flow golden depends on it — Inc 4 not yet built). The read-back finding for a non-conforming / base-less record is `milestone.record-read-back` (routed, blocking); `reseed_cache_from_record` re-derives both cache files when either is absent, else no-ops. Cross-ref [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → Engine capability 2.

- **T1 — engine: extend `store::read_slice` to whole-doc + item/leaf/deep.** Lift `store.no-fragment` so a fragmentless `<type>:<slug>` renders the **whole** committed doc, and lift `store.unsliceable-fragment` so a `UnitLeaf`/`UnitItem`/`UnitItemLeaf`/`Deep` fragment slices the addressed item/leaf over the already-parsed `ParsedSection`/`ParsedItem` data (the byte-stable span read, the writer's inverse). *Done:* `engine` unit tests (`cargo test -p engine`) prove — (a) a committed `adr`/`spec` read with **no fragment** returns the full doc content; (b) an item slice (`spec:…#criteria/<id>`) returns that item and a leaf slice (`#criteria/<id>/statement`) returns the leaf prose byte-for-byte; (c) an existing `#unit` slot slice still resolves byte-identical (no regression), and a `store.not-found`/`store.no-such-section` miss still blocks with its route. Full four-command gate green. *Why:* one coherent engine concern (the store reader gains the two shapes the read surface needs); additive — verified no test pins the two lifted codes and every live compose deref carries a `#unit` fragment (grounding (a)/(c)), so nothing the gate covers breaks. Files: `crates/engine/src/store.rs` (+ `address.rs` if a fragment-variant helper is needed). Design [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Identity is the path; [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The read surface.
- **T2 — cli: the `jigc doc show` verb + dispatch + the stable `--format json` serializer.** Add `DocCommand::Show { addr }` + its `dispatch`/`run_doc` arm, rendering the addressed ref two ways: **plain text** via the T1-extended `read_slice`; **`--format json`** via a net-new serializer emitting the pinned shape `{ type, slug, fields: {…}, sections: { <section>: <slot-prose-string> | [ {…item fields…}, … ] } }` (enum leaves lowercase-string), where a `#section` slice returns the item array. *Done:* a `crates/cli/tests/*.rs` suite drives the **real binary** — (a) `jigc doc show vision:<slug>` round-trips a committed `vision` (plain output carries every section; `--format json` matches a **pinned golden**, the stable contract); (b) `jigc doc show <spec/prd repeatable ref>` returns the item on a `#section/<id>` slice and the item **array** under `--format json`; (c) a bad ref exits non-zero with the routed block envelope (the existing failure funnel). Full gate green. *Why:* the verb, its dispatch, and the json serializer are one atomic gate-green unit — the serializer's only caller is this verb, so splitting it is dead code that fails `clippy -D warnings`; this task pins the 1.0 json contract (a one-way door) via its golden. *Builds on T1.* Files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs` (json shape), `crates/cli/tests/*.rs`. Design [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The read surface (json shape, line 74); [introspection.md](design/introspection.md):24 (the `doc show` forward-ref made real).

Order is engine read-capability → CLI verb + json contract. No atomic-gate coupling forces a merge: T1 is additive and green standalone (grounding (a)/(c)); T2 builds on it and is itself indivisible (verb + serializer). No new fork surfaced — the one design detail Inc 1 owns (a slot section's json serialization) is pinned by T2's golden per the design skeleton (grounding (d)), not a halt. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 39 → Increment 1. **Status: planned; hand off to task execution.**

## 2026-07-06 — M39 planning: decomposition (8 increments, risk-first)

Cut into **8 ordered, single-concern, risk-first increments** ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 39): (1) `jigc doc show` + `read_slice` whole-doc/item/leaf extension + stable `--format json`; (2) compose renders **all** grounded sources (multi-target `walk_edge` + the M37-doc revise + flip the two pinning tests); (3) the `milestone-record` doctype engine core (the `set: on-transition` write with its distinct append/in-place-mutate arms + the read-back authority making the committed `.md` the source of truth); (4) team-ready layout — the `milestone_dir` record/WIP split + path-scoped commit-at-each-op + gitignore 3→1 + fresh-clone resume + OOB conflict-block; (5) the freeze-exempt relocation floor (orphan re-key + extracted rename-move + parallel path + `config set` detect+route); (6) the invocation-log fd-tee output-size (the adoption-trial prerequisite); (7) minting ergonomics (slug word-cap + `--slug` + form-vision advisory); (8) acceptance + the reading-order doc fold-back (the M38 Inc-6 pattern). Ordering: the read surface first (the milestone record witnesses its json contract), the doctype engine before its layout/commit model, the floor after the doctype exists, the self-contained instrumentation + riders late, fold-back last. The planning gate-record ([completions/artifacts/M39/planning-gate-record.md](completions/artifacts/M39/planning-gate-record.md)) filled clean — no halts. **Status: planned; hand off to the build harness** (`milestone-build M39`).

## 2026-07-06 — M39 planning: Settle — the pre-1.0 RC-findings wave, forks resolved

Baseline verified by 4 `capability-auditor`s + gap-probed by 4 `gap-detector`s (all **exercised** at HEAD `f372b2b`, not read off roadmap prose); 2 `robust-advocate`s ran the cheap-vs-robust forks. Scope confirmed (human): the five core features stay **one milestone** — "size is not a constraint; do it now; make it robust." Forks settled:

- **Team-ready state → (c) a managed work-unit-record doctype** (not a raw-JSON relocate). Robust-advocate's decider: (c) is the *only* shape that **preserves** the [storage.md](design/storage.md) "the `.md` set is the only source of truth" invariant (the record *joins* the managed set) — a committed raw-JSON record *breaks* it (a second, unreconciled source of truth); and (c) is the only shape readable through `jigc doc show`, the read surface **M39 itself builds**, so a cheap cut ships M39 in self-contradiction. **Freeze-exempt** (methodology infra). The record/WIP split (today one `.jigc`-rooted `milestone_dir`) is drawn **field-granular**: intent/status/task-membership = committed record; `docs/`/worktrees/caches = gitignored WIP. Rests on the M12/M14/M16 working-docs→doctypes arc — `completion-record` (milestone-*close* state as a doctype) is the shipped precedent, so [doctype-map.md](implementation/doctype-map.md):51 "work-units are not doctypes" governs work-unit **identity**, not the **state a work-unit emits**. The one genuinely-new engine capability is a **set-on-transition** machine-maintained doctype (a CLI-appended ordered id-list) — assembled from proven primitives (M16 repeatable-section + `add-item`, M22 on-create materialization, M16 singleton-slug, M38 placement).
- **Log output-size → an fd-level counting tee at `main()`** (not a per-emitter tally). Robust-advocate's decider: the robust cut is *smaller* (one file vs 122 scattered print sites), structurally un-bypassable, and captures the clap `--help`/`--version` output the tally records as size 0; the cheap cut silently under-counts the exact mass-output (A7) it exists to measure, feeding a wrong number into the 1.0.0 GO call + the post-1.0 token-budget workstream. Cost accepted: one new dep (`libc`/`os_pipe`) + Unix-only (jigc's target).
- **doc-read-surface → `jigc doc show` ships a stable `--format json` contract from 1.0** (its own one-way door, accepted — the milestone exists to make the read surface something agents rely on). Net-new verb; `store::read_slice` extended for whole-doc + item/leaf (isolated from the write path — cannot regress the writer). Homes at a read-surface part-doc (not `write-commands.md`, which is write-side by charter; not `introspection.md`, which excludes filled-prose reads — its `:24` forward-ref to `doc show` becomes real).
- **Relocation floor / `config set docs-root` → detect+route+offer-move** (not warn-only, not hard-block): the set still applies but surfaces the orphaned instances + offers the extracted rename-move as resolution, honoring detect-and-route-never-silent. Freeze-exempt doctypes carry **no recorded prior home** (no snapshot) → the from-path is supplied explicitly (human/CLI arg); auto-move stays unsafe. The orphan detector is re-keyed on a recorded prior home (today it keys on the location-dir *basename*, blind to placement/root/rename homes — `validation.md:279`'s "the only stable discriminator is the location directory" is scoped, not left standing); the `rename` git-mv+re-key move is **extracted** from `apply_and_commit` into a standalone primitive; a **parallel freeze-exempt relocation path** is built (the M38 transform gates to the frozen manifest set).
- **Grounded-sources render (G2) → revise the M37 doc + build the multi-target slice.** [design-altitude-doctypes.md](design/design-altitude-doctypes.md) §3 constraint 2 documented first-only render as *intended*, but its basis ("the other groundings are in session memory") was **falsified by the trial** for a fresh session — a clean *revise* (stored `grounded-in` anchor unchanged; only the read view widens). Engine lift: `ContentStore::walk_edge` `Option<String>`→multi-target (blast radius 1 trait/1 impl/1 caller; validation's all-edge `ref_resolves` untouched); flip the two green tests that pin the bug (`flow_form_vision.rs:353`, `flow_design_altitude.rs:389`).
- **Slug (G6) → word-count cap (~5) + reuse the existing `jigc rename` `--slug` flag** on `start`/`doc create` (not a new `--id`), routed through the reject/resume collision path. Corrected premise (the cited RC slugs are clean word-boundary cuts, not mid-word — the defect is the 50-**char** cap producing long filler-ending slugs). Freeze-safe (mint is CLI behavior, outside `schema-hash`).
- **form-vision advisory (G7) → a narrow CLI-side advisory now** (query committed `research` count → print the route line); the general `state-aware-compose` primitive stays **stretch**/1.1. Direction pre-settled route-not-merge/advisory; `grounded-in` is `0..*` (zero research is a legal state).
- **move-INTO-workbench → foreign files only for M39** (the squatter case); move-INTO for a *managed* instance is deferred (needs an unmodeled "managed-but-uncommitted" doctype state). Reconcile the two-resolutions-for-one-collision (adopt-in-place vs. relocate-into-workbench) in [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md).

Owed/flagged: if the work-unit-record doctype is read by the planning loop, the **planning-gate-record doctype** (condition-keyed) may reopen; keep the **per-developer/team-layer config-distribution** deferral out of scope (don't let the record's stored shape pre-decide it). Ground truth: [trial-record](completions/artifacts/RC-greenfield/trial-record.md) + the auditor/gap ledgers.

**Independent design-review (pre-decompose) — 8 findings, all accepted + baked** into [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md): **F1 (blocking)** the record→engine *read-back* half was undesigned — settled **(a) the committed `.md` is the engine's authority**, `.jigc/*.json` demoted to a rebuildable cache re-derived from the record on a fresh clone (a *second* engine capability beyond `set: on-transition`), making "delete `.jigc`, rebuild from `.md`" genuinely true; "continue" = resume un-joined tasks from scratch (the existing restart-from-scratch policy), not WIP recovery; the history-rewrite edge (stale base-SHA pin) degrades via detect→route, a property of any sha pin, revisit if real (human call). **F2 (blocking)** the doctype is named **`milestone-record`** (not `milestone` — the work-unit owns the `milestone:<id>` address + `doctype-map.md:51`), slug = the milestone work-unit id. **F3 (blocking)** pure-machine-maintained (human-surface fork settled *no authored slot*); OOB drift is **detected + conflict-blocked** via a reconcile preflight before any overwrite (never silently clobbered) — the "reconciled like any doc" framing corrected. **F4** milestone-op commits are **path-scoped** (record file only, never sweeping WIP — the M30/M31 discipline); `create`/`add-task` are separate record-only commits, `join`'s status-flip folds into the existing join commit. **F5** the `join` **in-place mutate** arm is designed separately from the `add-task` append arm (byte-stable item-leaf rewrite of N items, its own red acceptance). **F6** the `doc show --format json` shape over the repeatable section is **pinned now** (1.0 one-way door). **F7** home is flat `milestone-records/` (consistent with `completion-record`'s `completions/`). **F8** the relocation floor's scope is stated honestly (which arm of the `storage.md:148` obligation M39 closes vs. leaves owed). Gate-record + decomposition follow.

## 2026-07-04 — M38 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 4 — the relocation transform kinds (engine)](implementation/roadmap.md) into **2 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded in the code at HEAD `a3302d4` (tree clean; Inc 1's `placement` key + `display-title` knob, Inc 2's reconcile/ownership, Inc 3's `root-render` retire + freeze-exempt relocations all landed). The one grouped-scope bullet ("the two classifier arms + the driver move-arm + the census safety rows — write-order, abort-strands-neither, re-key atomic") maps across the tasks: **the two classifier arms (`schema_diff`) + their transform handling (the `display-title-changed` H1 splice; `relocated` as a content no-op) → T1**; **the git-free move-arm in `migrate-corpus` + all three census safety rows (write-before-remove, abort-strands-neither, re-key `from→to` atomic) → T2**. This is a **substrate** increment proven **synthetically on a reconstructed fixture** (the M34-Inc-2 shape) — the real `changelog` schema flip + snapshot + real-binary acceptance are Inc 5/6, not narrowed away here.

**Grounding (verified against the code, not assumed):** (a) the **only** exhaustive `match` on `SchemaChange` is `transform.rs:144` (`match change`); the CLI's sole `SchemaChange` match (`migrate_corpus.rs:326` `per_doc_changes`) carries a `_ => true` catch-all (`:331`), so adding the two variants **forces** `transform.rs` to gain arms **in the same commit** (else the match is non-exhaustive → compile error → red gate) but does **not** break the CLI compile — so T1 = *variants + their transform arms*, one atomic engine unit, and T1/T2 are separable. (b) `schema_diff` (`schema_diff.rs:91`) today diffs only sections/fields and **never inspects** `location`/`placement`/`display-title`; the two new arms classify **outside** the per-section loop from the two `Schema` values alone (domain-empty, engine-pure): a pure home change (v1 `location` → v2 `placement`) → exactly `[Relocated{from,to}]` (not `[]`), a `display-title` add/change → `[DisplayTitleChanged{to}]`, `from`/`to` auto-derived from the two schemas' declared homes (no hand-written recipe — the determinism boundary). (c) there is **no** existing H1-rewrite primitive in `write.rs` (the H1 is emitted at `write.rs:148` `# {title}`; `set_slot`/`set_field` are the splice siblings) — so T1 builds the byte-stable H1 splice the `display-title-changed` arm needs, following `set_slot`'s re-render-the-region pattern (`write.rs:916` — a bare span splice is not byte-stable). (d) `transform()` (`transform.rs:136`) already carries `source` + `changes` + both schemas, so `DisplayTitleChanged{to}` needs no signature change (the new title rides the variant); `Relocated` is a **content no-op** in `transform()` (the WidenedCardinality sibling — the move is a filesystem op the CLI owns, never a content edit), so a pure relocation folds to byte-identical `v2 == source` and still gates clean, then the CLI move-arm relocates it. (e) the CLI move-arm site: `migrate_committed_corpus` (`migrate_corpus.rs:158`) writes each migrated doc back via `engine::state::persist(&repo_root.join(id), v2)` at the **same** path (`id == rel_key`), and the per-doctype walk keys on `dt.to.location` (`:175`, `continue` on `location: None`) — but a relocated doctype's `to` is `placement` (`location: None`), so the walk must instead key on the **`from`** home (census: "the corpus walk keys on the `from` home … not the empty `to`"); T2 teaches the move-arm to walk `from`, write the gated v2 bytes to `to`, `remove(from)`, and re-key file-state `from→to`. (f) the **abort-strands-neither** test has a precedent: `written_docs_are_baselined_..._when_a_later_write_aborts` (`:766`) forces an `engine::state::persist` failure by pre-occupying the `.tmp` sibling — T2 reuses that fault-injection to prove an abort **between** write-`to` and remove-`from` leaves **both** copies on disk (never zero). (g) both tasks are additive to the shipped surface — **no** shipped doctype declares a `location→placement` relocation until Inc 5, so the new classifier arms emit nothing over the dev/methodology packs and the existing `migrate_corpus` tests stay green; each task reaches a green four-command gate at its own commit (no atomic-gate coupling forces a merge — grounding (a)). (h) file-state re-key uses the existing `FileStateRecord::{get,record}` (`migrate_corpus.rs:280-281`); a re-key is a remove-old-key + record-`to` paired atomically with the move (the per-doc-commit discipline the verb already upholds).

- **T1 — the two classifier arms + their transform handling (engine, one atomic unit).** In `crates/engine/src/schema_diff.rs` add `SchemaChange::Relocated { from, to }` + `SchemaChange::DisplayTitleChanged { to }` and classify them in `schema_diff` **outside** the per-section loop, reading `location`/`placement`/`display-title` from the two schemas: a home change (v1 `location`-home → v2 `placement`-home) emits `Relocated{from,to}` with both homes auto-derived from the schemas; a `display-title` add-or-change emits `DisplayTitleChanged{to}` (equal/absent-on-both → no emit). In `crates/engine/src/transform.rs` add the two `match change` arms the new variants force: `DisplayTitleChanged{to}` rewrites the doc's H1 line to `# {to}` via a new byte-stable `write.rs` H1 splice (only the H1 line changes, every other byte preserved); `Relocated{..}` is a **content no-op** (the move is the CLI's filesystem op). *Done:* `cargo test -p engine` proves — (a) `schema_diff` of a **pure home change** classifies to exactly `[Relocated{from,to}]` (not `[]`), `from`/`to` the two derived homes; (b) a `display-title` add classifies to exactly `[DisplayTitleChanged{to}]`; (c) a combined location→placement + display-title-add pair classifies **both** kinds; (d) the `DisplayTitleChanged` transform over a synthetic doc with a lowercase H1 rewrites **only** the H1 (`# changelog`→`# Changelog`), round-trips byte-identical under the target schema, and is deterministic; (e) a `Relocated`-only diff folds to byte-identical output (content no-op). Retired-mechanism grep returns zero; foreign-`VISION.md` protection is now the **inherited** `finalize.promote-clobber` (no bespoke guard).

**Elaboration pin — a placement census site the relocation exposed:** the finalize `has_diff` signal (`task.rs`, non-migration arm) computed `staged_promotable` from `schema.location.is_some()` only, so a **placement** doctype (`location: None`) was dropped through the transient arm — a vision-only task whose sole diff is the `VISION.md` promotion tripped `finalize.empty-commit`. `placement_acceptance.rs` passed only incidentally (untracked `.jigc/config` supplied the signal). Fixed to mirror `plan_promotions`' promotability (`location.is_some() || placement.is_some()`); now covered by the re-pointed `flow_form_vision` / `design_altitude_schemas` vision-finalize tests (research committed first, so the placement promotion is the only diff). ## 2026-07-04

- **M37 inc-4 T3 — the `form-vision` re-entry flow ships; the managed vision lands at `vision/vision.md`, not the design's `docs/vision/vision.md`.** The three pack files (`create-vision` singleton command-ref, the re-entry `author-vision` step embedding the `{{ @task.vision.grounded-in#findings }}` edge-walk slice, the `form-vision` workflow) compose zero-engine-change: the multi-valued `grounded-in` set + edge-walk slice + `--task` re-compose are all proven-shipped mechanisms. The acceptance drives the load-bearing ordering (slice EMPTY at first compose, NON-EMPTY only after `set-field grounded-in` + re-compose — the first-bound research's findings read, the second's absent). Correction to the design's stated path (`design-altitude-doctypes.md` §2/§4/§7): the methodology pack ships **no `docs-root` knob**, and its whole `knobs.yaml` shadows the dev base's `docs-root: docs/` default, so every methodology doctype lands **flat** at its `location:` (`research/`, `ideas/`, `vision/vision.md`) — the design's `docs/vision/vision.md` describes the intended nesting, never the composed path. The `root-render: VISION.md` still lands byte-faithful at the repo root, and the H1 reads `# Vision` (display-title knob). Fold-back (doctype-map row) should use `vision/vision.md`.
- **M37 inc-2 T2 — root-render's "not in file-state" is scoped to the managed-doc set.** The engine `FinalizePlan.renders` carries each `root-render:` target; the CLI writes it byte-faithful to the promoted managed doc, stages + rolls it back alongside promotions, and the non-destructive first-write guard (`finalize.root-render-foreign`) blocks a foreign-file clobber (managed-doc-absent + target-present) before any plan. The render is excluded from the engine's `hash_updates` **managed-doc** set (the reconcile baseline) — proven in the engine unit — but, like every committed file (code, configs), it still carries the *universal* post-commit committed-file baseline; that is not a managed-doc entry and, since the render lives outside any `location:` dir, the reconcile sweep never treats it as one. So the design-note's "not added to file-state" is honored at the load-bearing layer (never a managed/reconciled doc, overwritten freely each finalize) without special-casing it out of the universal committed-file sweep.
