## 2026-06-16 — M24 completion: built + audited, e2e overall-pass, 4 audit findings auto-fixed

All seven increments built and independently validated clean; the milestone-completion audit (code-review + e2e) ran on the rebuilt binary. The build harness **halted twice, neither a design failure**: (1) at Inc-3 T2 on a genuine planning gap — the pre-existing top-level `remove_item` left a dangling EOF blank line when removing the *last* item, which the planner's "reuse the verified `remove_item`" assumption missed (it was byte-stable only for non-last items, the `remove_item_first` golden); resolved by an inserted engine-hardening commit mirroring `remove_nested_item`'s last-block edge (`6fce01e`, red golden `remove_last_item_round_trips_byte_stable`), then T2 completed via a `build-executor` (`d9b167e`). (2) An **orchestration plumbing** halt on resume — the `args` object reached the workflow script JSON-stringified, so `skipThrough` was dropped (→ 0) and the loop tried to re-plan already-built Inc 1; the `build-planner` correctly **refused to re-plan committed work** rather than duplicate a DECISIONS entry. Fixed in the workflow script's arg-parsing (recover a stringified-object `args`); **no repo change**. A build subagent also branched at Inc 6 (`m24-inc6-plan`) and never returned to `main`; the work was strictly ahead, folded back by fast-forward (no divergence).

**What shipped (no new schemas):** the **declarative whole-doc batch** `jigc doc author <doctype> --from <payload>` (Path A — `create_gated` then chain the existing splice primitives over one in-memory buffer, no persist between leaves, persist once; **byte-identical to the per-leaf chain**, dated and dateless); **write-time value validation** via one shared id-from-enum slug+membership helper called by both `add-item` and finalize + the closed item-field parity gap; **`remove-item`** (top-level + the new nested `remove_nested_item`); **migration-mode date-suppression** (CLI-side, gated by the recorded `source-path` — dateless sources render no date, no schema edit); the **in-location-squatter blank-seed** (the `source-path == promote-destination` discriminator extended from the retire side to `state::create` step 4, sharing one path-normalization, M16 clobber-fix intact); the **finalize-path** lift (auto-provisioned formulaic migration commit, migration-scoped `git add` of {promote + retire + jigc's own tracked config}, the advisory heuristic structural fidelity release-delta summary); `migrate-<doctype>` task naming; and the author-migration **map+merge** guidance. Framing A held throughout (the batch is CLI placement of agent-authored prose; it never touches the `{{source}}` seam; the auto-commit summary/body is a pure function of source-path + doctype; the fidelity summary is advisory and feeds no decision).

**Audit verdict:** **e2e overall-PASS** — all seven increments + worked-examples flow 26 proven through the rebuilt binary, determinism (byte-identical across independent runs) + the non-changelog MVP regression both clean; **code-review found no blocking defects** (two LOW notes were latent fragilities within documented contracts). **The measured done-bar** ([completions/artifacts/M24/migration-quality-measure.md](completions/artifacts/M24/migration-quality-measure.md)): the FULL live migration of **project-delta** (13 releases / 20 change-groups, 53/53 bullets preserved) and **project-gamma** (80 releases / 127 change-groups, 433/433 preserved), each authored in **ONE** batch call, byte-stable, retired + adopted — the **agent-call count cut from 54→1 (project-delta) and 335→1 (project-gamma)**, the verbosity fix's payoff and the milestone's whole point.

**4 audit findings auto-fixed** (triaged by size-not-severity; none too-big or contested): (a) the batch payload silently misrouted a slot value lacking the `<<…>>` marker into a field block — now rejects the whole payload **loudly** at parse, cross-checking each value's marker against the schema leaf-kind (`73a16ac`); (b) migration-mode on-create suppression dropped **all** on-create fields, not just date — scoped to the date stamp so M25's generalization inherits the right mechanism (`868642b`); (c) the migration-stage `git add` pushed `.jigc/config`/`.jigc/.gitignore` as unconditional pathspecs that would abort the byte-destructive commit if absent — now guarded on existence (`b189b52`); (d) the review-gate structural summary omitted its line when nothing was dropped — now always rendered (`(none)` when empty), matching flow 26 (`a60d4ef`). Verified-and-NOT-fixed: the fuzzy version-scan's possible false "dropped" lines (by design, within the settled C4 advisory contract); the serial-collision-via-proxy test note (behavior correct, validator-confirmed); the type/scope hardcode vs materialization (boundary-safe and correct — the prescribed materialization can't produce the doctype-varying `scope`).

Gate green from clean main (fmt/clippy/**1162 tests**/build). M24 commits `3b6a26d…a60d4ef`. Binary rebuilt + re-pinned (both bin dirs). **Honest bound:** changelog-only — M25 generalizes the corrected pattern to `adr`/`spec`/`prd`; M26 = arch-doc (code-anchors + the deferred empty-slot+field-group byte-stability fix). The grooved planning→build→audit→auto-fix loop held end-to-end. [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M24 Outcome.

## 2026-06-17 — M25 planning: generalize migration to the location-bearing doctypes adr/spec/prd

Planned via `/milestone-plan` from clean `main` (HEAD `39989a1`). Baseline verified by 3 `capability-auditor`s + 4 `gap-detector`s **exercising** the HEAD binary (not reading-and-inferring). The verified ledger separated what M23/M24 built **doctype-general** (the `migrate` verb arg surface, engine `create`'s per-title slug minting at the location, the declarative `doc author --from` batch, the supersedes forward-ref gate at finalize, the `cites-code` doc-code probe, write-time enum validation, committed-field-update via copy-on-first-touch, multi-word-heading, optional slot/field) from what carries a **singleton/changelog assumption** that breaks for multi-instance. Two handover claims were **corrected by exercise**: (a) "adr's historical date already works" is only half-true — an *explicit* date survives, but a *dateless* foreign adr **fabricates today** because the doc-level on-create materializer (`on_create_doc_fields`, `doc.rs:765`) takes no migration flag (M24 scoped suppression to the item-level path only; adr's `date` is a doc-level header field); (b) "M24 fixed the in-location squatter" is **singleton-gated** (`state.rs:691` `&& schema.singleton`) and does not apply to non-singletons.

**The four human-gated forks settled:**
- **Migration model = one-file-one-task, sequential** (not a dir/multi-instance one-pass). `jigc migrate <path> --as <doctype>` stays one foreign file → one doc → one commit; a corpus is N invocations. The one blocker is the **fixed `migrate-<doctype>` task-id** (`start.rs:114`; `mint_task` hard-rejects, never suffixes) — a 2nd `migrate --as adr` collides (**proven**). Fix = derive the migration task id-source from the source file (`migrate-<doctype>-<slug(stem)>`, path-aware or mint-suffixed for uniqueness); blast radius is **contained** (source-path/retire/squatter read the task *dir*, not the id string; `{{task.id}}` + the `commit:<id>` slug follow automatically). *Why:* smallest scope that delivers "a real corpus migrated end-to-end"; the source seam + retire are single-file **by construction**, and multi-promotion-in-one-task (built) plus the committed-store ref-resolution make sequential viable. **Edge integrity across a migrated set** rides a **dependency-ordering contract** in the `migrate-adr` guidance (migrate + finalize a `supersedes` *target* before the ADR that supersedes it, so the forward-ref resolves against the committed store), not new transaction code.
- **prd = build repeatable-requirements (no engine code, but NOT a free pack swap), no edge.** Convert the prd `requirements` fixed slot → a **repeatable section** (per-requirement `title` field + `statement` slot, mirroring `spec.criteria` minus the code-anchor); `vision`/`context` stay fixed slots. **No engine code** — `add-item` (M13) + multi-word-heading (M22) cleared the blockers. *Corrected by the design review (B1):* this is **not** "pack-only zero-cost" — `requirements` is authored as a **prose slot** by prd's only shipped driver, the project-setup **Flow-1 greenfield** path (`author-prd.yaml` `<<author: {{task.brief#requirements}}>>` + `flow11_new_project_arc.rs:194`), so M25 also **rewrites that greenfield authoring** onto the per-requirement item path and absorbs the blast radius (`author-prd.yaml`, `flow11`, the prd render golden). The `prd —decomposes-into→ spec` edge stays **deferred** (needs a *new header section* + re-incurs the ref-shape landmine, no migration driver). *Why over fixed-slots (the planner's lean):* a real foreign PRD's requirements deserve individually-addressable structure, and the same shape upgrades the greenfield flow; the edge is the part not earned, so it is cut.
- **Ref handling = build a write-time ref-shape check + widen `adr.supersedes` to `0..*`.** A `ref`-typed value is **shape-blind at write time today** (`write.rs:4174` is the opaque-scalar floor) — a bare slug authors *clean* and dangles at finalize with a misleading "resolves in neither" message. Add a write-time check requiring the `<type>:<slug>` form with the `type` matching the field's declared `to:` (immediate feedback, mirroring M24's write-time-enum rationale — the guidance≠enforcement lesson that cost M3/M24). And **widen `adr.supersedes` from `0..1` to `0..*`** (inverse `superseded-by` likewise): cardinality is **not enforced today** (a bracket-list `[adr:a, adr:b]` already authors *and* validates clean — the `0..1` is a decorative lie), and a real ADR commonly supersedes multiple priors. *Bound:* the comma form (`adr:a, adr:b` unbracketed) is the silent footgun — guidance must specify bracket-list syntax.
- **Acceptance corpus (broad).** Real **MADR/Nygard ADR** corpus is the headline arm — ideally one with **supersession chains** so the edge-wiring + ordering path is genuinely exercised; a **real-but-idiosyncratic spec** (no community standard, so ad hoc — even one real doc proves the best-fit doctype); a **synthesized PRD, labeled as synthetic** in the done-bar (no real foreign PRD corpus exists — the measured-on-real-corpus claim is honestly weaker for prd); plus mining jigc's own docs / the project-delta+project-gamma smoke repos for migratable material. Measured on the M23/M24 facts (round-trip conformance · fidelity-acceptance · content-preservation · agent-call count).

**Recommend-and-proceed (settled, not deferred):** **doc-level date-suppression** is an in-scope fix (thread the migration flag into `on_create_doc_fields`, mirror the item-level deriver — else M25 re-ships the exact false-history bug M24 declared fixed, on the reference's first generalization); the **spec `decided-by→adr` edge stays OUT/deferred** (net-new header section, foreign specs rarely carry parseable decision links, compounds the ref landmine — no driver); the **data-loss clobber guard fires at finalize-promote** (review S1 correction — a non-singleton create does *not* check the committed store at the mint site, so the guard blocks any create-provenance doc whose destination already holds a committed managed doc, **regardless of conformance/migration-ness** — covering the in-location squatter *and* a title-slug collision across the corpus, both off-canonical-bounded for the squatter case).

**Design review (one independent `design-reviewer`, 2026-06-17) — 1 BLOCKING + 4 SHOULD + 4 CONSIDER, all baked or consciously dispositioned.** *B1 (settled with the human):* the prd conversion was **not** pack-only — it breaks the Flow-1 greenfield driver; M25's prd arm now owns that rewrite (above). *S1:* clobber guard moved to finalize-promote (above). *S2:* the write-time ref-shape check fires at **both** `check_value` call sites — `write.malformed-value` at the write path AND `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` at the conformance gate (codes pinned at the build spike); the 0..* widen's re-pin churn (`schema.rs:636`, the adr snapshot, `validate_envelope.rs:457`) is named. *S3:* the ref-shape check **validates the slug body, not just the type prefix**, so the unbracketed comma form (`adr:a, adr:b`) is caught at write — closing the footgun rather than leaving it to a finalize dangle. *S4:* a `supersedes` target **outside the migration set** is dropped to prose (the partial-corpus escape), not authored as a forever-dangling ref. *C1:* the per-file task-id uniqueness pick (path-aware vs mint-suffix loop — two same-stem files in different dirs collide under `mint_task`'s hard-reject) is named as an owed (I)-pick. *C2 (deferred — review-agreed scope creep):* the **mint-before-compose orphan-residue cleanup** is NOT built — the per-file task-id dissolves the namespace-shadow risk and `task discard` already self-corrects (M17 need-driven posture). *C4 (settled with the human):* migrated titles render as the **slug in the H1** (`# use-postgresql`, exercise-confirmed) — **accepted as a pre-existing honest bound** (faithful kebab of the title, not data loss; the title→H1 round-trip fix has wide golden blast radius across every doctype, out of scope) rather than fixed in M25.

**Graduated out of [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md):** the prd repeatable-requirements deferral (now built at M25); the NGT committed-field-update sub-part (a) (closed by copy-on-first-touch — exercise-confirmed: a `set-field` on a committed doc copies-on-first-touch and re-promotes; sub-part (b) `0..*` last-write-wins stays owed). **Confirmed still-deferred:** spec `decided-by→adr` (no driver); the empty-slot+field-group byte-stability bug **does not fire** on adr/spec/prd (exercise-confirmed through both `add-item` and the batch path — spec's slot+field `criteria` item round-trips byte-stable because it has no on-create field to materialize at mint) → stays keyed to **M26**.

**No code-inferred docs / whole-repo inference** (that is M25+/north-star, explicitly out); **arch-doc migration + the empty-slot+field-group fix are M26.** Design home: [design/auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Generalizing to adr/spec/prd (M25); acceptance = worked-examples flow 27. The binary changes (new `migrate-{adr,spec,prd}` workflows + per-doctype author-migration steps, a per-instance migration task-id, a write-time ref-shape check, doc-level date-suppression threading, the `adr.supersedes` 0..* widening + prd repeatable-requirements schema deltas, the squatter clobber-guard + orphan-residue cleanup), so it must be **rebuilt + re-pinned** (both bin dirs) before any live exercise. Decomposition in [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M25.

## 2026-06-17 — M25 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 1 (per-instance migration task-id + the `migrate-adr` workflow — the spine generalizes to the first location-bearing, multi-instance doctype) into **three ordered, single-concern tasks**, against [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Migration model + Per-doctype workflows. **Edge-free** — `supersedes`/`cites-code` are not authored here (inc 2 wires edges). Grounded in the code: the migrate verb, source seam, retire transaction, adopt path, and `doc author --from` batch are all **doctype-parameterized** (the verb passes `doctype` through with **no allowlist** — `cli.rs::run_migrate` → `migrate::run` composes `migrate-<doctype>` directly), and adr promotion to `decisions/<slug>.md` is the proven M1 path — so the only **production** change is the task-id mint (T1); the workflow/step are **pure pack additions** (T2); T3 *exercises* the doctype-general retire/promote/adopt spine on the new non-singleton shape rather than assuming it (reuse-is-a-claim — a hidden changelog-specialness fails T3's red).

**(I)-pick resolved — path-aware, not a mint-suffix loop (the owed C1 pick).** The mint id-source moves from the fixed singleton `migrate-<doctype>` (`crates/cli/src/start.rs:114`) to `migrate-<doctype>-<slug(repo-relative source path, extension stripped, separators folded to `-`)>`. Path-aware (fold the whole rel path, not just the stem) is chosen over a mint-suffix loop because it is a **pure deterministic function of the source path** — distinct files → distinct ids, same file → same id, so re-migrating the same file **collides** into the existing serial-collision finding (resume/discard), the correct semantics; a suffix loop would instead silently mint a *second* task for the same file and additionally needs a `mint_task` change (`mint_task` hard-rejects, never suffixes — `state.rs:421`). Blast radius is contained in production (source-path/retire/squatter read the task *dir*, not the id; `{{task.id}}` + `commit:<id>` slug follow), as the design verified; the changelog migration task-id consequently becomes `migrate-changelog-changelog` (root `CHANGELOG.md`), a mechanical test-const update — the describe workflow-catalog snapshot is **unaffected** (it pins the *workflow* id `migrate-changelog`, which does not change).

Tasks:
- **T1 — per-instance migration task-id (the singleton-blocker fix; production + blast-radius fixup).** Derive the mint id-source path-aware in `mint_migration_in_repo` (`crates/cli/src/start.rs`) via a new pure helper. *Done:* a unit test on the helper — two distinct source paths → distinct ids, the same path → the same id, two same-stem-different-dir files → distinct ids; the existing changelog migration integration suite green after the mechanical `migrate-changelog` → `migrate-changelog-changelog` task-const + `migrate_seam.rs` recorded-id assertion updates (~12 test files). Independently green — changelog still migrates end-to-end at its new id.
- **T2 — the `migrate-adr` workflow + the adr-specific `author-migration` step (pure pack additions).** New `crates/cli/pack/workflows/migrate-adr.yaml` (the `migrate-changelog` shape: `creates-task: true`, `selectable: false`, `allows-create: [{type: adr, as: decision}]`, body = the adr author step + `step:finalize`); new `crates/cli/pack/steps/author-migration-adr.yaml` (the `{{ source }}` seam → a `doc author adr --from - --task {{task.id}}` payload example → Status/Context/Decision/Consequences heading map + foreign-status→3-enum mapping; **edge-free** — supersedes/cites-code dropped to prose, not authored); update the `embedded_pack_lists_the_mvp_steps` golden in `crates/cli/src/pack.rs` (adds `author-migration-adr`). *Done:* a compose-level integration test (model `migrate_workflow.rs`) — `jigc migrate <adr>.md --as adr` composes `migrate-adr`, the `{{ source }}` seam surfaces the foreign ADR verbatim, the composed view carries the adr guidance; the step composes standalone; the pack-list golden passes. (The payload example is a *claim* until T3 exercises `doc author adr --from` — T3 is its verifier.)
- **T3 — end-to-end adr migration acceptance (the deliverable's Proves; red on real input through the built binary).** New `crates/cli/tests/migrate_adr.rs` (model `flow25_migrate_changelog.rs` + `migrate_retire_adopt.rs`). *Done:* `jigc migrate <foreign-adr>.md --as adr` → `doc author adr --from -` (status field + context/decision/consequences slots) → `task finalize --approve` lands **one** commit that (a) writes `decisions/<title-slug>.md` **byte-stable** (`render(instance_from_source(x)) == x`), (b) carries `A decisions/<slug>.md` + `D <foreign>` (foreign original retired/gone), (c) `jigc ingest` reports the managed adr **adopted** (not unmanaged/needs-reconcile); a foreign status outside the 3-enum **mapped** per guidance authors clean, and the **red** — an un-mapped raw foreign status **blocks at the write-time enum check** (`check_value`, `crates/engine/src/write.rs`); a 2nd `jigc migrate <other-adr>.md --as adr` mints a **distinct** task (no serial-collision) and migrates independently; cold spike — migrate into an **empty** `decisions/`. This exercises (not assumes) the doctype-general retire/promote/adopt spine on a **non-singleton** doctype.

**Why this order:** T1 is the singleton-collision substrate a multi-instance corpus needs and is independently green; T2 adds the doctype workflow/step the verb composes; T3 drives the whole adr path end-to-end through the built binary and proves the deliverable — serial, building over the shared working tree. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 1.

## 2026-06-17 — M25 Inc 1 / T3: fix the `migrate-adr` guidance payload skeleton (doc-level `set:` → `- id: status` section)

T3's acceptance surfaced a defect in T2's shipped `author-migration-adr.yaml`: the example `doc author adr --from -` payload placed `status` under a **document-level `set:`** key, which the batch payload parser rejects (`AuthorPayload` is `deny_unknown_fields` over `title` + `sections` only — `crates/cli/src/author.rs`). A faithful agent following the skeleton verbatim would fail at the `doc author` step. **Fix (pack-only):** nest the `status` field under a `- id: status` section (its real schema home — a header section). A new T3 arm extracts the emitted heredoc skeleton from the composed `jigc migrate --as adr` view and parses it through the same `cli::author::parse_author_payload` the verb runs — the red→green guard that catches this masking class (a green spine test hand-building a valid payload while the agent-facing guidance is broken). Guidance/example only; no engine or schema change; `migrate_workflow.rs`'s composed-content assertions are unaffected (it pins the heading map + enum members, not the payload nesting).

## 2026-06-17 — M25 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 2 (edge migration — write-time ref-shape check + `adr.supersedes` `0..*` + ordering/drop guidance) into **three ordered, single-concern tasks** (1:1 with the three Grouped-scope bullets), against [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Edge migration + Write-time ref-shape check + Honest bounds. This exercises the **edge path the changelog reference never touched** (changelog was edge-free). Grounded in the code:

- **The ref-shape check is one production change reaching both call sites for free.** `check_value` (`crates/engine/src/write.rs:4114`) → `check_scalar` routes `FieldType::Ref` through the **opaque-scalar floor** (`:4174`, shared with `String`/`OwnedLocation`) — non-empty + single-line only, **shape-blind**: a bare slug `use-postgres` or comma-form `adr:a, adr:b` authors clean today. Both call sites already wrap `check_value`'s `Err`: `set_field_validated` (`:4316`→`:4331`) → **`write.malformed-value`**; the conformance gate (`crates/engine/src/validate.rs:865` + `:1020`) → **`schema-conformance.field-value-conformant`**. So splitting the `Ref` arm out of the floor into a `check_ref` flows to **both** finding codes with no per-site edit (the M24 enum-check precedent; review S2). The migration batch confirms the "blocks at write" promise: `doc author --from` routes a **Section** field (supersedes lives in the `status` header section) through `apply_field_target` → `set_field_validated` (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs:232`), so a malformed supersedes in the migrate-adr payload blocks as `write.malformed-value`, not a finalize dangle.
- **No stored ref carries a fragment — only the one synthetic unit-test assertion does (verified).** Every shipped/stored ref value is clean `<type>:<slug>` (`supersedes: adr:<slug>`, `cites: [adr:<slug>, …]`); the `#`-bearing forms in the codebase (`adr:single-node-cache#context`) are **read-path placeholder addresses** (`data_value.rs`), never passed through `check_value` (the edge model splits at the first `:` and resolves the slug against a canonical path — a fragment never resolves: `index.rs:403`). The lone fragment-bearing `check_value` input is the **synthetic** assertion `check_value(&r, "adr:auth#criteria/rate-limit").is_ok()` at `write.rs:4780` (a test of the *old* loose floor) — updating it to the tightened expectation is in-scope (the increment owns `write.rs`); no real fixture breaks.
- **No `is_slug` predicate exists** — `slug.rs` ships only `slugify` (idempotent, output `^[a-z0-9-]*$`, no leading/trailing/doubled `-`). T1 adds a validity predicate; `slug.rs` is its natural home.
- **The widen is mechanical, with the four re-pin sites enumerated** (verified): `crates/cli/pack/schemas/adr.yaml` (`card: "0..1"`), the golden assert `crates/engine/src/schema.rs:636`, the **insta** snapshot `engine__schema__tests__schema_adr.snap:35` (regenerate, don't hand-edit), and the embedded-schema text `crates/cli/tests/validate_envelope.rs:457`. The inverse `superseded-by` has **no separate field to edit** (it is a name on `supersedes.inverse`); "likewise" is conceptual. Cardinality is **unenforced** (`ref_min_cardinality_zero`, `validate.rs:1065`, only checks min=0) — a bracket-list already authors + validates clean — so the widen is an **honesty fix**, and the genuinely-new exercise is a **multi-element** supersedes through the resolve gate.

**(A)-assumption to verify, not assert — the `to: None` ref.** No shipped ref has `to: None` (`adr.supersedes`/`arch-doc.cites` both declare `to: adr`), so the design's "type matching the field's declared `to:`" has no live counterexample. T1's red proves the obvious reading: **enforce type-equality only when `to` is declared; always validate the `<type>:<slug>` shape + slug grammar** (a `to: None` ref still requires the typed shape, but skips the equality check). If a build-time finding contradicts this, halt rather than guess.

Tasks:
- **T1 — write-time ref-shape check in the shared `check_value` (the net-new code; reaches both finding codes).** Split `FieldType::Ref` out of the opaque-scalar floor into a `check_ref` (`crates/engine/src/write.rs`): non-empty + single-line, then `<type>:<slug>` where (a) `type == field.to` when `to` is declared, and (b) `<slug>` matches the slug grammar (new validity predicate in `crates/engine/src/slug.rs`); for a list ref, **each element**. Update the now-tightened synthetic assertion at `write.rs:4780`. *Done:* engine unit tests over `check_value`/`set_field_validated` — `use-postgres` (bare slug), `spec:foo` (wrong type for a `to: adr` field), and `adr:a, adr:b` (comma-form → non-slug remainder) **reject**; `adr:use-postgres` and a 2-element list `[adr:a, adr:b]` **accept**; control-char still rejects; the `set_field_validated` reject surfaces `write.malformed-value` **and** a `crates/engine/src/validate.rs` test shows the same malformed `supersedes` fires exactly one blocking `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` at the supersedes leaf — **and** an `arch-doc.cites` valid `[adr:…, adr:…]` list still passes (regression). `cargo test -p jigc-engine` green (no other fixture breaks).
- **T2 — widen `adr.supersedes` `0..1` → `0..*` (the honesty fix + the multi-supersede resolve exercise).** Edit the four re-pin sites above (`adr.yaml` source; regenerate the `schema_adr` insta snapshot; update the `schema.rs:636` golden assert and the `validate_envelope.rs:457` embedded text). *Done:* the `schema_adr` golden + the `validate_envelope` envelope test pass with `card: "0..*"`; a validate/finalize test where an adr with a **2-element** `supersedes: [adr:a, adr:b]` resolves **clean** (zero `ref-resolves` findings) when both targets are committed, and blocks with exactly one `schema-conformance.ref-resolves` when one target dangles — exercising the widened cardinality through the existing resolve gate (the path `0..1` left untested).
- **T3 — adr migration guidance: the dependency-ordering contract + the out-of-set drop (pack-only).** Replace the **EDGE-FREE** block (`crates/cli/pack/steps/author-migration-adr.yaml:45-48`) with the supersedes edge guidance: author an in-set supersession as a **typed bracket-list** `supersedes: "[adr:<slug>, …]"` under the `- id: status` section; the **dependency-ordering contract** — migrate + finalize a supersession *target* before the ADR that supersedes it, so the forward-ref resolves against the committed store (one-file-one-task has no cross-task transaction); the **out-of-set drop** — a `supersedes` whose target will not be migrated is folded into `context`/`consequences` **prose**, never authored as a forever-dangling ref. *Done:* a compose-level test (`crates/cli/tests/migrate_workflow.rs`) asserts the composed `jigc migrate <adr>.md --as adr` view carries the ordering-contract + out-of-set-drop + bracket-list instructions and no longer says EDGE-FREE; the emitted payload skeleton still parses through `cli::author::parse_author_payload` (the inc-1/T3 masking-guard class); the `migrate-adr` workflow composes.

**Why this order:** T1 is the net-new code risk (the shape check both later tasks lean on — T2's 2-element accept and T3's bracket-list both ride the tightened grammar); T2 is the mechanical widen + the multi-supersede resolve exercise; T3 is guidance describing the now-validated, now-widened form — serial, building over the shared working tree. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 2.

## 2026-06-17 — M25 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 3 (doc-level date-suppression — the doc-level twin of M24's item-level dateless-history fix) into **two ordered, single-concern tasks** against [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Doc-level date-suppression and the M25 fork-C recommend-and-proceed ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 2026-06-17 M25 planning). The single Grouped-scope bullet (thread the migration discriminator into `on_create_doc_fields` so a `type: date, set: on-create` **header** field skips the today-stamp in migration mode, both call sites passing the flag) is the **production change of T1**; **T2 is its acceptance** — the deliverable's "Proves" demands a real-binary dateless-adr migration that renders **no date line**, a claim (an absent doc-level on-create date renders + finalizes clean) T2 must *prove*, not assume. Both tasks together deliver the whole bullet (T1 makes the change; T2 proves the deliverable).

Grounded in the code (verified, not analogized): `on_create_doc_fields` (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs:765`) takes **only** `&Schema` today — no migration flag — and unconditionally stamps `today_iso()` on a `type: date, set: on-create` header leaf. The proven item-level mirror already exists: `on_create_block_field(field, today, migration)` (`doc.rs:653`) drops **only** the date stamp under `migration` while a non-date `set: on-create`/`default` leaf (e.g. `status: proposed`) still materializes — the exact predicate-scoped suppression M24 shipped (audit fix `868642b`). The header `fields` iterated by `on_create_doc_fields` are the same `engine::schema::Field` type `on_create_block_field` consumes, so the deriver can delegate to it (executor's choice; the done-criterion is behavioral, not structural). **Exactly two callers** (`run_create:838`, `run_author:889`) plus the unit test — no third caller silently broken (grep-verified across `crates/`). Both callers hold the resolved `ActiveTask`, whose `is_migration()` (`doc.rs:1087`, reads the recorded `source-path` — written only by `jigc migrate`) is the discriminator; the `is_migration()? → DocFailure` `?`-conversion is **already proven in the same module** (`doc.rs:351`, and `run_author` already binds `let migration = task.is_migration()?` at `:914` — T1 reuses that binding, lifting it above `:889`). spec/prd carry **no** `type: date, set: on-create` header field, so the flag is **inert** for them (flag-invariance — unit-covered in T1).

Tasks:
- **T1 — thread the migration flag through `on_create_doc_fields` + both call sites (the whole scope bullet; production + unit).** Add `migration: bool` to `on_create_doc_fields` (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs`); under migration suppress **only** the `type: date, set: on-create` header stamp (defaults like `status: proposed` still materialize — mirror `on_create_block_field`). `run_create` and `run_author` pass `task.is_migration()?` (reuse run_author's `:914` binding). *Done:* a doc.rs unit test (mirroring `on_create_item_fields`'s migration test) — `on_create_doc_fields(&adr, true)` yields exactly `status` (default `proposed`) and **no** `date`; `on_create_doc_fields(&adr, false)` yields `status` **and** `date == today_iso()`; `on_create_doc_fields(&commit, _)` empty under both flags (inert); `on_create_doc_fields(&spec, true) == on_create_doc_fields(&spec, false)` (no date field → flag-invariant, spec/prd unaffected); the existing `on_create_doc_fields_materializes_default_and_on_create` updated to pass `false`. `cargo test -p jigc-cli`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo build` green.
- **T2 — end-to-end dateless adr migration acceptance (the deliverable's Proves; red on real input through the built binary).** A real-binary integration test (extend/model `crates/cli/tests/migrate_adr.rs`): (a) `jigc migrate <dateless-foreign-adr>.md --as adr` → `doc author adr --from -` (payload carries **no** date) → `task finalize --approve` lands the promoted `decisions/<slug>.md` with **no `date:` header line** and **finalizes clean** (the red — proves an absent doc-level on-create date renders + finalizes clean, not assumed); (b) an **explicit** `date:` in the author payload survives verbatim into the promoted doc (overwritable on-create, unchanged); (c) a **non-migration** `jigc doc create adr` still renders today's `date:` line (regression — suppression is migration-gated only). *Done:* the three assertions pass through the built binary; `cargo test -p jigc-cli` green. (spec/prd date-field-invariance is unit-covered in T1, so it is not re-exercised here.)

**Why this order:** T1 is the production threading + its unit floor (independently green); T2 drives the dateless adr migration end-to-end through the built binary and proves the deliverable — serial, building over the shared working tree. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 3.

## 2026-06-17 — M25 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 4 (finalize-promote clobber guard — no silent data loss) into **two ordered, single-concern tasks** against [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Honest bounds (the clobber guard) and the M25 fork recommend-and-proceed ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 2026-06-17 M25 planning). The single Grouped-scope bullet (a finalize-promote guard blocking a **create-provenance** doc whose promote destination already holds a committed managed doc — regardless of conformance or migration-ness) is the **production change of T1**; **T2 is its acceptance** — the deliverable's "Proves" demands a real-binary triad (title-slug collision blocks, in-location squatter blocks, first-time migration unaffected) that T2 must *prove*, not assume. Both tasks together deliver the whole bullet (T1 makes + unit-floors the guard; T2 proves the deliverable through the built binary).

Grounded in the code (verified, not analogized):
- **The mint site genuinely can't catch this — finalize-promote is the right seam (confirmed).** `engine::state::create` (`crates/engine/src/state.rs:646`) step 3 (`:674`) checks only the **working area** (`path.exists()` under `task_dir`); step 4's committed copy-in (`:691`) is `&& schema.singleton`-gated, so a **non-singleton** create (adr/spec/prd) **never reads the committed store** and provisions blank → a 2nd same-slug ADR, and an in-location squatter at the canonical path, both mint clean and would clobber `<location>/<slug>.md` at promote. So the guard must fire at finalize-promote, exactly as the design corrected (review S1).
- **Provenance is the regression hinge, and it already exists.** Every staged doc carries `Created` vs `EditedFromBase` in the `docs/provenance.json` manifest (`ProvenanceRecord`, `crates/engine/src/state.rs:181`, keyed by the `<type>:<slug>` address): `provision_doc` → `Created` (a fresh non-singleton create, and the blank-seeded squatter), `copy_in` → `EditedFromBase` (copy-on-first-touch of a committed doc). The guard **must gate on `Created`** so the NGT committed-field-update path (an `EditedFromBase` doc legitimately re-promoting over its own committed canonical file) does **not** block — that is the load-bearing regression-safety distinction. `Provenance::record` is write-once-sticky (`:200`), so a created-then-edited doc stays `Created`.
- **The committed-store check needs `repo_root`, which `plan_finalize` does not take today — that is T1's blast radius.** `plan_finalize` (`crates/engine/src/finalize.rs:169`) takes `task_dir`/`schemas` but no `repo_root`; the promotion's `destination` is repo-relative (`<location>/<slug>.md`, `plan_promotions:507`). The guard checks `repo_root.join(&destination).is_file()` (a present canonical file == committed-at-base, since phase-1 pins `base.sha == head_sha`). Threading `repo_root` into `plan_finalize` is a **mechanical signature update across its ~12 in-crate test call sites + the `validate.rs:3122` test + the one production caller `task.rs:561`** (which already holds `self.repo_root`, used at `:614`). Scoped to `plan_finalize` — the milestone sibling `plan_milestone_finalize` is **left untouched** (its by-task-id join owns the created-vs-created clash rule; widening the guard there is out of scope and unneeded by the deliverable).
- **The guard is migration-agnostic by construction, which is correct, not creep.** It fires for **any** `Created` promotion to a committed destination, so it covers the title-slug collision, the in-location squatter (where `plan_retirements:274` already skips the source==destination retire, leaving the promote to clobber), **and** the non-migration `doc create` clobber together — exactly the design's "regardless of conformance or migration-ness; this single promote-time block covers the squatter, the title collision, and the non-migration clobber together" ([auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Honest bounds).

**(A)-assumption to verify, not assert — the disk-presence predicate == "committed managed doc".** The guard reads `repo_root.join(destination).is_file()` as the committed-store check; phase-1's `base.sha == head_sha` pin means a file present at a canonical destination at plan time was committed at base (promote has not run). T1's unit reds prove this reading (a committed destination + `Created` blocks; an absent destination does not). If a build-time finding shows a stray untracked file at a canonical path defeats the predicate, the executor may pin git-tracking instead — but do not pre-build that; the bounded acceptance corpus is committed fixtures.

**Suggested finding code:** `finalize.promote-clobber` (the `finalize.promote-io` / `finalize.migration-no-replacement` / `finalize.source-path-io` family) — **pinned at the build spike**, named in both tasks' done-criteria.

Tasks:
- **T1 — the engine finalize-promote clobber guard (the whole scope bullet; production + signature blast radius + unit floor).** In `plan_finalize` (`crates/engine/src/finalize.rs`): thread `repo_root: &Path` through the signature, and after `plan_promotions` add a guard that loads the task's `ProvenanceRecord` and, for each promotion whose recovered `<type>:<slug>` address has `Provenance::Created` **and** whose `repo_root.join(&destination)` is an existing committed file, returns a blocking `finalize.promote-clobber` finding (code pinned at build). Mechanically pass `repo_root` at every call site (`task.rs:561` → `self.repo_root`; the ~12 finalize.rs test calls; the `validate.rs:3122` test). *Done:* engine unit tests over `plan_finalize` — (a) a `Created`-provenance staged doc whose canonical destination already holds a committed file **blocks** with exactly one `finalize.promote-clobber`; (b) an `EditedFromBase` staged doc whose destination already holds a committed file does **not** block (the copy-on-first-touch / NGT committed-field-update regression — the load-bearing safety case); (c) a `Created` doc to an **absent** destination does **not** block (the first-time-migration regression). `cargo test -p jigc-engine`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo build` green after the mechanical `repo_root` threading.
- **T2 — end-to-end clobber-guard acceptance (the deliverable's Proves; red on real input through the built binary).** A real-binary integration test (model `crates/cli/tests/migrate_adr.rs`): (a) **title-slug collision** — with `decisions/<slug>.md` already committed from a prior migration, a 2nd `jigc migrate <off-canonical-other-adr>.md --as adr` whose title slugs to the same `<slug>` → `doc author adr --from -` → `task finalize --approve` **blocks** with `finalize.promote-clobber`, commits **nothing**, leaves the committed ADR **byte-intact**, and does **not** retire the 2nd foreign original; (b) **in-location squatter** — `jigc migrate decisions/<slug>.md --as adr` where that canonical path holds a committed managed doc **blocks at finalize-promote**, the squatter **intact** (the retire-skip + the new promote-block compose to no data loss); (c) **regression** — a normal first-time `jigc migrate <foreign>.md --as adr` into a non-colliding/empty `decisions/` **promotes + retires + adopts clean** (`jigc ingest` reports adopted). *Done:* the three assertions pass through the built binary; `cargo test -p jigc-cli` green. **Bound (recorded, not charged):** the squatter case proves only the *block* — end-to-end authoring over an in-location squatter stays off-canonical-foreign-path-bounded (the M24 blank-seed is singleton-gated, out of M25; [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Honest bounds).

**Why this order:** T1 is the net-new guard + its signature blast radius + the unit floor that pins the `Created`-vs-`EditedFromBase` regression-safety distinction (independently green); T2 drives the collision/squatter/regression triad end-to-end through the built binary and proves the deliverable — serial, building over the shared working tree. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 4.

## 2026-06-17 — M25 Inc 4 / T1: the clobber guard's in-place exclusion is SINGLETON-gated (elaboration the planner note under-specified)

The naive guard (`Provenance::Created` + `repo_root.join(destination).is_file()` → block) **regresses M24's flow 26** (`crates/cli/tests/flow26_marquee.rs::flow26_red_in_location_squatter_seeds_blank_and_authors_via_batch`, verified empirically: it emits `finalize.promote-clobber` and fails): the M24 **singleton** in-location squatter (`changelog/changelog.md`) is blank-seeded → `Created`, the foreign original is **committed** at the canonical destination (so `is_file` is true), and `source-path == destination` — exactly the case M24 made author **in place**. So `plan_clobber_guard` excludes the in-place rewrite (`source-path == destination`, both `lexical_normalize`d, matching the retire guard's discriminator) **but only when the doctype is `singleton`** — because the M24 blank-seed/in-place-authoring path is itself `state.rs` step-4 `&& schema.singleton`-gated ([auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Honest bounds: non-singleton in-location squatters are "bounded to off-canonical foreign paths"). A **non-singleton** in-location squatter (adr/spec/prd, `source-path == destination`) therefore still **blocks** — the retire-skip + this promote-block compose to no data loss, which is exactly T2(b)'s intent. The guard threads `schemas` to resolve each promotion's `<type>` for the singleton check. Unit-floored both sides: `finalize_plan_allows_the_in_place_singleton_rewrite` (changelog, no block) + `finalize_plan_blocks_a_non_singleton_in_location_squatter` (adr, blocks). Cross-ref: [finalize.rs](crates/engine/src/finalize.rs) `plan_clobber_guard`.

Grounded in the code (verified, not analogized):

(Renamed from `…_three_author_slots`.)
- **The batch `doc author --from` path is doctype-general + shipped; project-setup supplies prd's create-gate (no migrate-prd needed here — that is inc 6).** `jigc doc author prd --from -` runs through `state::create_gated` over the active task's gate; `project-setup` is `allows-create: [{type: prd, as: brief}]`, so T4 mints a project-setup task and authors the multi-requirement prd over it (the same gate flow11 uses for `doc create prd`). Tasks:
- **T1 — prd `requirements` → repeatable section + byte-stable round-trip (schema bullet + the prd render golden; Proves P1).** Edit `crates/cli/pack/schemas/prd.yaml`: `requirements` slot → `repeatable: { id-from: title, block: [{id: title, type: string}, {id: statement, slot: {hint: …}}] }` (mirror `spec.criteria` minus `maps-to-test`); `vision`/`context` stay fixed slots; **correct the stale header comment** (drop the "FIXED PROSE SLOTS / single-word-only / add-item wall" reasoning — now obsolete). Rewrite the doc.rs round-trip unit to author `requirements` as repeatable items. *Done:* a doc.rs unit test — the prd schema loads; an `Instance` with vision/context section slots + ≥2 `requirements` `ItemContent` (title field + statement slot) renders → writes canonical `prds/<slug>.md` → `store::read_slice` resolves each requirement's `#requirements/<id>/statement` **byte-for-byte**; **cold/empty spike** — requirements minted with **zero** items renders + reparses byte-stable, then one added item reparses byte-stable (no on-create field at mint, no empty-slot+field-group drift). `cargo test -p jigc-cli`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build` green (no other golden breaks).

Re-grep `develop-idea.yaml` for a `#requirements` slot directive; touch only if present (expected: no change). Update + rename the form-D test. *Done:* `crates/cli/tests/start_compose.rs` form-D test green — the composed `jigc start --workflow project-setup <idea>` view emits the `Run: jigc doc create prd` create-gate, **exactly two** `<<author: …>>` slot lines (vision/context), and the per-requirement `add-item`/`set-slot …#requirements/…` guidance lines; gate green.

- **T4 — multi-requirement prd via `doc author --from` (`items:`) round-trips (Proves P3, red on real input through the built binary).** A new integration test (model `crates/cli/tests/migrate_adr.rs`'s batch usage): mint a `project-setup` task (the prd create-gate), pipe a declarative payload to `jigc doc author prd --from - --task <id>` with vision/context section slots + a `requirements` section carrying ≥2 `items` (each `title` + `statement: "<<…>>"`), then assert the authored `prds/<slug>.md` **round-trips byte-stable** (`render(parse(on_disk)) == on_disk`) and each requirement statement re-reads verbatim. *Done:* the multi-requirement batch-authored prd round-trips byte-stable through the built binary; `cargo test -p jigc-cli` green.

**Why this order:** T1 ships the schema substrate (independently green, byte-stability proven on the new shape) every later task builds on; T2 rewrites the greenfield driver + its compose floor; T3 drives the greenfield arc end-to-end through the binary (Proves P2); T4 proves the doctype-general batch `items:` path on the new shape (Proves P3, the path inc-6 `migrate-prd` will lean on) — serial, building over the shared working tree. ## 2026-06-17 — M25 Increment 5 RE-SEQUENCED: T1–T3 collapse into one atomic gate-green task (build halt, corrected)

The Inc-5 build **halted at T1**, correctly: T1's scope (`prd.yaml` + `doc.rs`) flips `prd.requirements` slot → repeatable, which **immediately breaks `flow11_new_project_arc.rs`** (`set-slot prd:habit-tracker#requirements` — a slot that no longer exists) **and** the `start_compose.rs` form-D test — both T2/T3's named deliverables. So **no green full-gate commit boundary exists for T1 in isolation**: "green full gate before commit" collides with "do only T1." This is a **decomposition gap, not an engine gap** — the build-planner split a change the locked design ([auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → prd, "not a free pack swap") had already declared **one inseparable change** (schema flip + author-prd.yaml + flow11 + the prd render golden land together). **Fix (re-sequence):** **collapse T1+T2+T3 into ONE task** — the prd schema flip + the `doc.rs` round-trip/cold-spike + the `author-prd.yaml` greenfield rewrite + the `start_compose.rs` form-D update + the `flow11` end-to-end rewrite, all in one commit with a green full gate. **T4 stays separate** (the multi-requirement `doc author --from` round-trip is additive test coverage — it does not break the gate on its own). The original T1–T4 task *content* is unchanged; only the **commit grouping** is corrected. Driven to completion via `build-executor`(s) outside the workflow, then the build resumes `skipThrough: 5`. Tree was clean at the halt (T1's reverted work fully recoverable). Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 5.

Landed the re-sequenced atomic task in one commit, full gate green. `prd.requirements` is now a **repeatable section** (`id-from: title`; block `title:string` + `statement:slot`) mirroring `spec.criteria` minus the code-anchor; `vision`/`context` stay fixed slots; stale single-word/add-item-wall header comment corrected. `author-prd.yaml` greenfield driver rewritten onto the per-requirement `add-item`/`set-slot …#requirements/<id>/statement` path (modeling `author-arch-doc.yaml`); `develop-idea.yaml` needed **no** change (re-grep confirmed: references "requirements" in prose only, no slot directive). **Verification-mechanism pin (T1 spec correction):** the doc.rs round-trip asserts each requirement's `#requirements/<id>/statement` re-reads byte-for-byte by **re-parsing the committed bytes with `engine::parse::parse_sections` + comparing `item.slot.slice(source)`** — *not* via `store::read_slice`, which only slices single-hop `#unit` fragments and rejects `#unit/item/leaf` with `store.unsliceable-fragment` (the T1 decomposition's "read_slice resolves #requirements/<id>/statement" mechanism does not exist at this scope; the byte-for-byte contract is the re-parse, identical to `item_authoring_acceptance.rs`). T4 (`doc author --from` multi-requirement round-trip) remains the separate follow-on. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 25 Increment 5.

## 2026-06-18 — M26 planning: arch-doc migration + the (now-due) byte-stability fix

The migration arc's last doctype. Baseline-verified by 3 `capability-auditor`s + 4 `gap-detector`s **exercising** the re-pinned binary (sha `856f84fab4cc`), which sharpened three handover assumptions and settled four human forks.

**Exercise corrected three carried claims:**
- **The migration spine + dispatch is pure pack-config.** `migrate --as <doctype>` resolves by string interpolation (`migration_workflow(d) = "migrate-{d}"`) with **no Rust enumeration** of doctypes; the arch-doc schema shipped at M13. So the migration arm = **two yaml files** (`workflows/migrate-arch-doc.yaml` + `steps/author-migration-arch-doc.yaml`), **zero engine/CLI/schema change**. All four gap-detectors converged on this independently.
- **The byte-stability bug *does* fire through the migration batch — the "parse-once/render-once" justification was factually wrong.** `doc author --from` flattens to leaves applied **per-leaf over one buffer** (`author.rs`): an `AddItem` leaf mints `slot:None` (`\n\n`), the next `SetField` leaf re-parses → `slot:Some("")` → renders `\n\n\n\n`. The unstable form is produced. **But the conclusion stands:** `required-slot-present` blocks the unfilled-`description` component from ever committing, and the `\n\n\n\n` form is a *stable fixed point* (doesn't grow). So the fix is a **#1-risk robustness paydown decoupled from migration working**, not a migration unblocker — correcting the roadmap/decisions-pending mechanism note. (`ensure_single_trailing_newline` additionally masks the trailing-item case; the only two engine fixtures pinning the three-blank form are changelog nested change-groups.)
- **doc↔code on a *migrated* doc is genuinely unexercised, and `doc-code` is Rust-only with a silent non-Rust pass.** No prior migration authored a *resolving* code anchor (adr deferred `cites-code`; spec authored zero `maps-to-test`). A present non-`.rs` file with a vanished symbol **finalizes clean** (probe returns `None` for non-Rust) — so a foreign arch-doc over non-Rust code makes every `implemented-by` anchor vacuous. The `doc-code` sibling binary **is** found beside the installed `jigc` from a non-jigc repo (M20 embed-extract — load-bearing risk retired).

**Four human-gated forks settled (all the recommended path):**
- **C1 · Acceptance corpus = HYBRID** — a **real** foreign arch-doc (file-only anchors accepted, non-Rust OK) **plus** a **synthesized-over-jigc's-own-Rust** arch-doc (the M13 flow-16 shape, driven through migration) so resolving anchors are genuinely exercised. The real arm carries the in-the-wild fidelity claim; the synthetic arm carries the code-checked claim. (Driven *toward* synthetic-over-Rust because `doc-code` is Rust-only — a real foreign doc rarely satisfies arch-prose + Rust code + a citable ADR set at once.)
- **C2 · Code-anchor done-bar = MANDATE** — the synthetic-Rust arm **must** migrate ≥2 components with real, independently-resolving `implemented-by` anchors **and** prove the **blocking red** (delete component A's symbol → finalize blocks on `arch-doc:<slug>#components/<a-id>/implemented-by` while B stays valid — the flow-16 bar reached *through migration*). Inheriting M25's optional-anchor/drop posture would leave doc↔code-on-migrated permanently unexercised (no later milestone owns it) and hollow the milestone.
- **C3 · Write-time code-anchor shape check = NOT BUILT (finalize-only, bound recorded).** M25 added a write-time *ref*-shape check because migration manufactures refs from prose; the same argument applies to `implemented-by` (manufactured `path#symbol`), but the corpus is controlled (jigc's own Rust) + guidance says omit-unless-a-concrete-symbol, so the M13-deferred item-leaf adjudication-parity gap stays finalize-only. Carried bound: a malformed anchor dangles at finalize-`doc-code` rather than rejecting at write; a non-`.rs` anchor silently passes.
- **C4 · The byte-stability fix = Increment 1, isolated, NON-GATING.** Re-justified as a #1-risk paydown (not a migration unblocker); direction **B** (canonicalize an empty present-slot `Some("")` to render identically to an absent slot `None` in `render_item_at` — `slot_empty = slot.as_deref().is_none_or(|s| s.trim().is_empty())`); blast radius = 1-line predicate + 2 engine fixture rewrites (both changelog nested change-group literals — review-verified: 503 pass / exactly those 2 fail) + ~8 stale item-path comments (re-grep `write.rs`, not the pinned "4") + a parsing.md home; acceptance = an engine `render(parse(x))==x` test on a minted-empty slot+field item, **independent of** the migration acceptance. **Not re-keyed a fifth time** (M22→M24→M25→M26 ends here).

**Dispositions recorded (not forks):** slug-as-H1 → keep bounding (consistent with M25) but finally **key it** in `decisions-pending.md` (it's the same title→H1 fix across all four `id-from: title` doctypes, wide golden blast radius — its own post-M26 concern); `adr.cites-code` migration → stays **out**, recorded as an unowned deferral with trigger; `arch-doc` create-or-update-via-bind → confirmed **out** (migration creates fresh from a foreign file, never re-opens a committed doc via a bound read-role); the required `description` slot → **stays required** (the guidance synthesizes a one-line responsibility per component; making it optional would unmask the byte-shape as a *persistent promotable* doc). **No schema/field-type/engine change for the migration itself.** Design home: [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → arch-doc migration (M26); the byte fix → [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → Round-trip guarantees.

**Decomposition — three increments, risk-first + linear** ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 26): **(1)** the isolated byte-stability fix (engine, non-gating — direction B + 2 fixture rewrites + ~8 comment corrections; red = an engine `render(parse(x))==x` on a minted-empty arch-doc component); **(2)** the migration arm (`migrate-arch-doc.yaml` + `author-migration-arch-doc.yaml`, pack-only — the six guidance obligations; red = a smoke migration round-trips + the dangling-cites / unfilled-description / vanished-symbol reds fire); **(3)** the measured hybrid acceptance + rebuild/re-pin (flow 28 — real-foreign arm file-only + synthetic-Rust arm with ≥2 resolving anchors + the blocking red over a committed adr; the four facts recorded under `completions/artifacts/M26/`). Survived the pre-decompose review (0 BLOCKING + 2 SHOULD + 5 CONSIDER, all baked: the `overview` required-slot synthesis, the committed-adr precondition for the cites mandate, the fixture-symbol-for-the-red, the ~8-not-4 comment count, the Inc-2-gate wording, the M25-rationale sharpening, the pre-existing greenfield multi-cite defect recorded).

## 2026-06-18 — post-M26 shakedown: DX fixes before the first real-project test

Before pointing jigc at a real project, a `general-purpose` agent drove the **installed** binary (production path — embedded pack, sibling `doc-code` probe, no env overrides) through the full loop in throwaway repos: setup → greenfield single-task + in-task ADR → multi-cite arch-doc → changelog + ADR migration (reject + approve) → ingest. **Verdict: ready-with-caveats — no run-breakers**, but real first-session friction. The human chose to fix the actionable findings now (no milestone — these are understood UX/polish, not design-uncertain). Fixed, each via the dev-workflow, gated, binary re-pinned:

- **Greenfield arch-doc multi-cite data loss** (`5c209b8`): the `author-arch-doc` step instructed one `set-field #cites` per ADR, but `set_field_validated` **replaces** — so a multi-ADR arch-doc kept only the last. Now one bracketed `[adr:a, adr:b]` (the form migration already used). Found at the M26 completion review.
- **The first-task finalize wall** (`348022f`): the `single-task` guidance staged only `commit:#summary`, but finalize blocked on empty `type`/`scope`/`body`. Made `scope`/`body` **optional** (closing the logged latent defect — M22's optional-field capability, never applied to `commit`; an optional present-but-empty field is now exempt from `field-value-conformant`, not just `required-field-present`), and wired `set-commit-type` into the commit-authoring steps so the required `type` is guided.
- **slug-as-H1** (`f06ec5e`): created/migrated `id-from: title` docs rendered the kebab slug as the H1 (`# use-mysql`). Now the **original title** renders in the H1 while the **id stays the slug** (addressing/filename unchanged). The "wide golden blast radius" that deferred it three times was **overstated** — only 2 assertions flipped. **Graduated out of decisions-pending.**
- **migrate --help stale** (`bea8c92`), **finalize success output** (`9cf1eb0` — reports the landed commit + promoted docs), **`jigc task list` + enumerated ambiguous-task error** (`1bb3eb8`), **setup self-commits its install** (`26eacff` — so it stops landing in the first feature commit), **reject empty/punctuation intent** (`68acc62` — no more fallback-named `commit` task), **copy/guidance nits** (`d0a10c2` — the `<<…>>` markers flagged as required-not-placeholder, the SessionStart hook named, store-validate wording).

Gate green throughout (113 test binaries). Binary re-pinned both dirs (`jigc` sha `4943a63`). **Carried, NOT fixed (a real feature, not a quick fix):** `doc-code` is **Rust-only** — on a non-Rust project, `implemented-by`/`cites-code`/`maps-to-test` anchors silently degrade to file-existence-only (a vanished symbol on a present non-`.rs` file finalizes clean). Multi-language probes are a future milestone; until then, the "validate against reality" advantage holds only on Rust targets. Remaining minor backlog tracked in-thread (none block a real test).

## 2026-06-18 — M26 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 26 Increment 1 (empty-slot+field-group byte-stability fix — engine, isolated, non-gating) into **one atomic, gate-green task** against [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → Round-trip guarantees → Empty-slot canonical form and [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 2026-06-18 fork C4. **Grounded in HEAD (verified, not assumed):** the predicate to change is `crates/engine/src/write.rs:232` (`let slotless = item.slot.is_none() && item.slots.is_empty();`); the arch-doc `components` item carries **both** a `description` slot and an `implemented-by` field (`crates/cli/pack/schemas/arch-doc.yaml:34-35`) and a test-module `arch_doc_schema()` helper already loads it (`write.rs:5833`); the two fixtures hold the three-blank empty-change-group literal that flips (`write.rs:6562` `cold_fill_one_nested_leaf_at_a_time_is_byte_stable` / `write.rs:7014` `top_level_field_write_after_nested_child_lands_in_parent_region`); the stale `\n\n\n`/`\n\n\n\n` empty-item comments live at `write.rs` ~231/900/1136/2200-2223/2504/2523/2658/4055-4058; the parsing.md home is **already authored** (`implementation/parsing.md:131`) so it is **not** a task; engine write tests are green at baseline (79 pass).

**Why one task (gate-atomicity, not under-cutting):** the four Grouped-scope deliverables form a single inseparable gate-green unit — the 1-line predicate change *breaks* the two existing fixtures (they pin the old three-blank form; only the fixture rewrites repair them), it is *proven* by the new `render(parse(x))==x` red test (which is green-on-arrival, i.e. has no real red step, if it lands after the predicate is already in), and the ~8 stale comments are *falsified* by the same change. None of the four reaches a green full gate as a standalone task with a real red step, so splitting would manufacture a broken-gate boundary — they are one commit.

- **T1 — canonicalize empty present-slot to the one-blank slotless form + prove byte-stability** (all four Grouped-scope bullets). In `render_item_at` (`crates/engine/src/write.rs:232`) replace the slotless predicate with direction B: `let slot_empty = item.slot.as_deref().is_none_or(|s| s.trim().is_empty()); let slotless = slot_empty && item.slots.is_empty();` — so a reparsed empty present-slot (`Some("")`) renders identically to a freshly-minted absent slot (`None`). Add a new engine test that mints an **arch-doc component** with an empty `description` slot + a filled `implemented-by` field and asserts `render(parse(x)) == x` (RED before the predicate change: minted one-blank vs reparsed three-blank diverge), **and** a masking-guard assertion that a genuinely-slotless changelog release (`slot: None`, no slot leaf) stays byte-identical (the fix moves only `Some("")` items). Rewrite the two named fixtures from the three-blank to the one-blank empty-change-group form. Re-grep `write.rs` for the `\n\n\n`/`\n\n\n\n` empty-item-form comments (~8: lines ~231/900/1136/2200-2223/2504/2523/2658/4055-4058) and correct each to the one-blank form. *Done:* the new test passes (named, e.g. `write::…::minted_empty_slot_field_group_item_is_byte_stable`), the two rewritten fixtures pass, `cargo test -p engine` green, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` clean. *Executor note (red obligation, not a trust):* the C4 pin "exactly these 2 fixtures flip (503 pass)" is review-verified but re-confirm by exercise — after the predicate change, the only engine failures must be the new red (now green) plus exactly these two fixtures; if a third fixture flips, rewrite it the same way (still in-scope: the canonicalization is the single cause) and record it. Built against [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → Round-trip guarantees → Empty-slot canonical form; DECISIONS fork C4.

**Scope coverage:** all four Grouped-scope bullets land in T1 (predicate / 2 fixtures / ~8 comments / + the proving test); the parsing.md home is pre-authored, not a task. **No new fork surfaced** — the deliverable, direction B, blast radius, and acceptance are fully settled in fork C4 and the locked parsing.md Round-trip-guarantees home; nothing here is unresolved from the locked docs. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 26 Increment 1.

the byte-stability substrate is Inc 1, shipped `62e6ded`). **Grounded in HEAD (verified, not assumed):** the migrate verb derives the workflow generically with **no doctype allowlist** — `crates/cli/src/migrate.rs:62` `migration_workflow(d) = format!("migrate-{d}")` — so `migrate --as arch-doc` resolves the moment the file exists (the test's "no longer errors `no workflow`" is the proof, not a trust); the arch-doc schema is migration-ready as shipped (`crates/cli/pack/schemas/arch-doc.yaml` — `meta.cites` ref `0..*` to adr, `overview` slot, repeatable `components` with `title`/`description` slot/`implemented-by` code-anchor; ids are the fixed single words `meta`/`overview`/`components`); the **only workflow-enumerating golden** is `crates/cli/tests/snapshots/describe__describe_byte_snapshot_is_necessary_but_insufficient.snap` (one line, lists `migrate-adr`/`migrate-changelog`/`migrate-prd`/`migrate-spec` — `migrate-arch-doc` sorts between `migrate-adr` and `migrate-changelog`), to be re-accepted; the acceptance combines `migrate_spec.rs` (the migrate→author→finalize spine over `JIGC_PACK_DIR` = the on-disk `pack/` tree) with `flow16_acceptance.rs` (the `doc-code` probe built once + selected via `JIGC_DOC_CODE_PROBE`, real `git init` temp repo, per-item disambiguation of the blocking red).

## 2026-06-18 — docs-root: nest managed docs under a single parent (default `docs/`)

Post-shakedown footprint cleanup. The dev pack's five persisted-doctype dirs (`decisions/`/`specs/`/`prds/`/`architecture/`/`changelog/`) landed at repo root — pollution that deters adopters. Settled with the human: nest them under one parent via a new pack-default cascade knob **`docs-root`** (string, default `docs/`), prepended to each persisted doctype's `location:` → `docs/decisions/`, etc. Per-project overridable (`jigc config set docs-root <path>`; `.` restores flat — and the config-set path canonicalizes an empty `""` to `.` so `docs-root ""` does the intuitive thing rather than hitting the opaque-scalar floor's non-empty rule, which exists for document field bullets, not knobs). Doctype id, addressing (`adr:foo`), and stable-id invariants unchanged — only the on-disk path gains the prefix. `docs/` chosen as the conventional home for project docs (override if you already use `docs/` for a site-generator).

Implementation — **one shared hygiene helper** (`crate::start::apply_docs_root`: trims the root, preserves the location's trailing slash so `file_state`'s `{location}{slug}.md` key stays intact, empty/`.`→flat, transient location-less schemas untouched) applied at **every** schema-load surface, plus the `committed_store` store-key fixed to key by the **final** path segment (`specs`, not `docs/specs`) so `{{store.<name>}}` still resolves. **Surface count corrected 3→5 during the build** (the Plan named three; patching only three is the read/write split-brain the consistency requirement warns against): (1) `CascadeDefs::all_schemas` (compose/describe/committed-store), (2) `ingest::load_schemas` (`ingest`/`unmanage`), (3) `TaskArea::schemas` (finalize-promote write path), **(4) `doc.rs::ActiveTask::schema()/schemas()`** (the warm copy-in `canonical_path` read — found via a failing changelog cold→warm test: copy-in read flat while finalize wrote `docs/`), **(5) `milestone.rs::shipped_schemas`** (the join committed-index rebuild + add-from-spec read). All five resolve the same parent so read and write paths always agree.

**`docs-root` is an opt-in knob** (deviation from the Plan's literal `unwrap_or("docs/")` fallback): the helper falls back to **flat** (`""`) when the resolved cascade does not carry `docs-root`, so it nests only where the key is actually declared. The dev pack declares it (default `docs/`) → dev-pack projects nest. The **methodology pack** ships its own `knobs.yaml` that deliberately omits `docs-root` and its owner-artifact home is the **flat engine constant** `completions/artifacts/` — forcing `docs/` on it (the literal `unwrap_or("docs/")`) would diverge the completion-record location from that constant and silently break owner-artifact drift detection. So standalone-methodology stays flat; composed `[dev ▸ methodology]` nests (the dev pack's `docs-root` is in the resolved cascade). The dev pack's default still lands in `base_scalars`, so every dev-pack resolution returns `docs/`.

Test sweep: ~40 integration test files re-pinned (dev-pack docs → `docs/...`; methodology standalone stays flat); two `migrate_{spec,arch-doc}` foreign sources relocated to flat `specs/`/`architecture/` (now off-canonical, since the canonical home moved into `docs/`); engine bare-schema unit tests + the 2 schema snapshots unchanged (they bypass the cascade); `file-state.json` record keys change (`decisions/foo.md` → `docs/decisions/foo.md`) — moot pre-release. Design home: [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Repository layout / Config layout.

## 2026-06-19 — finalize dirty-tree sweep: B1 (surface a pre-commit manifest + `--dry-run`)

**B1** chosen for `jigc task finalize`'s `git add --all` sweep: a landed finalize emits a **pre-commit manifest** (the commit file-set tagged promoted / modified / deleted, with an **untracked sweep flagged distinctly** so a stray `scratch.txt` is noticed), and a new `--dry-run` flag prints that manifest and stops — committing nothing, no destructive side effect, no `--approve` on a migration. B1 *surfaces* the set; it does not prevent inclusion. **Option A** (a declared task change-manifest that refuses out-of-set files) is deferred. Design home: [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → Dirty-tree policy.

## 2026-06-19 — methodology `re-verify` step: de-Rust the gate (prose-align with `gate.yaml`, no knob)

The trigger for the deferred "portable-gate-knob" fired — a real **PHP + TypeScript + Vite** project will compose the methodology pack, so `re-verify.yaml`'s hardcoded `fmt · clippy -D warnings · test · build` would name the wrong toolchain. Resolved **not** with a cascade knob but by **prose alignment**: the pack already established gate-portability in `gate.yaml` ("run the project's own gate; do not assume a particular toolchain"), and `re-verify.yaml` was the lone step out of step with it. The gate is agent-run (test/lint/build), never CLI-owned, so no determinism is at stake — a knob would be premature generality. `re-verify.yaml` now reads "the project's full gate green (its own format, lint, test, and build gate, whatever toolchain it uses)". It is the only Rust-hardcoded prose in the pack (used solely by `completion.yaml`).

## 2026-06-19 — M27 planning: doc-code multi-language (generalize the code-anchor probe Rust→6 languages)

Plan-the-milestone Settle. **What M27 proves:** the "validate docs against reality" advantage stops being Rust-only — a `code-anchor` (`implemented-by`/`cites-code`) on a `path#symbol` in a TypeScript/JavaScript/Python/PHP/bash file genuinely resolves at finalize (blocks on a vanished symbol, passes when present), closing the **non-Rust silent-pass** (`#symbol` on a non-`.rs` file used to emit *no finding*). **Scope:** purely **probe-internal** — the baseline auditors verified the pack schema, the three code-anchor doctypes, the engine, and the wire contract are all language-blind, so M27 needs **zero** pack/engine/CLI change; all logic lands in `crates/cli/probes/doc-code/` and its grammar deps stay out of the engine/cli lock graph (detached-workspace invariant).

**The reframe (gap-detector spike, not analogy):** the baseline's "symbol-exists is field-driven, so it ports for free" claim is **REFUTED**. A spike against the real grammars (tree-sitter 0.26.9) showed the new grammars expose a `name` field on *non-declaration* nodes (bash `command`, TS `import_specifier`/`variable_declarator`, PHP `simple_parameter`, Python imports), so M10's any-`name`-node walk **false-PASSES a called-but-undefined symbol** — the exact rot the probe exists to catch. So the resolution model itself changes from field-driven to a **per-language node-kind allowlist** (the real deliverable, a fourth seam beyond the three dispatch points).

**Forks settled** (all recommended options; design home [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Multi-language resolution): **(F1) symbol policy** = all declarations at any nesting, visibility/export ignored (mirrors Rust), via a per-language node-kind allowlist. **(F2) unsupported extensions** = a non-blocking `doc-code.unsupported-language` advisory (never silent-pass), a **distinct check-id** (isolated from `symbol-exists` tuning) but **un-keyed/informational** — *refinement of the cost quoted at the fork:* no inventory row, no `knobs.yaml` key, no golden re-pin (the inventory stays 27); a keyed `unsupported-language.severity` is earnable later if a project needs to enforce checkability. **(F3) bash** = `.sh`/`.bash` extensions + **shebang-sniff** for extensionless scripts (pure file-bytes read, determinism intact); functions-only (`function_definition`), non-function bash symbols stay unverified. **(F4) `criterion-maps-to-test` on non-Rust** = the `symbol-exists` floor **blocks on a vanished symbol** (consistent with `implemented-by`) + the `unsupported-language` advisory that the is-a-test half is unverified; the `#[test]` predicate itself stays Rust-only (no portable cross-language test signature). **(F7) acceptance done-bar** = the blocking-red mandated on **two** languages (TypeScript + Python — the most structurally distinct grammars) on a real polyglot repo, measured on the installed binary (mirror flow 13/16 on a non-Rust target → new worked-examples flow). **Build details settled, not forks:** the extension→grammar dispatch table (incl. `.tsx`→**TSX**, a distinct grammar — plain TS errors on JSX); grammar set + versions verified to compile against the probe's pinned tree-sitter 0.26.9 (`-typescript 0.23.2`, `-javascript 0.25.0`, `-python 0.25.0`, `-php 0.24.2`, `-bash 0.25.1`); the probe's re-declared `Severity` enum gains an `Advisory` variant (engine already accepts it — no engine change); tighten the 150 MB `cargo_install` size guard to a release-realistic ceiling so future grammar bloat trips it.

**Graduated:** the M17-frictions **doc-code non-Rust silent-pass** ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md):82) — M27 is its trigger firing. **New deferrals recorded (with triggers):** CSS + docker-compose code-anchor resolution (their addressable units — selectors, service keys — aren't `path#symbol` AST named items; need a distinct semantics; trigger = a real arch-doc/spec cites a CSS selector or compose service); the non-Rust **is-a-test predicate** port (trigger = a non-Rust pack ships a `maps-to-test` field). **Confirmed NOT firing** (recorded so they aren't silently assumed): the cross-pack probe/field-type collision ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md):78 — M27 ships no second probe/pack), the A==A-oracle lint (:18 — no test-source target), the `cites-code` migration deferral (orthogonal — about authoring a resolving anchor during migration, not which languages resolve). **Stale record to fix in Inc 1** (M27 edits this very file): root `Cargo.toml` `exclude` points at the non-existent `crates/cli/pack/probes/doc-code` (real path `crates/cli/probes/doc-code`; harmless no-op today — detachment is via the probe's own empty `[workspace]` table — but a trap).

**Survived independent design review** (the reviewer spiked all five grammars at their pinned versions). The allowlist *model* held; five table corrections baked back before decompose: TS `abstract_class_declaration` added (else an abstract class false-blocks); PHP `interface`/`trait`/`enum` declarations added (else they false-block); and the two **value-position** kinds **tightened** to a declaration position — `variable_declarator` resolves only at module/export/top-level (not a function-local `let`), `method_definition` only as a class-body member (not an object-literal method) — else the over-match the model exists to close re-opens. The non-Rust `criterion-maps-to-test` emission was pinned to a truth table (symbol absent → one blocking finding, no advisory; symbol present → one advisory, symbol passes — never co-fire), and extension-wins-over-shebang precedence stated. All in [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Multi-language resolution.

A **fresh spike of all four grammars against the probe's pinned `tree-sitter 0.26.9`** (`-javascript 0.25.0`, `-python 0.25.0`, `-php 0.24.2`, `-bash 0.25.1` — all compile) dumped the real ASTs and verified every allowlist node-kind + the over-match negatives: **JS** — `function_declaration`/`class_declaration`, `method_definition` (parent `class_body` for a class method, `object` for an object-literal method), `variable_declarator` (parent-chain `lexical_declaration`→`statement_block` for a function-local `let`, →`program`/`export_statement` for top-level) — **identical node-kinds + value-position semantics to TS**, so JS **reuses `is_ts_citable` verbatim** (the TS-only kinds `interface_declaration`/`type_alias_declaration`/`enum_declaration`/`abstract_class_declaration` simply never appear in a JS AST); JSX parses **natively under `tree_sitter_javascript::LANGUAGE`** (`has_error=false` — *no* separate JSX grammar, unlike TS/TSX), so `.js`/`.jsx`/`.mjs`/`.cjs` all map to one `Grammar::JavaScript`. **Python** — `function_definition`/`class_definition`, a nested `def` sits under a `block` and resolves at any nesting; an `import` is an `import_statement` carrying a `name` field (the over-match the allowlist must exclude). **PHP** (`LANGUAGE_PHP`) — `function_definition`, `class_declaration` (an abstract class is the **same kind** with an `abstract_modifier` child), `method_declaration`, `interface_declaration`, `trait_declaration`, `enum_declaration` — all six confirmed (the review's interface/trait/enum false-block fix). **bash** — both `function f { }` and `f() { }` parse to `function_definition`; a bare call is a `command` node carrying `name=` (the over-match — functions-only), and a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang-led script parses cleanly under `tree_sitter_bash::LANGUAGE` (`has_error=false`). **Why four tasks, not one or two:** each grammar is a genuinely-independent allowlist + dispatch arm with its own red obligation in *Proves* and its own hostile-input fixture — four parallel concerns, not one; and bash's shebang-sniff is inseparable from bash (bash is the *only* grammar a `#!…sh` shebang resolves to), so it rides with bash as one gate-green unit. The four grammar deps land **distributed** — each task adds its own dep, inseparable from its allowlist compiling — and all four deliver the *Grouped scope* "add the four deps" bullet. **The shebang reshape:** `grammar_for(&Path)` cannot sniff a shebang (it has only the path); T4 widens the dispatch so that when the extension yields no grammar the caller reads the file's **first line** and maps `#!…sh`→bash (extension always wins; pure file-bytes read, no wall-clock/network — determinism intact).
