## 2026-06-21 — M31 Inc 5 fork settled (human): restore the user's hooks on squash:true, WIP-safe, folded into Inc 5

The M31 build **halted at Inc-5 planning** on a genuine settled-decision conflict the planning pass didn't foresee (the hook question was framed only around squash:false relay, fork B2). Inc-4's squash:true combine commits via off-line `git commit-tree` (review S2's WIP-safe build) which runs **no** `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` hook — violating `finalize.md`'s hard contract (`:69`/`:171`: "the CLI never passes `--no-verify`; the user's hooks are policy and the CLI respects them"). squash:true is the **default** knob, so the bypass is on the common path; the basis the Inc-4 executor accepted it on ("no hook in any squash:true test") was **proven false** (`milestone_finalize_relays_only_the_aggregate_hook_output` installs a pre-commit hook on squash:true). The two settled decisions — S2's off-line WIP-safe combine vs. the never-bypass-hooks contract — cannot both hold with `git commit-tree`. The build correctly halted rather than override either.

**Settled (human, 2026-06-21):**
- **MECHANISM = restore the hooks, WIP-safe** (over accepting the carve-out). Run the user's `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` hooks against the combined tree **without touching the main checkout** — reuse M31's worktree machinery (commit the combined tree from / run hooks in a clean dedicated context — e.g. a dedicated worktree where `git commit -F` runs the hooks against the would-be-committed tree — then fast-forward main). This honors **both** finalize.md's hook contract **and** S2's WIP-safety; the conflict is dissolvable (not irreducible) precisely because M31 already builds worktree machinery. The exact shape (dedicated-worktree `git commit` vs. running the hook scripts around the off-line tree) is settled at Inc-5 re-plan. *Rejected — the carve-out (keep commit-tree, accept no hooks on the aggregate, document it):* silently drops the user's hooks on the **default** commit path, a retreat from the contract Inc-1 *just revised the docs to tell the truth about*; the M30 index-validated `doc-code` gate (at validate) is only a **partial** mitigation (covers doc-code, not arbitrary user hooks — formatters, policy checks).
- **SCOPE = fold into Inc 5** (over a separate increment). Both squash:true and squash:false now build through the same Inc-4 combine, so resolving hooks once for both is one coherent motion and makes Inc-5's in-scope `finalize.md:104` fold-back tell **one** honest hook story. Inc 5 grows; the roadmap Inc-5 scope is widened accordingly.
- **squash:false stays independently plannable** (unchanged by this): live-apply each worktree's staged patch (collision-block across the whole fan-out up front, reusing `combine.rs`'s block-set) + `git commit -F` per sub-task (hooks run + relay via the existing `git_commit`/`relay_hook_output`), reset-on-abort; the merged docs ride the parent aggregate. Whatever squash:true mechanism is chosen must be **consistent** with this so finalize.md tells one truth.

The retargeted `milestone_finalize_relays_only_the_aggregate_hook_output` (squash:true currently asserts `HOOK_WARNING == 0` with the marker "Inc 5 restores hook execution") flips back to asserting the hook **fires** on the squash:true aggregate. *Tree clean at halt (HEAD `ea0244e`, Inc-4 landed); this is a plan-phase fork, no code fix needed — record + widen roadmap Inc-5 + resume.*

`combine_commit` (`task.rs`) no longer commits via the hook-less `git commit-tree` + `git reset --hard`. The off-line combined tree is still built in a throwaway index (unchanged), then committed via a new `commit_combined_tree_with_hooks`: a `DedicatedWorktree` (a detached `git worktree add` under the gitignored `.jigc/worktrees/.combine-<pid>-<nanos>`, removed on drop) is set to the combined tree with `git read-tree --reset -u <tree>` (HEAD stays at the parent, so the commit's parent = main HEAD and its tree = the combined tree), then the **shared** `git_commit` (`git commit -F`, **never** `--no-verify`) commits it there — so the repo's shared `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` hooks run against the combined tree (a linked worktree shares `.git`, hooks included). The captured hook stream is returned (not `String::new()`) so the existing success-relay surfaces it. Main is fast-forwarded (`git reset --hard <commit>`) **only after** the hook-running commit lands, so a hook rejection lands nothing and unrelated main-checkout WIP survives (review S2 preserved). `git_commit_tree` removed (dead). The squash:true half of `milestone_finalize_relays_only_the_aggregate_hook_output` flips to asserting the non-blocking hook fires exactly once + relays in the `--- hook output ---` section; flow33 (clean tree / order-invariance / WIP-survives-a-blocked-combine) stays green. The `squash: false` milestone boundary now lays one commit per sub-task carrying **that** sub-task's worktree code. `commit_per_subtask_messages`/`commit_empty_message` (the tree-empty `git commit --allow-empty` form) are replaced: `commit_per_subtask_code` (`milestone.rs`) reads each provisioned worktree's staged patch (`git diff --cached --binary`, id order) and, for each worktree that staged code, applies it onto the **main checkout** (`git apply --index`, via the new `crate::task::commit_subtask_code`) then `git commit -F` its rendered `commit:<sub-id>` doc through the shared `git_commit` — so the user's hooks run on **every** per-sub-task commit and each commit's non-blocking hook output is relayed. **Elaboration:** a worktree with **nothing staged** contributes **no** per-sub-task commit (no `--allow-empty` substitute) — the commit sequence is a pure function of the *code-carrying* sub-task id set; the merged docs ride the parent aggregate (review B1/B2), which now stages over the clean index the per-sub-task commits left via `StagePolicy::IndexHonoring` (the **`Sweep` variant + its match arm are removed** — dead once its sole construction site moved; the M2-I2-T2 clippy lesson). A cross-worktree code collision **blocks up front** before any commit via `combine::detect_code_collision` (the rename-aware `block_set`/`collision_finding` factored out of `combine_worktree_trees`, which now delegates to it). Reset-on-abort: `git_reset_hard` to the captured pre-finalize HEAD undoes the per-sub-task commits on any per-sub-task or aggregate failure (all-or-nothing). The squash:false tests are reworked to provision worktrees + stage disjoint code (`setup_squash_false`), assert each per-sub-task commit's `git show --name-only` carries its files (not an empty tree) + the merged docs land in the aggregate (not partitioned), the relay test (renamed `milestone_finalize_relays_every_fan_out_commit_hook_output`) flips to N+1 relays, and a net-new same-file-collision-blocks test is added. squash:true (T1) untouched. ## 2026-06-21 — Direction: methodology forcing-functions authored pack-shaped; live-repo self-hosting deferred behind external proof

A working-direction call (human, 2026-06-21), from the M31 retrospective. The laziness/prose-accretion class we keep hand-patching in the methodology docs (`milestone-planning-workflow.md`, `increment-workflow.md`, the agent prompts) **is the class jigc exists to solve**: a required *slot* in a managed doc cannot be skimmed-past the way a prose paragraph can; a composed *step* always appears. The "make it a forcing function, not prose" lever *is* the determinism boundary. So:

- **New methodology forcing-functions are authored *pack-shaped* from now on** — framed as the *slot / step / presence-validation* the methodology pack will encode, even while they still live as markdown. This makes the markdown a **spec for the pack**, so the eventual encode is transcription, not redesign — closing the drift between the docs we hand-maintain and the pack the self-hosting arc will encode. (First instance: D, the consolidated plan-time gate-record, designed pack-shaped in [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The planning gate-record.)
- **Honoring the A-3 honesty bound** ([methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → What M16 does not prove): the pack-shape is **presence-conformance, never content-scoring**. jigc enforces that the gate-record slot is *filled* (required-slot-present); it never reads/grades the judgment (the #5 owner-artifact "presence, not content" precedent). A composed step that emits a `gap-count ≥ N` lint or auto-checks a checklist would *hollow* the judgment — barred. The checkpoints halt; they never score; the agent authors the judgment into the slot.
- **The honest boundary on what folds:** the working *docs* fold (the M16 doctypes) and the workflow *content* folds (steps/slots/checkpoints/fan-out); the *orchestration* does **not** (the bounded fix-loop, the multi-agent planning fan-out, the 3-round cap stay the `milestone-build` harness's job — no DAGs/runtime, by invariant) and *judgment* stays human (jigc asserts the census is present + the review ran, never that they were good).
- **The live-repo migration stays deferred** behind external proof + human testing — exactly the existing self-hosting sequencing ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M16 "jigc's own docs migrate at v1" + M17 external pilots/A-B/measurement). We do **not** put our own critical-path process docs on the tooling until it is earned elsewhere. Recorded so new methodology edits are pack-shaped *now* without triggering a premature self-host.

*Trigger for the encode:* the self-hosting planning-workflow encode / v1 migration (keyed in [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)).

## 2026-06-21 — M32 planning: decouple commit-doc provisioning from `selectable` (settled)

Resolves the M31-completion finding (graduated from [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → M32). Baseline verified **by exercise** (3 capability-auditors + 4 gap-detectors, all at HEAD `92acbc5`):

- **Audit verdict — 1 broken / 10 false-positive.** Eleven workflows are `creates-task: true, selectable: false` and match the gate `!def.creates_task || !def.selectable` in `provision_on_first_entry` (`crates/cli/src/start.rs:335`). Only **`sub-task`** is genuinely broken (exit 1, *"no staged instance — provision it first"* on a real `jigc workflow sub-task --task <id>` re-entry) — it is the **sole fan-out `run:` target** and the **only** workflow whose commit doc is provisioned *exclusively* on the re-entry path (minted by `milestone execute`, never by `compose_core`'s mint arm). The 5 `migrate-*` ride a separate provisioner (`provision_migration_commit_doc`); the 4 methodology + `record-change` are fresh-started via `compose_core`'s mint arm (gates on `creates_task` alone). All 10 verified fine — false-positive matches of the *flag*, never traversing the buggy *function*. Recorded so the "11 matched the predicate" alarm doesn't re-fire blind at a future audit.
- **Root cause = gate-divergence.** The `|| !def.selectable` clause is a byte-identical **transplant** of the router-catalog filter predicate (`selectable_workflows`, `start.rs:1326`) into a provisioning guard where only the `creates_task` half belonged. Added by **`7e5393a`** (2026-06-05) under a commit message entirely about the router catalog — never mentions `provision_on_first_entry`, and left the function's docstring still reading *"Gated on `creates_task`."* No decision-record couples provisioning to `selectable`; the over-reach is confirmed incidental. The decouple *honors* `7e5393a`'s actual rationale (router-catalog exclusion) and M16's authoring-spine rationale ([methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) — `creates-task: true, selectable: false` mints a task *to author managed docs*, which the bug directly contradicts).
- **Fix = robust shared predicate, not the one-line flip (human fork, settled).** Both the mint arm (`compose_core:843`) and `provision_on_first_entry` consult one `should_provision_commit_doc(def) -> bool { def.creates_task }`, so the provisioning property has **one source of truth** and the catalog predicate can't be re-transplanted into it. *Why over the cheaper flip:* the defect *is* the divergence (two hand-synced predicates); a one-liner restores correctness today but leaves the re-diverge vector — a fragility the code has *now* (shipped undetected 16 days), so consolidating is solving the real problem, not premature generality (PRINCIPLES → Keep it minimal = smallest *robust* solution). The `path.exists()` write-once guard (`start.rs:340`) makes the now-reachable re-entry provisioning safe for the 6 mint-provisioned siblings (re-entry finds the doc present → no-op; no clobber of a filled `migrate-*` commit).
- **`selectable`'s contract is now written down** ([workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md) → On-disk definition format + the router section): a boolean (default `true`) governing **router-catalog membership only**, orthogonal to minting/provisioning — *"coupling `selectable` into a minting or provisioning gate is a bug, not a symmetry."* Closes the regression vector (the field was undocumented in the front-matter spec and the router section conflated `selectable ≡ creates-task`).
- **Acceptance (full prevention scope, human fork).** The genuine path no test has ever covered: `milestone execute` → real `jigc workflow sub-task --task <sub>` re-entry → `set-field`/`set-slot` on **`commit:<sub>`** → finalize, in **both** squash modes (the existing flow10 drives genuine re-entry but authors only the ADR, finalizes squash:true, and never asserts the commit doc — green *despite* the bug). Plus a sibling-census regression (a re-entered filled `migrate-*` commit survives byte-untouched) + a resume guard, and the in-code comment corrections (`start.rs:317-328` docstring, `workflow_reentry.rs:204-207`). Decomposition in [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 32.

## 2026-06-21 — Differentiator pilot study 1: executed; value gate NOT cleared (jigc ≈ plain/GSD < static)

The reversible value-gate pilot ([ideas/differentiator-pilot.md](ideas/differentiator-pilot.md)) **ran end-to-end**. A 4-arm × 2-model × 2-task matrix (16 cells + a 4-cell follow-up) on isolated container twins of `gherrink-ui-doc @ 542b3206`, doc↔code engaged, blind-judged. Full artifact: [completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/](completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/) (VERDICT · LESSONS · RUNBOOK · pre-registration · results · 20 raw cells).

- **Verdict — jigc did not beat a static `CLAUDE.md`; if anything the static arm won.** Clean-rate (no doc↔code drift shipped): **static-methodology 4/4 · plain 2/4 · GSD 2/4 (dormant) · jigc 2/4**. jigc tied the unguided baselines and lost to the static-methodology file. Not a clean refutation (one small task, n=1/cell), but the gate is **unproven, leaning negative** — extends M17's *tie* into a *loss*.
- **Three diagnosed jigc failure modes (not a broken mechanism — the detection works + the seeded instrument check passed):** (1) **adapter bypass** — the weaker model (Sonnet) used zero jigc verbs and shipped drift like plain (Opus engaged it; so discoverable, bypass was a choice — the *enforced-not-sandboxed* risk made real); (2) **prose blind spot** — jigc's anchor check polices `implemented-by` symbols, not `###` titles/prose, so the only Opus drift in the matrix was jigc's own doc title; (3) **friction on bypass** — a *correct* out-of-band rename still trips `file-state.hash-matches`, so jigc would block-and-demand-rework of right answers.
- **The dilution confound was tested (arm E) and did NOT materialize.** Hypothesis: static won only because its `CLAUDE.md` was a 42-line single-rule file; a realistic many-rule file would dilute the rule. Arm E embedded the *same* rule verbatim in a 157-line file (1 of 14 sections, ~23%) → **4/4 clean, same as the focused file.** Moderate dilution didn't degrade single-task adherence — which *strengthens* the negative read. Untested: heavy dilution (~5%) and the **long-horizon many-edit** regime — now jigc's only live structural case.
- **Pivots from the locked plan (all settled mid-execution, recorded in the pre-registration):** task → **public-API symbol rename** not the `@hideCode` string rename (verification: `symbol-exists` matches *declarations*, never string-literal values, and every transformer exports the same `tag` symbol — the original task could not fire jigc; user-approved); managed doctype → the **shipped `arch-doc`** not a bespoke pack (the binary loads doctypes only from its embedded pack — the project layer *shadows*, never *adds*; pinned binary unmodified); **4 arms** incl. a static-methodology control (user); **both model tiers** (user); **GSD installed clean** via `npx @opengsd/gsd-core --claude --portable-hooks` (user); cross-model judge (Codex) **quota-blocked** → same-family blind judge corroborated the objective grep cell-for-cell.
- **Implication for productive-go:** unchanged operationally — do **not** commit a productive corpus or self-host — but the *reason* is now "value unproven/leaning-negative," not just "not yet measured." Path to clearing (or honestly closing) the gate: the **long-horizon many-edit study**, plus two fixable product weaknesses — make the warn-only git pre-commit hook **blocking** (kills the bypass), and **close the doc prose blind spot**. See [LESSONS.md](completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/LESSONS.md) §5.

## 2026-06-22 — Pilot follow-on: the bypass fix works (jigc→parity via always-on catch); next, route proactively not just catch

Folded Study-1's #1 learning back into the jigc arm and re-ran it ([completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/ADDENDUM-jigc-enforced.md](completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/ADDENDUM-jigc-enforced.md)).

- **The bypass fix is cheap and it works.** An **always-on `Stop` hook** running jigc's own `jigc validate` (blocks finishing while a managed-doc anchor dangles, feeds the finding back) took the jigc arm **2/4 → 4/4 — parity with the static arm** — recovering both original drifts (the Sonnet bypass and the Opus prose-title). No binary rebuild; only the *activation point* changed (finalize-gated → always-on), which is how the warn-only pre-commit backstop should behave.
- **Honest caveats:** **parity, not superiority** (matches static, doesn't beat it — beating it still needs the long-horizon many-edit regime); it's a **hybrid** (`jigc validate` mechanically catches only the *anchor*; the README/title breadth rode on the hook's instruction text — the probe's prose blind spot is unchanged); **ceremony cost rose** (re-prompt loops). A grep false-positive (an old filename in a *valid* anchor path — class renamed, file not) was caught and corrected; the original 16-cell verdict is unaffected.
- **Direction settled this exchange (human): catch *and* route, not catch alone.** Keep the catch as the mechanical guarantee, but also **tweak the adapter bootstrap/instruction so the agent engages jigc up front** — reduce reliance on after-the-fact catching and cut ceremony. **Guardrail:** jigc's thesis is *enforce-don't-instruct*; a "please use jigc" instruction must not collapse jigc into *instruction-to-use-jigc + enforcement* (the static arm already wins by instruction on short tasks). The routing tweak buys **adoption/ergonomics**, not the thesis — the differentiating value is enforcement that doesn't degrade, so the **decisive proof stays the long-horizon test**.
- **Product takeaways (3):** (1) make doc↔code enforcement **always-on**, not finalize-gated; (2) **broaden the probe beyond anchors** (titles/prose) so mechanical coverage matches the instruction's breadth; (3) **sharpen proactive routing** in the bootstrap. Next experiment: **arm A″** — proactive bootstrap + the catch, measuring engagement-rate and ceremony, then the long-horizon study for superiority.

## 2026-06-22 — Correction: the jigc "parity" recovery is confounded by variance; proactive routing didn't help

Ran arm **A″** (proactive `.jigc/AGENT.md` bootstrap + the always-on catch, with the catch instrumented to log) and it forces a **correction to the previous entry's "fix works → 4/4 parity" reading** ([ADDENDUM](completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/ADDENDUM-jigc-enforced.md) → Follow-on).

- **Proactive routing did NOT raise engagement.** Sonnet used **0 jigc-verbs** in both A″ cells (bypassed despite the sharpened instruction); total verbs fell (A′ 5 → A″ 3) and Sonnet's turns ballooned (46 vs 17–20). The instruction bought ceremony, not routing — softer instruction doesn't move the weaker model.
- **The catch fired only once** across A″ (logged). Most "clean" cells logged `ALLOW`-only — no drift at stop, so the hook never engaged.
- **The 2/4 → 4/4 "recovery" is largely run-to-run variance at n=1.** task1-sonnet across the three runs: orig **drift**, A′ **clean**, A″ **clean** — all three with **0 jigc-verbs** (A″ with 0 catches). The clean cells were the agent doing a complete rename on its own that run, not jigc. **The mechanism is sound (it works deterministically when it fires — seeds/linchpin/A″-task2-opus confirm), but it rarely fired, so the recovery is not safely attributable to it.** Read A′ "parity" as "clean in one run set," not "the catch closed the gap."
- **Methodological lesson (the real next step):** n=1/cell can't separate mechanism from noise — **replicate** (5–10 runs/cell) to measure base drift-rate by arm and the catch's marginal contribution, rather than adding more single-shot arms. And since proactive *instruction* failed to route the weaker model, the design lean is toward **harder routing** (a gate that can't be skipped) over softer instruction — consistent with the *enforce-don't-instruct* thesis.

## 2026-06-22 — Replication (n=16/arm) settles it: jigc's benefit is its bootstrap-as-instruction, not its mechanism; static instruction wins

Ran the replication the A′/A″ variance problem demanded — 4 arms × Sonnet × 2 tasks × 8 reps = 64 independent runs ([REPLICATION.md](completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/REPLICATION.md)). Drift = old class name in README or arch-doc title/prose. This **supersedes the n=1 readings** (plain "2/4", jigc "parity") which were variance.

- **Drift-rates (robust):** plain **88%** · static **0%** · jigc (bootstrap, bypassable) **19%** · jigc-gate (bootstrap + always-on catch) **0%**.
- **Base rate: unguided agents drift 88%** — doc↔code drift is the norm without help. Any doc-aware instruction largely fixes it; the **direct static rule is best (0%)**.
- **The decisive number: 0/32 tool engagement.** The agent ran a jigc command in *zero* of the 32 jigc/jigc-gate runs — it read the `AGENT.md` bootstrap and edited files directly every time, yet drift fell 88%→19%. So **jigc's measured benefit is its bootstrap *prose* (an instruction), not its tooling or its gate** — and a purpose-built static instruction beats it (0% vs 19%) far more simply. This is the *collapse-to-instruction* risk, confirmed.
- **The mechanism never activated:** the gate fired **0/16** (the bootstrap already prevented drift-to-stop), so jigc-gate 0% vs jigc 19% is within noise — the gate is *sound but un-triggered*, its value confined to a tail this regime didn't produce. "Enforce-don't-instruct" is **moot when there's no enforcement, only instruction**.
- **Direction sharpened:** for jigc's enforcement to ever differentiate, routing must be **forced, not instructed** (managed files un-editable directly, or an unconditional commit gate) — the proactive bootstrap (A″) did not move Sonnet to engage. And the tail where the gate matters is the **long-horizon many-edit regime** (instruction degrades, residual drift rises into the gate's territory). Single small tasks generate no such tail. These two — *forced routing* and the *long-horizon study* — are the only paths left to a genuine value-gate clear; absent them, a maintained static instruction is the honest recommendation.

## 2026-06-22 — Diagnosed *why* Sonnet bypasses jigc: not awareness — retrieval-under-execution + consequence-modeling gaps

Three direct context probes ([WHY-SONNET-BYPASSES.md](completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/WHY-SONNET-BYPASSES.md)) answer the "does Sonnet even read the instruction?" question: **it does — verbatim.**

- **Probe 1 (no task):** Sonnet quotes `.jigc/AGENT.md` word-for-word; the bootstrap loads (CLAUDE.md→@AGENT.md) and the SessionStart hook fires for both models headless. **Not an awareness gap.**
- **Probe 2 (plan the rename):** both *intend* jigc, but **Sonnet picks `quick-fix`** ("a rename has no architectural ambiguity") — the workflow that *skips* managed docs — while **Opus rejects quick-fix** ("affects the public API surface, which the commits show is documented") and plans to update the arch-doc. That is Opus "recognizing the value": consequence-modeling.
- **Probe 3 (bare task, full transcript):** jigc enters Sonnet's reasoning **0 times** — it goes grep→Read→Write, never consulting the instruction it holds. Knowing–doing gap.
- **Root cause:** two compounding *capability* gaps, not awareness — (1) retrieval-under-execution (Sonnet doesn't surface the held instruction under task pressure), (2) consequence-modeling (mis-judges a rename as doc-irrelevant). The A″ proactive bootstrap already showed a stronger instruction doesn't fix (1).
- **Implication (sharpens the thesis):** instruction is *provably insufficient* for the weaker model → **enforce-don't-instruct is necessary, not stylistic.** The robust fix is the workflow-agnostic always-on **gate** (validate doc↔code at finish regardless of engagement), which covers both Sonnet failure modes (full bypass + quick-fix mis-selection). Its replication 0/16 fire was variance over the ~19% tail; measuring its value needs scale or the long-horizon regime. A `UserPromptSubmit` just-in-time nudge may aid retrieval but is still instruction (ergonomics, not guarantee).

## 2026-06-22 — UserPromptSubmit nudge: fixes Sonnet's retrieval, but it's instruction again (quick-fix finalize doesn't validate doc↔code)

Tested the just-in-time nudge arm ([NUDGE-ARM.md](completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/NUDGE-ARM.md)) — a `UserPromptSubmit` hook injecting "run `jigc start` first" at task time, targeting Sonnet's retrieval gap.

- **Drift (n=16, Sonnet): nudge 0%** (vs jigc 19%, plain 88%, static 0%). The nudge fixed the *outcome*.
- **Retrieval fixed:** stream-json (n=6) shows Sonnet now engages jigc (6/6 run `jigc start`) — the just-in-time injection surfaces jigc where the static `AGENT.md` didn't.
- **But it's instruction, not mechanism.** Sonnet picks **`quick-fix` 6/6** (the consequence-modeling gap at scale), and **`quick-fix` finalize does NOT validate doc↔code** — adversarial test: a dangling arch-doc anchor finalized **clean** under quick-fix, no `doc-code` block. So jigc's validation **never fired** in any nudge run; the 0% drift came from the nudge's doc-consistency clause + manual doc edits. Same pattern as every arm: the differentiator stayed dark, an instruction did the work.
- **Architectural insight (the durable takeaway):** jigc's doc↔code gate is **workflow-scoped**, and the weaker model reliably picks the one workflow that omits it. Enforcement that depends on the agent choosing the right workflow is defeated by the agent's choice. **Only a workflow-agnostic always-on check** (Stop-hook gate / blocking pre-commit / finalize that always runs store-wide `validate`) catches drift regardless of workflow — that is the concrete, fixable form "enforce-don't-instruct" must take.
- **Harness honesty:** two one-off diagnostic runners were buggy (backtick command-substitution in the container `bash -c`; a stream-json sample missing `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` → jigc permission-blocked); both caught by reading transcripts and re-run. The n=16 drift result used the correct `run-rep.sh` and is unaffected.

## 2026-06-22 — Pilot meta-lesson: doc↔code validation belongs as a universal finalize floor; workflows need behavioral (not just structural) testing

Prompted by "is the problem that Sonnet picks the wrong workflow?" The pilot's diagnosis is deeper: **the workflow taxonomy axis ("is there a decision to record?") is orthogonal to the safety axis ("does this touch documented code?").** `quick-fix` = "no decision" — and a rename genuinely *has* no decision, so Sonnet's pick is *reasonable given the description*. The bug is `quick-fix` conflating "no decision" with "no validation," so it omits the doc↔code check a documented-symbol rename needs. Three responses, ranked:

- **Rework workflow descriptions — weak lever, hygiene only.** Descriptions *are* instructions; the pilot showed the weaker model doesn't reliably apply instructions under task pressure (retrieval gap) or model consequences (the quick-fix pick). Sharper descriptions help Opus/humans (already fine), won't fix Sonnet. Do it, but not as the safety mechanism.
- **Bake validation in as a UNIVERSAL FINALIZE FLOOR — the robust fix (recommended).** Every workflow, `quick-fix` included, runs the store-wide doc↔code anchor check at its commit boundary. Treat doc↔code consistency as a **repo invariant, not a per-workflow feature** (like a syntax gate — no opting out by picking a lighter workflow). Then workflow-misselection can't bypass it. This is the "workflow-agnostic always-on check" (from [NUDGE-ARM.md](completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/NUDGE-ARM.md)) applied at the finalize layer; pair with the adapter backstops (blocking pre-commit / Stop-gate) for the total-bypass path.
- **Behaviorally test the workflows — a real, unaddressed gap.** Workflows are validated for *structure* (deterministic composition, golden tests) but never for *agent behavior*: does a real agent select / engage / complete the right one? The pilot is effectively the first behavioral test of the workflow layer and it failed all three (mis-selection, 0/16 bare-task engagement, fumbled completion). Standing practice going forward: every workflow gets an **agent-in-the-loop behavioral eval** — "the CLI composes it correctly" ≠ "an agent uses it correctly." The pilot container harness is the seed of that eval.

Net: the value-gate path (forced/workflow-agnostic enforcement + the long-horizon study) and the workflow-floor fix are the same idea at different layers — enforcement must not be opt-out-able by the agent's workflow choice.

## 2026-06-22 — Phase 0: the quick-fix doc↔code hole reproduced host-side (no Docker); names the Phase-2 fix

Drove the exact Sonnet path against the installed binary in a throwaway repo: a `quick-fix` `jigc task finalize` commits **clean** despite a dangling committed arch-doc anchor, while store-wide `jigc validate` **catches** it. Root cause confirmed at the code level: `finalize` runs `validate_task` (task-scope), and `schedule_doc_code` enumerates **the task's own** effective-state anchors — a quick-fix task carries only a `commit` doc (no anchor), so doc-code is skipped; the dangling anchor lives in the *committed store*, which only `jigc validate` (store-scope) enumerates. So `finalize` is structurally blind to drift a task *causes* in a doc it doesn't *touch* — and the drift persists until some unrelated future task happens to re-validate that doc. The fix this licenses (Phase 2): **`finalize` must run a store doc↔code sweep scoped to the code the task changed — blocking — under every workflow.** Recorded in `completions/artifacts/differentiator-pilot-study1/PHASE0-FLOOR-DEMO.md`.

## 2026-06-22 — Phase 1 (hygiene, value ≈ 0 for the weaker model): sharpen quick-fix's selection hint toward the safety axis

Sharpened `quick-fix`'s `when` (the catalog selection line) from "apply a small commit-only fix with no decision to record" to "…that **touches no documented code** and records no decision," and its `usage` to redirect documented-symbol renames to `single-task`. This makes the *taxonomy* hint at the *safety* axis the pilot found orthogonal. **Explicitly hygiene, not the fix:** the replication proved description changes are an instruction lever, and the weaker model (Sonnet) doesn't reliably apply instructions under task pressure (measured value ≈ 0); this helps Opus/humans only. The robust fix is the Phase-2 universal finalize floor — which makes the safety axis *enforced*, not *selected*. Gated by `cargo test`/`fmt`/`clippy`; touched `quick-fix.yaml` + the six pinned `when`-string test occurrences + the `describe` insta snapshot.

## 2026-06-22 — Phase 2 (design): the universal finalize floor = the doc→doc blast-radius invariant, completed on the code-anchor axis

Settled via the design-workflow (discuss → converge). **The reframe that resolved it:** this is *not* a new gate and *not* a determinism-boundary change — `validation.md` already mandates a per-task blast radius ("if a task removes a ref target, the now-dangling referrers it didn't directly edit are flagged too, so a task can't commit breakage elsewhere"), enforced today for **doc→doc** refs via the edge index. The quick-fix hole is that this invariant has never covered **doc→code** anchors (code isn't an edge-index node), so a task that renames a symbol dangles a committed arch-doc anchor and nothing catches it. Phase 2 completes the *same* invariant on the code surface. Decisions:

- **Scope = the task's staged code change-set, NOT a full-store sweep.** Re-resolve every committed `code-anchor` whose target *file* is in `git diff --cached --name-only`. This is the **more robust** choice, not the cheap one (engaging Maurice's "robust over cheap"): a full-store sweep would block task A on doc↔code drift A never caused (pre-existing/other-task drift), re-introducing the cross-task coupling the integrity/completeness split (2026-05-25, this file → line ~128) exists to forbid. *(Correction — see the 2026-06-22 remediation entry below: change-set scoping alone does NOT prevent false-attribution; the **newly-dangled comparison** does, and it had to be built. The first cut's "structurally cannot false-attribute" claim was wrong.)*
- **Change-set scoping covers the right set, guarded by path-locality.** doc-code resolution is **path-local** (`p#s` is a pure function of `p`'s bytes, at finalize the materialized git index — `validation.md` → M30), guarded by a `path_locality_*` property test that fails loud if a future non-local resolver breaks it. *(Correction: the first cut said "provably complete"; that overclaimed — see the remediation entry for the path-normalization, symlink, and pre-existing-drift gaps a cross-model review surfaced.)*
- **Blocking, in jigc-core `finalize` (not the adapter).** Integrity the task caused and can fix (revert the code, or update the doc) → blocks, same class as a dangling forward-ref. Core finalize holds for any adapter. The M19 warn-only `pre-commit` hook **stays advisory** — it covers the *out-of-loop* total-git-bypass path (no task to attribute/block); making it blocking would penalize every direct commit and is a separate, heavier UX call, not bundled here.
- **The block names the doc + anchor + symbol, carrying both routes** (update the committed doc's anchor — absorbed via reconciliation — *or* revert the code), reusing the route-bearing `Finding` envelope. Robust/actionable for the weaker model, no new machinery.

Store-scope `jigc validate` is unchanged (the un-attributed health check). VISION's determinism table is untouched; `validation.md` → Scope = effective state gains the code-anchor blast-radius. Build next: dev-workflow, test-first (RED = a quick-fix rename dangling a committed anchor blocks at finalize).

## 2026-06-22 — Phase 2 (built): the universal finalize floor lands; the quick-fix hole is closed in core, end-to-end

Built test-first (`af26db1`). `engine::validate::validate_task` gains a `changed_code: &BTreeSet<String>` param (the CLI's `git diff --cached --no-renames --name-only`); `schedule_doc_code` drags every committed `code-anchor` whose target file is in the change-set into the doc-code surface (deduped by address) and re-resolves it against the materialized index. `anchor_file` is the documented path-locality chokepoint, guarded by `path_locality_*`. The probe's `dangling` findings now carry the repair route. **E2e-verified through the rebuilt binary** (the Phase-0 repro, re-run): the quick-fix rename that committed *clean* in Phase 0 now **blocks at finalize** (exit 3, no commit) with the actionable route, and the **fix path is real** — updating the committed arch-doc's anchor is *absorbed* by reconciliation and re-finalize passes. Not a dead-end; the floor blocks *productively*. RED confirmed by stubbing the blast loop (only the baseline-adopt advisory remained). 514 engine + full cli + 78 probe tests green; fmt + clippy clean. **Phase 2 (design + build) complete** — the safety axis is now *enforced* at the commit boundary under every workflow, not selected.

## 2026-06-22 — Phase 3 (built): the behavioral workflow-eval harness — jigc's missing "does an agent *use* it correctly" test

Generalized the pilot's one-off container rig into a reusable, per-workflow, agent-in-the-loop eval at `completions/workflow-eval/`. The standing gap it closes: the whole `cargo test` suite proves the CLI *composes* a workflow correctly (deterministic golden output) but never that a real agent **selects / engages / completes** it — the pilot was the first such test and failed all three. The harness: `run-eval.sh` (one isolated run, generalized from `run-rep.sh`, capturing **stream-json** — the tool-call trace the behavioral signals need, which the pilot's `--output-format json` lacked), `analyze.py` (one transcript → the engage/select/complete record + outcome, with the **Phase-2 floor's `jigc validate` as the outcome oracle**), `eval.py` (N runs → engage-rate / select-rate / complete-rate / outcome distribution + markdown), and `selftest.sh` (verifies the analysis layer over committed synthetic fixtures — **zero API spend**, CI-safe). **Verifiable proof now:** `selftest.sh` passes (engage 67% / select-on-expected 50% / complete 33% over the three fixtures) and `analyze.py` runs correctly over the pilot's *real* result-only transcripts (extracting turns/cost/outcome, honestly reporting behavioral=null without a tool stream). **Honest boundary:** the stream-json parser is pinned against synthetic fixtures matching the documented event schema (defensive — scans every `tool_use`, tolerates `message`/top-level content, word-bounds `jigc`); the first *live* run must spot-check one transcript, the one thing fixtures can't certify. This is the substrate for the long-horizon many-edit study. **Phase 3 complete** — all three handover phases (0 demonstrate · 1 hygiene · 2 floor · 3 harness) landed.

## 2026-06-22 — Floor remediation: a cross-model (Codex) review caught that the Phase-2 floor *overclaimed*; fixed the gaps, corrected the docs

Before pushing, routed the floor diff through Codex (`/review-codex`) as an independent adversarial check. It found the design's "**provably complete**" / "**structurally cannot false-attribute**" claims were not borne out by the implementation. Real findings, all fixed (test-first), per Maurice's "robust over cheap":

- **P1 false-attribution (the central claim was wrong).** Change-set scoping blocked on *any* committed anchor dangling in a changed file — it never compared base-vs-now. So a task touching a file that already carried *pre-existing* drift (broken at `HEAD`) was wedged on drift it didn't cause. **Fix:** the **newly-dangled comparison** — the CLI materializes the changed files' `HEAD` versions (`materialize_head_subset` → `base_code_tree_root`), the engine re-resolves the blast set against base too, and blocks only on `resolved-at-base ∧ dangles-at-index`. Task-surface anchors are unaffected (always the task's own). New test: pre-existing drift in a touched file stays clean; genuinely-new drift blocks (RED-confirmed by stubbing the base filter).
- **P1 false-negative (non-canonical paths).** `./src/foo.rs` didn't match git's `src/foo.rs`, silently escaping the floor. **Fix:** `lexical_normalize` both sides before the membership test; test with a `./`-prefixed committed anchor.
- **P2 symlink breaks path-locality.** A tracked symlink anchor file resolves through its target's bytes, which change-set scoping can't see. **Fix:** the `doc-code` probe emits a `doc-code.symlink-anchor` **advisory** instead of silently following it; probe test added.
- **P2 multi-valued committed guard.** The blast path dropped `enumerate_committed_surface`'s list-valued guard. **Fix:** made the drop a **documented, reasoned scope decision** — list-valued committed anchors are store-scope (`jigc validate`), and no shipped doctype declares one, so there is no per-task trigger (per-task list-element parsing is deliberately not built — no handling for a scenario that can't happen).
- **P2 doc overclaim + P3 perf.** Corrected `validation.md` (Scope = effective state) and the stale `target_surface.rs` module doc ("never on pre-existing drift in unrelated committed docs" — now false); documented the O(committed docs) walk as an accepted cost with the persisted-anchor-index optimization named but **not built** (premature for current store sizes).
- Codex **confirmed no defect** in `anchor_file`-vs-`split_anchor` agreement and the dedup-by-address merge (matching the in-house analysis).

Lesson banked: cross-model review before push earned its keep — it caught a load-bearing overclaim my own tests didn't. 516 engine + full cli + 79 probe tests green; fmt + clippy clean; the Phase-0 e2e repro still blocks productively.

## 2026-06-22 — Floor remediation round 2: a second Codex pass confirmed the fixes closed the prior findings and caught three new ones (all fixed)

Re-ran Codex over the remediation diff before pushing. It confirmed **all four prior findings CLOSED**, and found **three new defects the first remediation introduced** — all now fixed test-first:

- **P2a — base-probe failures were swallowed.** The newly-dangled base comparison consumed the base probe's findings only to build the suppression set, discarding its `pack-probe-integrity.*` meta-findings — so a base probe that *crashed/timed-out* (the comparison never actually ran) passed silently. **Fix:** surface the base probe's integrity findings into the report, so a broken base comparison blocks loudly (the same contract the index probe holds).
- **P2b — "resolved at base" was coded as "not *blocking* at base".** An *uncheckable* base advisory (a symlink-anchor / unsupported-language) wrongly counted as resolved, so an index dangle on such an anchor was attributed to the task. **Fix:** an anchor counts as resolved-at-base only if the base probe returned **no finding at all** for it; any base finding (dangle OR advisory) means we cannot claim it resolved, so its index dangle is not attributed (the store sweep still surfaces it). RED-confirmed.
- **P3 — `git_staged_paths` corrupted paths with leading/trailing spaces or newlines** (`--name-only` + `lines()` + `trim()`). **Fix:** `git diff --cached --name-only -z` (NUL-separated, no trim) so any valid path survives verbatim. (Also fixed an orphaned doc comment the first cut left on `git_diff`.)

Codex re-confirmed no defect in `anchor_file`/`split_anchor`, dedup, the symlink ordering, and the multi-valued store-scope decision. 517 engine + full cli + 79 probe tests green; fmt + clippy clean; e2e regression holds (genuine rename blocks, unrelated edit on a pre-drifted file commits). Two review rounds; the floor is now independently checked clean.

## 2026-06-23 — Long-horizon many-edit study: the founding empirical claim, finally tested (qualified yes for the weak model; self-refuting for the strong one)

Ran the study the pilot + three ties (M17–M19) named as jigc's best remaining shot at *empirical* superiority over a static `CLAUDE.md` — in the regime they all excluded: **8 sequential edits, fresh cold agent each, evolving twin, salience-independent enforcement (a *blocking* pre-commit hook) vs salience-dependent instruction (a dilution ladder).** 5 arms × Sonnet (R=3) + 2 arms × Opus (R=2) × 8 edits = 19 sequences / 152 cold-agent runs; objective `doc-code`-probe oracle + **blind cross-model judge (Codex** — the one the pilot couldn't run, quota-blocked). Pre-registered before any run; build-time amendments recorded. Full record: [completions/artifacts/long-horizon-study/](completions/artifacts/long-horizon-study/) (VERDICT → results → pre-registration).

- **Sonnet — the first controlled, blind-confirmed jigc-beats-static win in the project's history.** A-Sonnet held drift **flat at 0** (anchors *and* prose, judge 3/3 clean) across all 8 edits; plain compounded to **5.0** dangling; every static arm shipped **residual** drift. Two diagnosed mechanisms: (1) **salience-independent enforcement** — the hook fired on `git commit` and drove repair even on edits where the agent ran **zero jigc commands** (edited directly, got blocked, fixed); (2) **the move blind spot of name-based instruction** — every static arm left the *file-move* anchor (edit 3) pointing at a dead path because the symbol *name* was unchanged, so "grep the old name" (and a human, and the symbol-checking judge) saw nothing wrong: **6/9 Sonnet static reps shipped it; jigc 0/3.** "Validate against reality" beating "remember to check" — the integration advantage, measured.
- **Opus — the same study refutes the claim.** jigc's hook governs anchors, not prose; Opus surgically cleared the gate (anchors 0) and committed **stale titles** → prose drift to 3.0 mean / 5 worst, **judge 0/2** — *worse than a plain instruction*. Static-Opus stayed clean (0/0, judge 2/2) by following the broad written rule ("update every reference, including headings"), at **1/3 the cost** ($8.71 vs jigc-Opus $27.64). The M18/pilot prose blind spot, previously a footnote, is **outcome-determining** for a capable model.
- **Net + the fix it points at.** The value gate is **partially cleared** — jigc's mechanism is proven valuable and *located* (weaker model × long horizon × move/path-drift), not unconditional. The single highest-value next increment the data surfaces: **let the arch-doc anchor its component titles** (or add a prose-mention check) — jigc's anchors were already perfect; the only Opus leak was the unenforced title, squarely inside the existing `doc-code` mechanism. Then re-test Opus. Corpus-commitment recommendation unchanged (M33/M34 gate it); the *reason* shifts from "value unproven" to "value proven-in-regime; close the prose gap."
- **Method notes banked.** The reusable **evolving-twin sequence harness** (`run-sequence.sh` + `measure.py` + `eval-sequence.py`) is the handover's named deliverable, built and self-tested. The **blocking hook is a 1-line delta** from the shipped warn-only `precommit_hook_body` (`exit 1` on a `doc-code` finding) — no jigc-core change, floor design not reopened. An OAuth-token expiry truncated the first Opus pass (HTTP 401 mid-run); the 15 Sonnet sequences finished before it (0×401, headline intact), the 3 affected Opus sequences were cleanly re-run after `/login` (0×401, 0 dead edits), truncated originals preserved.

## 2026-06-23 — Title-anchoring fix: closed the Opus prose blind spot the long-horizon study found, and re-tested (stale 3.0 → 0.5)

The long-horizon study's one anti-jigc result was Opus: the `doc-code` floor governs anchors, not prose, so the capable model fixed the `implemented-by` anchor to clear `symbol-exists` and committed with the component **heading** still naming the renamed symbol — ending dirtier than a plain static instruction. Implemented the verdict's named fix and re-tested. Code: commit `9d99924`; result: [completions/artifacts/long-horizon-study/title-fix-retest.md](completions/artifacts/long-horizon-study/title-fix-retest.md).

- **The fix (`title-names-symbol`, pack-declared opt-in).** A `code-anchor` field can carry `title-names-symbol: true`; arch-doc's `implemented-by` does. The engine then blocks when the sibling repeatable-item title carries a **compound code-identifier** (camelCase hump *or* acronym-then-word — `CommentBlockParser`, `UIDoc`, `HTTPServer`) that is **not** the anchored symbol — a stale symbol name left in the heading. Pure string check in target-surface enumeration, emitted as a `doc-code.title-names-symbol` finding so `jigc validate` + the finalize floor + the pre-commit hook all enforce it **with no hook change**. Engine stays generic: spec criteria (prose titles) don't opt in. Camel/acronym discriminator keeps **descriptive** titles legal ("Session store", "Cache Layer" never flag).
- **Overrode a recorded decision with cause.** The arch-doc schema's "component titles are free text, not matched" note (DECISIONS 2026-06-07) predated the evidence that unmatched titles cause outcome-determining drift; updated the schema comment. The record is rebuttable — engaged the rationale (flexibility / parser-bug avoidance), preserved the slug's free-text id, added only the symbol-naming validation.
- **Re-test (Opus arm-A, valid run).** Stale prose **3.0 → 0.5** mean (rep2 clean all 8 edits; the title check blocked every edit and drove heading repair). The lone residual (`UIDoc` at edit 8) exposed a heuristic gap — the first cut keyed only on the camelCase hump, which acronym-prefixed `UIDoc` lacks — **closed in the same commit** (acronym-then-word shape) and verified by unit test + e2e (the `UIDoc` stale-title now blocks). So the current binary scores that residual clean too, proven by test rather than a further paid run.
- **Honest bounds.** The measured 0.5 ran on the v1 (camel-hump-only) binary; a clean confirmatory run on the corrected binary to *measure* ~0.0 is **owed but auth-blocked** (the OAuth token expired mid-run on the confirmatory attempt — HTTP 401 from edit 2 on; that run discarded). The blind judge was not used for the post-fix number this round: it mis-flagged each component's stable lowercase `{#slug}` (an opaque ID that correctly never renames) as a stale symbol — a judge instrument error, so the objective oracle is canonical per the pre-registration's "objective first." Gate: test-first RED→GREEN, 519 engine + full cli + probe green, fmt + clippy clean.
- **What it changes.** Removes the specific reason jigc lost to a static instruction for the capable model: the enforced surface now covers the heading Opus was leaving stale. Broader reading unchanged — jigc's value is salience-independent enforcement of a *checkable* surface; extend the checkable surface and the win extends with it.

Recorded so it isn't re-litigated. ## 2026-06-23 — Cost of enforcement flagged as a real concern (the block→recovery tax)

The long-horizon study's cost data ([completions/artifacts/long-horizon-study/results.md](completions/artifacts/long-horizon-study/results.md) → Cost) showed jigc ≈ static on Sonnet ($4.52/seq) but **3–6× static on Opus** ($27.64 → ≈$50.7/seq after the title fix added more checks). Root cause = the **block → re-orient → recover** loop; a capable model makes it expensive by re-investigating jigc every blocked edit (Opus thrashed exploring verbs; 8/8 edits blocked, nothing front-loaded). User flagged it (2026-06-23) as owed work. Strategy + concrete levers shaped in [ideas/cost-of-enforcement.md](ideas/cost-of-enforcement.md) (prescriptive "mechanical fix, don't investigate" block messages · deterministic title↔symbol `--fix` · sharper front-loading bootstrap nudge · block-cycle instrumentation). Decouple the salience-independent *guarantee* from the *cost*: common case proactively-correct + silent validate, block as rarely-firing backstop. Indexed in VISION → Open questions; unscheduled.

## 2026-06-23 — Store-wide `ref-resolves` — the 4th store-sweep family (cross-doc forward-ref integrity)

`validate_store_families` gained a **4th content family**: cross-doc forward-ref integrity, the **store-wide analog of the task-scope `ref-resolves` finalize gate**. Discovery that motivated it: `schema-conformance.ref-resolves` fired *only* at `finalize`, scoped to task-touched edges (`crate::index::ref_resolves`); the store sweep ran doc↔code, workflow↔refs, and file↔CLI-state but **not** ref-resolves — so a dangling `supersedes`/`cites` *already committed* in the store was **invisible to `jigc validate`**, hence to any backstop keyed on its findings. **Why now:** the next study (the "harder claim" — does jigc beat a static `CLAUDE.md` on cross-doc ref integrity, a non-instruction-replicable surface?) enforces via the salience-independent pre-commit hook, which keys on `jigc validate` findings; the differentiator was **not hook-reachable** until this gap closed. **Build:** factored `committed_reachable` out of `index::target_reachable`'s surface-a (shared reachability rule, no fork), added `index::ref_resolves_store` (walks every committed edge in the rebuilt committed index — no surface-b/working-area, no `task_froms` filter, the store being closed), wired it as Family 4 over a `rebuild_committed` (pure in-memory builder, inert stamp). **Severity:** reuses the existing intrinsic-blocking `schema-conformance.ref-resolves` check id — **no new check id / knob / inventory growth** (the M20 pattern: same id, store/read-only scope). Blocking is a finalize verdict; under the read-only store sweep the finding is *listed*, never a gate (exits 0) — consistent with the M18/M20 read-command exit rule. **Not the M20 "deliberately-not-a-fourth-target" exclusion** (that was override↔default, which has *no committed doc to walk*; ref-resolves walks the committed edge index — a real store surface). jigc's shipped warn-only hook is **unchanged** (stays `doc-code.*`-keyed); a study harness keying a blocking hook on `schema-conformance.ref-resolves` is study config, not a jigc behavior change. Test-first: RED `validate_store_surfaces_dangling_cross_doc_supersedes` + clean-path guard. Design: [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Store-wide forward-ref integrity — the fourth family.

## 2026-06-23 — Do NOT fix the cost-of-enforcement tax before the cross-doc study (harness frozen)

User asked whether to address the Opus ceremony tax (3–6× plain, the block→recovery loop) before running the "harder claim" cross-doc study. **Decided: no.** Three reasons: (1) **wrong axis** — the study measures a correctness/capability claim (cross-doc ref-dangle catches), not cost; a high tax doesn't invalidate a drift win. (2) **Fixing it can only help jigc** — every cost lever (prescriptive block messages, `--fix`, front-loading nudge) reduces thrash and would flatter jigc's numbers, so running the **un-optimized** jigc is the *conservative* test: a win despite the full tax is robust. (3) **It would confound** — the two biggest levers are *prose the agent reads* (block-message wording, bootstrap nudge), so changing them mid-program means the cross-doc study runs on a behaviorally different jigc than the doc↔code study; the pre-registration wants the harness held fixed. Cost-of-enforcement stays its own future experiment with cost as the *dependent* variable. Operational mitigation only: **Opus extremes as last study** (Sonnet R=3 primary carries the verdict + Opus R=2 on extremes, in small post-re-login batches to bound the OAuth-expiry-on-slow-runs risk). Reflected in the Step-2 pre-registration honesty bounds.

## 2026-06-24 — The "harder claim" cross-doc study: REFUTED (cross-doc ref integrity is instruction-replicable for capable models)

Ran the pre-registered cross-document forward-ref integrity study (the differentiator a static `CLAUDE.md` *structurally cannot replicate* per the §2 premise — store-wide `supersedes`/`cites` integrity, enforced by the blocking hook now that the [4th store-sweep family](design/validation.md) makes it hook-reachable). **19 valid sequences** (Sonnet 5 arms ×3 + Opus A·C550 ×2), evolving synthetic ADR-graph twins, two-path edge oracle (store-walk + `jigc validate` cross-check, agreed every sequence), 0 control violations / 0 oracle disagreements / 0 auth failures (one transient 401 discarded + re-run per protocol). **Result: the harder claim is refuted on BOTH models.** Plain drifts to **4** dangling cross-doc refs (the problem is real); but every static-rule arm AND the jigc arm held **flat at 0** across all 8 edits at *every* dilution level (incl. C550 = 452 lines, rule at ~75% depth) — and jigc's hook merely **ties** the static rule, at **2.9–3× the cost** ($3.63 Sonnet / $7.66 Opus per seq vs $1.22–2.67 static). This is the pre-registered hypothesis-refuting branch, reported straight. **Why** (the real lesson): doc↔code drift is a *separate-artifact* problem (the doc is an easy-to-forget side errand → enforcement wins, as the long-horizon study showed); cross-doc ref integrity is a *same-intent* problem ("I renamed it" and "I fix what points at it" are one motion → a capable agent does it once told). So jigc's edge is **not "enforces more things"** — it is enforcing what *instruction-salience reliably misses*; here salience doesn't miss, so the guarantee is **redundant, not wrong**. Honest standing after both studies: jigc-vs-static is **proven superior on non-locally-salient surfaces (doc↔code, weak model), tied on locally-salient ones (cross-doc refs, capable models), always more expensive** — value gate **not** decisively cleared. Sharpest next tests the data points at: a *genuinely non-local* ref break (triggering edit doesn't name the slug that dangles) + a weaker model (Haiku). VISION proven-section updated. Artifacts: [completions/artifacts/cross-doc-refint-study/](completions/artifacts/cross-doc-refint-study/) (VERDICT.md · results.md · pre-registration.md · harness).

## 2026-06-24 — CLI-owned rename scheduled as M35 (direction-decided): own the rename, don't freeze it

The cross-doc study's refutation (above) exposed that jigc was enforcing the wrong verb — *detection* of a dangling ref (which a static `grep` rule ties) instead of *ownership* of the rename. **Decided (user, direction-locked):** make `jigc doc rename` a deterministic, transaction-bound CLI operation that rewrites every structured managed referrer atomically (incl. non-greppable ones), making slugs **mutable + legible** instead of frozen. **Honest scope (Codex cross-review, gpt-5.5):** a static project can *script* the effect (`git mv` + `sd`/grep, an ADR linter); the differentiator is shipping it as the **canonical, transaction-bound managed-doc interface** + the cost inversion — *not* "static structurally cannot." **Why it's a real win where detection wasn't:** it *inverts the cost story* (one command vs. N turns of manual ref-chasing → jigc cheaper than plain, turning the enforcement tax into a labor saving) and wins on the genuinely non-greppable referrers the agent can't search for. **Invariant amendment — a genuine identity-model revision, not a mechanism swap** (Codex sharpened this: storage says "identity *is* the path," so a rename *does* change identity): stability stays under **reorder + retitle-without-reslug**; an identity change is allowed only through the **atomic CLI operation** (never an untracked move — `reconciliation.rename` backstops that); diff-legibility *improves*; opaque-ID-indirection (`adr:7f3a`) rejected. Determinism boundary holds: CLI rewrites structured ref *fields* in the managed store; prose + unmanaged-file mentions are *reported, never rewritten*. Acceptance = a **cost+completeness study** (reuse the cross-doc harness) — the first designed for jigc to **beat plain on effort**; confounds pre-registered (verb-engagement ≠ availability · static-arm shell one-liner baseline · rename-error recovery · small-N noise). Mechanism opens (rename-vs-retitle · collision-on-`--to` · OOB-rename precedence `reconciliation.rename` > `ref-resolves` · fan-out forbid · git-history continuity · prose/unmanaged reporting · rollback inventory · migration) deferred to M35 planning ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)). Shaped + Codex-reviewed: [ideas/cli-owned-rename.md](ideas/cli-owned-rename.md); charter: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M35; indexed VISION → Open questions.

## 2026-06-24 — M33 + M34 planned as a paired unit (schema freeze + corpus migration); the charter's "reuse the detect-half" premise refuted by the baseline audit

Planned M33 (schema/format freeze) and M34 (managed-corpus migration) together — they are coupled (M34's transform migrates onto the v1 shape M33 declares; M33's freeze is only *enforceable* once M34's stamp + detector exist). **The baseline capability audit overturned the charter's cost basis** (4 `capability-auditor`s + 4 `gap-detector`s, exercised on the real binary at `3d0190e`): the M34 charter's load-bearing premise *"reconciliation already provides the detect half"* is **false** — store-scope `jigc validate` runs four families (doc↔code, workflow↔refs, file↔CLI-state **hash-only**, ref-resolves) and **none re-parses a committed doc against its schema**; a doc made non-conformant by a *schema* change with **bytes unchanged** passes `validate` clean (exit 0, verified). So the pair is **substantial net-new machinery**, not a cheap reuse: a store-scope schema-conformance detector, a per-doc version stamp, a schema-diff, and a deterministic transform producer are all net-new. Settled forks (human-gated):

- **Build the full pair now** — the productive-go value gate is **proven-in-regime, not unproven**: the long-horizon many-edit study (2026-06-23, blind cross-model judge — [completions/artifacts/long-horizon-study/VERDICT.md](completions/artifacts/long-horizon-study/VERDICT.md)) is the project's first controlled jigc-**beats**-static result (Sonnet × long-horizon × the move/path-drift class: drift held flat at 0 while every static `CLAUDE.md` shipped residual it structurally cannot catch), and the one regime it lost (Opus prose blind-spot) was **fixed + re-tested** (the `title-names-symbol` check). The study's own verdict names **M33/M34 as the productive-go gate** to build next. (An earlier read of this milestone leaned on the 2026-06-21 readiness-assessment's stale "value unproven, leaning-negative" framing — corrected here against the study that ran two days later.)
- **The transform is robust CLI-owned, not LLM-routed.** Structural changes (add-optional-field, widen-cardinality, fixed-slot→repeatable-with-default) are computed from a schema-diff and applied as byte-stable splices over the proven `write.rs` primitives; only *prose-needing* changes route to the agent (Framing A — the determinism boundary holds). Reusing `jigc migrate`'s LLM re-author path for structural transforms was **rejected**: lossy, non-deterministic, and a determinism-boundary breach (`migrate` adopts *foreign*→*fresh* docs; it never re-opens a managed committed doc).
- **The per-doc schema-version stamp is declared *in each doctype's schema*, engine-valued** (engine-injected uniformly, value supplied by a new "current active schema version" deriver — the `status`/`date` model: in-schema field, engine-set value), **not** an out-of-schema engine/manifest field. Reason (review Finding 1): the transform is driven by a **schema-diff over two `Schema` values**, so an *out-of-schema* stamp would produce no `added-field` classification and the schema-diff classifier (the riskiest net-new code) would get only synthetic coverage. In-schema makes adding the stamp a genuine add-field migration the transform proves on. (For `spec`/`prd`/`changelog`, which render zero front-matter today, this introduces a `---` block — a real v0→v1 shape change.)
- **The v0→v1 corpus stamp-migration is a real dogfood of M34's add-field transform** — because the stamp is in-schema, stamping the corpus is a genuine `added-field` schema-diff the transform classifies and applies (build-order: the transform exists before the stamp lands).
- **Build all 5 deferred schema-engine opens into v1 — the freeze is a one-way door.** Deferring a shape-bearing open past the freeze does not *save* work; it *guarantees* a future breaking migration. So a *complete, correct* v1 is the robust cut: the **prd→spec edge** (the one genuine schema-shape change — see the correction below); **inverse/min-cardinality** ("a PRD must have ≥1 spec"); **repeatable-item managed-ref edges**; **in-prose mentions**; **schema-fragment `include`**. (This reverses an earlier triage that deferred all 5 — that was the cheap path past the freeze; the freeze's one-way-door cost is the discriminator.)
- **Correction (2026-06-24, caught at M33 Inc-2 build-plan) — the prd→spec edge is stored *spec-side*, not PRD-side.** Settle initially modeled it as a new `prd` header section carrying a `decomposes-into → spec` forward ref. The build-planner halted: that **contradicts the M9-settled model** (`project-setup.md:65` — "the *spec-side* `derived-from` relation, inverse derived never stored") and `document-type-schema.md:90-91`'s sole worked ref declaration (`spec.derived-from → prd, inverse: has-specs, inverse-card: "1..*"`), and is **unsatisfiable** for the "PRD ≥1 spec" check (the registered `schema-completeness.inverse-cardinality` constrains the *target* side, so the forward ref must point spec→prd; a PRD-side forward `1..*` would deadlock PRD-first finalize, violating the "completeness is never a per-task gate" invariant — the one clarified above). **Resolved spec-side:** `spec.derived-from → prd` (forward `card` `0..1`, pinned at task decomposition so a PRD-less spec is valid; `inverse: has-specs, inverse-card: "1..*"` carries the PRD-completeness obligation, store-scope advisory). The PRD file is unchanged; `spec` gains the ref field (introducing its header block — the real add-field the transform proves on). My Settle miss: I did not spike this open against the locked `project-setup.md`/`document-type-schema.md` (the "a locked doc you build around is a claim" discipline, applied to the detect-half but not here). Ripple: **repeatable-item refs** is no longer prd→spec's substrate (that edge is doc-level) — kept in v1 as a byte-neutral general edge-extractor completion. Docs corrected: corpus-migration.md, roadmap M33 Inc-2 + M34 Inc-2, doctype-map.md.
- **Byte-fuzz extension to `prd`/`spec`/`changelog`/`arch-doc` is a freeze *prerequisite*** (only `commit`/`adr` are arbitrary-instance fuzzed today). You cannot declare a doctype byte-frozen v1 without arbitrary-instance round-trip proof, and the fuzz must run *before* the stamp mutates those doctypes. `changelog` (two-level nesting, multi-word section id, optional field) is the highest-risk un-fuzzed shape.
- **The freeze is enforced, not asserted** — a versioned, hashed **doctype-set manifest** + a self-enforcement check (a schema-shape change without a bumped version + an M34 migration is blocked), not prose discipline alone.

Corrections landed in the same motion: the M34 charter's false "reuse the detect-half" + the conflation of M34 with the *self-host* "v1 in-place migration" deferral (the self-hosting adoption migration, post-spine, gated behind M17 — distinct machinery, kept independently keyed); the stale `document-type-schema.md` "keys are placeholders pending implementation" claim (the schema-definition format is **shipped + golden-locked** — that line is the literal artifact M33 freezes). The `jigc` *name* deferral stays keyed to productive-go, **not** pulled into this pair. Design: new part-doc [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md); elaborations to [validation.md](design/validation.md) (5th store-scope family), [storage.md](design/storage.md) + [document-type-schema.md](design/document-type-schema.md) (the stamp field), [doctype-map.md](implementation/doctype-map.md) (the frozen v1 set). Decomposition: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M33/M34.

## 2026-06-24 — M33 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut the byte-stability fuzz floor (extend `arb_doc()` / `mod roundtrip` in `crates/engine/src/write.rs` from `commit`/`adr` to the four un-fuzzed persisted doctypes) into **four ordered single-concern tasks, one per doctype**. *Why one-per-doctype:* each is the **#1-risk round-trip property proven for a distinct render surface** with its **own potential remediation** — separable (different code paths), so each remediation isolates to its own gate-green commit (the freeze audit reads them per-doctype). Ordered **ascending structural complexity** so a bug in the shared *populated-repeatable-item* path surfaces in the simplest carrier first. Each task's RED step is the new generator arm itself (the roadmap's "red obligation: arbitrary-instance round-trip byte-identity, proven before green"); both existing property clauses run over every new arm automatically via `arb_doc()`'s `prop_oneof!`. Done-criterion throughout: `cargo test -p engine roundtrip` green over the new arm + full dev-workflow gate (`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`). Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M33 Increment 1.

- **T1 — `prd` fuzz arm.** Add a `prd` generator to `arb_doc()` (`vision` slot + a populated `requirements` repeatable `[title + statement slot]` + `context` slot; **no front-matter** → `edit: None`, surgical clause self-skips the established way). *Done:* `cargo test -p engine roundtrip` passes with the `prd` arm present; any byte-instability surfaced (the M26 empty-slot/field-group class is prior art) is remediated; full gate green. First fuzz of the **populated repeatable-item render path** (`### <title>  {#id}` + per-item slot) — shared substrate T2–T4 also ride.
- **T2 — `spec` fuzz arm.** Add a `spec` generator (`goal`/`context` slots + populated `criteria` repeatable `[title + statement slot + a `maps-to-test` code-anchor field]`). *Done:* roundtrip green with the `spec` arm; remediation gate-green. Extends T1 with an **item-level code-anchor field** inside a repeatable item (verify it renders/round-trips byte-stable).
- **T3 — `arch-doc` fuzz arm.** Add an `arch-doc` generator (`meta` `header: true` carrying the `cites` ref-list `card: 0..*` + `overview` slot + populated `components` repeatable `[title + description slot + `implemented-by` code-anchor]`). *Done:* roundtrip green with the `arch-doc` arm; remediation gate-green. First fuzz of a **header section with a list-shaped front-matter field** — exercise both empty- and populated-`cites`; `edit: None` (ref-list is no scalar `set_field` target — do **not** extend `set_field`; item/list mutation is M34).
- **T4 — `changelog` fuzz arm (the riskiest shape).** Add a `changelog` generator: **two-level `releases` nesting** (`### <ver>  {#id}` → nested `#### <category>  {#id}` change-groups), the **multi-word `## Unreleased Changes`** section id, and the **optional `link`** field exercised both present and absent. *Done:* roundtrip green with the `changelog` arm covering {link-present, link-absent, ≥1 nested release with ≥1 change-group}; any instability remediated; full gate green. After T4, all six persisted doctypes are arbitrary-instance fuzzed — the increment deliverable.

### 2026-06-24 — M33 inc-1 T4 landed: `changelog` fuzz arm (all six doctypes now fuzzed); no instability found

The `changelog` arm renders through `render()` so its bytes are canonical by construction; both round-trip clauses pass at 4000 cases. Two elaborations the generator pins (no remediation needed — the byte-form was already stable): (a) **change-group `notes` prose uses a `#####`/H5 deeper-heading fragment, never `####`/H4** — a nested change-group renders at `####`, so a `####` heading inside its slot collides with a *sibling* change-group heading and fails the conformance gate (`item-anchor-missing`, verified empirically); H5 is deeper than both the unreleased (`###`) and nested (`####`) depths, so it stays prose at either. (b) The **empty `unreleased-changes` section** (the post-cut KaC state) is generated (`change_groups(0..=6)`) and round-trips byte-stable: a middle empty repeatable renders `## Unreleased Changes\n\n` and `render(parse(x)) == x` holds (the trailing double-blank is the *stable* canonical form, idempotent under re-render — not an instability). Category distinctness drawn from a subsequence of the six-member enum (a repeatable rejects duplicate `{#id}` anchors). Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M33 Increment 1.

The `schema-completeness.inverse-cardinality` check id + its `advisory` knob exist (`result.rs:227`, `knobs.rs:316`) but **no code emits the finding** (verified — net-new in T2). The `doc_edges` repeatable branch is a literal `continue` today (`index.rs:493`) and **no shipped schema carries a repeatable-item ref**, so T3 is byte-neutral (verified). Done-criterion throughout: the named new test green + full dev-workflow gate (`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`). The `inverse: has-specs, inverse-card: "1..*"` keys ride on the field here (parsed, inert until T2). No engine extraction/exemption change (header-`Simple` ref auto-extracts; `0..1` auto-exempts) — the test proves it for the new shape.
- **T2 — store-scope `schema-completeness.inverse-cardinality` check (the PRD ≥1-spec completeness).** Add a fifth store family to `validate::validate_store_families` (`crates/engine/src/validate.rs`) that reads `spec.derived-from`'s `inverse-card: "1..*"` obligation, enumerates committed `prd` docs, counts each PRD's **inbound `derived-from`** edges over the committed edge index (reuse the Family-4 `committed_index`), and emits an **advisory** `schema-completeness.inverse-cardinality` finding (severity from the existing cascade knob, default `advisory`) for any PRD below the minimum. *Done:* a test — a committed PRD with zero inbound `derived-from` surfaces exactly one advisory `schema-completeness.inverse-cardinality` finding at store scope; a PRD with ≥1 inbound surfaces none; `validate_task` (per-task finalize) **never** emits it — store/milestone-scope only, never a per-task gate (`document-type-schema.md:128`); full gate green. Depends on T1 (reads its declaration).
- **T3 — repeatable-item managed-ref edge-extractor branch (byte-neutral general completion).** Wire `index::doc_edges` (`crates/engine/src/index.rs`) to recurse `SectionBody::Repeatable` item bodies, emitting one forward edge per **ref-typed** `Leaf::Field` in a repeatable item (today the repeatable arm is a bare `continue` — silently inert; no shipped schema carries a repeatable-item ref, so production edge sets are unchanged). *Done:* a unit test over a synthetic schema whose repeatable section carries a `ref` leaf asserts the repeatable-item ref **enters the edge index** (`doc_edges` emits it); the existing `arch_doc_cites_tests` invariant holds (repeatable `code-anchor` leaves — non-ref — still contribute **no** edges) so adr/arch-doc extraction goldens stay byte-identical; full gate green. Independent of T1/T2.

Landed T1. `spec.yaml` gained a `meta` header section carrying `{ id: derived-from, type: ref, to: prd, card: "0..1", inverse: has-specs, inverse-card: "1..*" }` (section id `meta`, mirroring `arch-doc` — a header section renders as `---` front matter, never a `##` heading, so it is exempt from the multi-word title-case reparse defect). New CLI integration test (`crates/cli/tests/prd_inverse_cardinality.rs`) drives the built binary: a committed PRD with zero inbound `derived-from` surfaces exactly one advisory finding at store scope (`jigc validate` exits 0); a PRD with a committed spec deriving from it surfaces none; a `jigc task finalize` over an unrelated task with the deficient PRD committed emits none (proving the per-task gate omits it).
